definition_zh: 使烦恼；使恼火；困扰（难题）
definition_en: to annoy someone or to cause them trouble, especially with something that keeps happening
core_image: 鞋里一颗小石子：不至于受伤，却每一步都硌得人心烦
scene: 邻居深夜的狗叫让整栋楼难以入睡。The dog next door vexed the whole building every night.
sceneCN: 这里 vex 是「使烦恼；惹恼」（第 1 个义项：反复发生的小事让人心烦）；句意：隔壁的狗每天晚上都搅得整栋楼不得安宁。

pos.zh: 使烦恼；使恼火；困扰

derivatives.zh: vex 加 -ation 构成的名词，表示「恼怒；烦心事」
拉丁语 vexare 加 -ous 构成，表示「令人烦恼的；（诉讼）无理纠缠的」
vexing 加 -ly 构成，表示「令人恼火地」

senses.title: To annoy by something repeated
senses.definition: to make someone feel annoyed with something that keeps coming back
senses.definitionCN: 用反复出现的事情让人感到烦恼
senses.example: Her constant questions vexed the teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她没完没了的问题让老师很恼火。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to shake or harry, so vexation is being shaken again and again.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为摇晃、反复骚扰，所以烦恼就是被一再摇晃。

senses.title: To cause trouble for someone
senses.definition: to create practical problems or burdens for a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 给个人或群体带来实际的麻烦或负担
senses.example: The missing records vexed the whole office.
senses.exampleCN: 档案丢失让整个办公室都陷入麻烦。
senses.why: A small persistent trouble grows into a real burden on work.
senses.whyCN: 持续的小麻烦逐渐累积，变成工作里的真实负担。

senses.title: To plague a person emotionally
senses.definition: to keep disturbing someone with worry or self doubt
senses.definitionCN: 让担忧或自我怀疑持续侵扰某人
senses.example: Doubts about the decision vexed her for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 对这个决定的疑虑困扰了她好几周。
senses.why: The shake moves from the body into the mind and keeps it restless.
senses.whyCN: 这种摇晃从身体移到心里，让思绪始终安静不下来。

senses.title: To set a hard problem
senses.definition: to keep troubling people as an unsolved question
senses.definitionCN: 作为未解的问题持续困扰人们
senses.example: This question has vexed scholars for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题困扰了学者数十年。
senses.why: A stubborn puzzle is personified as something that worries its solvers.
senses.whyCN: 顽固的谜题被拟人化，仿佛它主动去烦扰解题的人。

senses.title: A disputed issue
senses.definition: a matter that has long caused argument and disagreement
senses.definitionCN: 长期引起争论和分歧的事情
senses.example: Fees for museum entry remain a vexed issue.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆是否收费仍是一个争议议题。
senses.why: The participle vexed labels a topic that keeps disturbing debate.
senses.whyCN: 分词 vexed 用来标记一个不断搅动辩论的话题。

senses.title: To tease lightly
senses.definition: an older use meaning to tease or provoke playfully or roughly
senses.definitionCN: 较古老的用法，指玩笑或粗暴地逗弄、挑动
senses.example: The old poem says the boys vex the sleeping bear.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古诗说，男孩子们去逗弄熟睡的熊。
senses.why: The oldest sense was physical prodding, now kept mainly in older writing.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是身体上的拨弄，如今主要保留在较早的文本中。

senses.title: A minor setback
senses.definition: a small passing annoyance rather than a serious difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 短暂而轻微的烦扰，而非严重困难
senses.example: A delayed train was only a mild vex.
senses.exampleCN: 火车延误只是一个小麻烦。
senses.why: English speakers turn the verb into a countable noun for tiny troubles.
senses.whyCN: 英语使用者把动词变成可数名词，用来指微小的困扰。

senses.title: To trouble by thought
senses.definition: an old literary use meaning to discuss or turn over in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 较早的文学用法，指反复讨论或在心里琢磨
senses.example: The elders vexed the matter till dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 长者们把这件事商量到天亮。
senses.why: To keep shaking a question mentally is to keep turning it over.
senses.whyCN: 在心里反复摇晃一个问题，就是把它翻来覆去地琢磨。

intro.en: Vex comes from Latin vexare, to shake or harry, and was first borrowed through Old French into legal English.
intro.cn: vex 来自拉丁语 vexare（摇晃、反复侵扰），经古法语进入英语，最早多用于法律文书。

items.en: Vexare means to shake, toss, or harry.
items.cn: vexare 意为摇晃、抛掷或反复侵袭。

items.en: Some link it to vehere, to carry, but the origin is not certain.
items.cn: 有人把该词与 vehere（运送）联系起来，但来源不确定。

items.en: Vexer carries the meaning harass into French.
items.cn: vexer 把「侵扰」这一意义带入法语。

items.en: Vexen names legal annoyance in court records.
items.cn: 中古英语 vexen 在法律记录中指受人烦恼侵扰。

items.en: The word widens to mental and social annoyance.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到心理与社会层面的烦恼。

items.en: Vexed now also describes disputed questions.
items.cn: vexed 如今也用来描述有争议的难题。

note.en: Vex shares its shape with vexation and vexatious, and its meaning with annoy and irritate.
note.cn: vex 在形态上与 vexation、vexatious 同族，在语义上与 annoy、irritate 相邻。

entries.definition: the feeling of being annoyed
entries.definitionCN: 烦恼；恼火

entries.definition: troublesome or needlessly annoying
entries.definitionCN: 令人烦恼的；无理纠缠的

entries.definition: annoyed or much disputed
entries.definitionCN: 恼怒的；有争议的

entries.definition: to make someone slightly angry
entries.definitionCN: 惹恼；使生气

entries.definition: to make someone impatient
entries.definitionCN: 使烦躁

entries.definition: to keep pressing someone with unwanted actions
entries.definitionCN: 骚扰；不断侵扰

normalIntro.en: Vex is a small repeated shake: a nagging worry or a noisy neighbour keeps jolting the mind.
normalIntro.cn: vex 是反复的小摇晃：一件总也甩不掉的烦心事或吵闹的邻居，不断撞得人心神不宁。

normal.en: To be vexed by something is to be bothered by it.
normal.cn: be vexed by something 就是被某事困扰。

normal.en: A vexed issue is a problem that people argue about.
normal.cn: vexed issue 就是人们争执不休的问题。

normal.en: Vexation is the noun of annoyance.
normal.cn: vexation 是表示「烦恼」的名词。

normal.en: The Latin vexare means to shake or harry.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 vexare 意为摇晃、侵扰。

normal.en: Compare worry: vex is usually milder and about repeated small troubles.
normal.cn: 对比 worry：vex 通常更轻微，多指反复的小麻烦。

abstract.en: A grain of sand in a shoe that never quite leaves.
abstract.cn: 鞋里一粒小沙，怎么也倒不干净。

abstract.en: A phone that hums on the desk all afternoon.
abstract.cn: 一部手机在桌上嗡嗡响了一整个下午。

abstract.en: A hedgehog rolling into a sleeping dog again and again.
abstract.cn: 一只刺猬一次又一次地滚到睡着的狗身上。

examples.en: The noise vexed the neighbours night after night.
examples.cn: 噪音夜复一夜地惹恼着邻居们。

examples.en: She was vexed by the delay in the results.
examples.cn: 她因结果延迟而烦恼。

examples.en: The origin of the custom is a vexed question.
examples.cn: 这一习俗的起源是个有争议的问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「Wie克斯」——小石子（克斯）硌脚，越想越烦；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vexare（摇晃、反复侵扰，来源一般认为与「拉扯、来回折腾」有关，确凿词根尚无定论）→ 古法语 vexer → 英语 vex，核心义「反复搅扰」。

sensesIntro.en: Vex begins with repeated physical shaking, passes into everyday annoyance, then into mental worry, and finally becomes a label for stubborn disputed questions.
sensesIntro.cn: vex 从反复的身体摇晃出发，过渡到日常的烦扰，再深入内心的焦虑，最后成为顽固争议问题的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pebble in a shoe that is felt at every step.
core.cn: 核心意象：鞋里的一颗小石子，走一步硌一下。

branches.en: Repeated small annoyance is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 反复的小烦扰是日常义项。

branches.en: Practical trouble is the burden sense.
branches.cn: 实际问题是一种负担义项。

branches.en: Emotional plaguing is the inner sense.
branches.cn: 内心的煎熬是内在义项。

branches.en: An unsolved problem vexes the people who study it.
branches.cn: 未解的问题会困扰研究它的人。

branches.en: A vexed issue and a mild vex both name troubles with a label.
branches.cn: vexed issue 与轻微的 vex 都是用标签命名麻烦。

intro.en: Vex is a plain Latin verb in English, so nearly all of its word family is built with Latin or English endings.
intro.cn: vex 在英语中是一个不经拆分的拉丁语动词，因此它的词族几乎都靠拉丁语或英语词尾构建。

latinIntro.en: Latin vexare and its derivatives carry the idea of shaking and harrying into legal English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vexare 及其派生形式把「摇晃、侵扰」的意思带入法律英语。

items.example: Latin vexare carried the sense of shaking.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 vexare 含有摇晃之意。

items.example: The suffix forms vexed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 vexed。

items.example: The suffix forms vexes.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -es 构成 vexes。

items.example: The suffix forms vexing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 vexing。

items.example: The suffix forms vexation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 vexation。

items.example: The stem appears in vexatious.
items.exampleCN: 该词干出现在 vexatious 中。

items.example: The suffix forms vexatious.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成 vexatious。

items.example: The suffix forms vexingly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ingly 构成 vexingly。

items.example: The prefix forms unvexed.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unvexed。

definition_zh: 可行性；生存能力；存活率
definition_en: the quality of being able to work, survive, or continue successfully
core_image: 一株幼苗自己扎住了根，不用再靠别人浇水也能活下去
scene: 投资人先问项目能不能持续赚钱。The investors questioned the viability of the small farm project.
sceneCN: 这里 viability 是「可行性」（第 1 个义项：计划能否真正运作）；句意：投资人质疑这个小型农场项目的可行性。

pos.zh: 可行性；生存能力；存活率

derivatives.zh: 词根 vi- 加 -able 构成，表示「可行的；能存活的」
viable 加 -ly 构成，表示「可行地」
in- 加 viability 构成，表示「不可行性；不能存活」

senses.title: Workability of a plan
senses.definition: the ability of a plan or idea to work in practice
senses.definitionCN: 计划或想法在实践中行得通的能力
senses.example: The team tested the viability of the storage plan.
senses.exampleCN: 团队检验了这项储存方案的可行性。
senses.why: Something viable can live on its own, so a workable plan is one that survives contact with reality.
senses.whyCN: viable 指能独立存活，因此可行的计划就是能与现实接触后仍站得住的计划。

senses.title: Survival of a living thing
senses.titleCN: （生物、群体的）生存能力；存活率
senses.definition: the ability of an organism or group to keep living and reproduce
senses.definitionCN: 生物或群体继续存活并繁殖的能力
senses.example: Cooler water improved the viability of the young fish.
senses.exampleCN: 水温降低提高了幼鱼的存活率。
senses.why: The Latin root life is taken literally, so viability measures how well life holds.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根的「生命」在这里被照字面理解，所以 viability 衡量生命能维持多久。

senses.title: Commercial success
senses.definition: the ability of a business to earn enough to keep going
senses.definitionCN: 企业赚到足够收入以持续经营的能力
senses.example: Small farms question the commercial viability of the scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 小农场主质疑该方案的商业可行性。
senses.why: A firm that cannot pay its way is treated as a body that cannot live.
senses.whyCN: 付不起自己开支的企业，被视为无法存活的生命体。

senses.title: Of a fetus
senses.definition: in medicine, the stage when a fetus could survive outside the womb
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指胎儿能在子宫外存活的发展阶段
senses.example: Doctors explained fetal viability to the parents.
senses.exampleCN: 医生向父母解释了胎儿的存活能力。
senses.why: Medicine uses the word for the exact point where independent life becomes possible.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个词来指标记独立生命成为可能的那一点。

senses.title: Long term persistence
senses.definition: the ability of a community or system to last over many years
senses.definitionCN: 社区或系统持续存在多年的能力
senses.example: Water supply worries the viability of the village.
senses.exampleCN: 供水问题让村民担心村庄的长期存续。
senses.why: Anything that must last is judged by how well it keeps living.
senses.whyCN: 凡是要持续存在的东西，人们都用能否持续存活的尺度来评判。

senses.title: Of a seed or cell
senses.definition: the state of a seed, cell, or spore being alive and able to grow
senses.definitionCN: 种子、细胞或孢子活着并有能力生长的状态
senses.example: The test checked the viability of the stored seeds.
senses.exampleCN: 这项检测检查了贮藏种子的活力。
senses.why: Biology measures life as a property that a seed either has or lacks.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把生命当作种子或具备或不具备的属性来测量。

senses.title: Of a solution
senses.definition: the practical merit of a proposed answer among competing options
senses.definitionCN: 在多个选项中提出的解决方案的实际可行程度
senses.example: Engineers compared the viability of two designs.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师比较了两种设计的可行程度。
senses.why: A solution that cannot live long in practice loses the comparison.
senses.whyCN: 在实践中活不长的方案，自然会在比较中落败。

senses.title: Of a species
senses.definition: the chance that a species continues in a certain place
senses.definitionCN: 某物种在特定地区继续存续的可能性
senses.example: The report doubts the viability of the wild population.
senses.exampleCN: 报告对野生种群的存续可能性表示怀疑。
senses.why: Conservation uses the word to ask whether a population can keep living on its own.
senses.whyCN: 保护生物学借这个词追问一个种群能否靠自己继续活下去。

intro.en: Viability is the English noun of viable, which comes from Latin vita, life, through French.
intro.cn: viability 是 viable 的英语名词，viable 经法语借入，源自拉丁语 vita（生命）。

items.en: Vita means life, and vivere means to live.
items.cn: vita 意为生命，vivere 意为生活、活着。

items.en: Viable first describes a fetus able to live after birth.
items.cn: viable 最早描述出生后能存活的胎儿。

items.en: English takes viable from French medical writing.
items.cn: 英语从法语医学文献中吸收 viable。

items.en: Viable extends to plans and businesses that can work.
items.cn: viable 扩展到能够运转的计划和企业。

items.en: Viability is formed to name the quality itself.
items.cn: viability 被构成，用以命名这种性质本身。

note.en: Viability belongs with viable and viva on the form side, and with feasibility and survivability on the meaning side.
note.cn: viability 在形态上同族于 viable、viva，在意义上邻近 feasibility 与 survivability。

entries.definition: able to work or to live
entries.definitionCN: 可行的；能存活的

entries.definition: long live, an old Latin cheer
entries.definitionCN: 万岁；古老的拉丁语欢呼语

entries.definition: necessary for life or success
entries.definitionCN: 生命的；至关重要的

entries.definition: the quality of being possible to do
entries.definitionCN: 可行性

entries.definition: the ability to survive
entries.definitionCN: 生存能力

entries.definition: the quality of being solid and reliable
entries.definitionCN: 健全；可靠

normalIntro.en: Viability asks whether a thing can live: a plant, a business, or a plan must stand on its own.
normalIntro.cn: viability 追问一件事能不能活下去：一株植物、一家企业或一个计划，都得自己站得住。

normal.en: Economic viability asks whether a project can pay for itself.
normal.cn: economic viability 追问项目能否自己养活自己。

normal.en: To assess viability is to judge whether something can work.
normal.cn: assess viability 就是判断某事能否行得通。

normal.en: Fetal viability marks when a baby could live outside the womb.
normal.cn: fetal viability 标记胎儿能在子宫外存活的时间点。

normal.en: The base adjective viable comes from Latin vita, life.
normal.cn: 基础形容词 viable 来自拉丁语 vita（生命）。

normal.en: Compare feasibility: feasibility is about doing, viability is about lasting.
normal.cn: 对比 feasibility：feasibility 关注做不做得成，viability 关注能不能长久。

abstract.en: A seedling whose roots finally grip the dry soil.
abstract.cn: 一株幼苗的根终于抓住了干旱的泥土。

abstract.en: A shop that pays its own rent month after month.
abstract.cn: 一家小店一个月一个月地自己交得出房租。

abstract.en: A bridge that holds when the flood arrives.
abstract.cn: 洪水到来时仍然撑住的桥。

examples.en: The study questions the viability of the new rail link.
examples.cn: 这项研究质疑新铁路线路的可行性。

examples.en: Farmers worry about the viability of small holdings.
examples.cn: 农民担心小型农场的存续能力。

examples.en: Light and water affect the viability of the seeds.
examples.cn: 光照与水分影响种子的存活率。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为爱别离」——为了爱不得不离开，还能不能活下去？这就是 viability（生存能力）；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vita（生命）/ vivere（活着）→ 法语 viable（能存活的）→ 英语 viable → viability，核心义「能不能活下去」。

sensesIntro.en: Viability begins with the literal survival of living things, then lends that test to plans, firms, designs, and species.
sensesIntro.cn: viability 始于生物的字面存活，再把这项检验借给计划、企业、方案与物种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seedling that grips the soil and needs no watering.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株自己抓住泥土、不必再浇水的幼苗。

branches.en: A workable plan is the most common sense.
branches.cn: 可行的计划是最常见的义项。

branches.en: Literal survival of a living thing is the biological sense.
branches.cn: 生物的字面存活是生物学义项。

branches.en: A business that earns its keep is judged as a living body.
branches.cn: 能自给的企业被当作生命体来评判。

branches.en: The medical sense marks the start of independent life.
branches.cn: 医学义项标记独立生命的起点。

branches.en: Communities and species are judged by how long they can last.
branches.cn: 社区与物种都以能维持多久来评判。

intro.en: Viability is a Latin root plus suffixes, so its word family mirrors the shape of reversible and probability.
intro.cn: viability 由拉丁词根加后缀构成，其词族结构与 reversible、probability 相似。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem viv and vita run through the whole family, from vital to survive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干 viv 与 vita 贯穿整个词族，从 vital 到 survive。

items.example: The root appears in viable and vital.
items.exampleCN: 该词根出现在 viable 与 vital 中。

items.example: Latin vita means life.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 vita 意为生命。

items.example: The root appears in survive and vivid.
items.exampleCN: 该词根出现在 survive 与 vivid 中。

items.example: The suffix forms viable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 viable。

items.example: The suffix forms viability.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 viability。

items.example: The suffix forms viably.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 viably。

items.example: The prefix forms inviable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 inviable。

items.example: The suffix forms vital.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 vital。

items.example: The prefix forms survive.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sur- 构成 survive。

items.example: The prefix forms biodiversity.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 bio- 构成 biodiversity。

definition_zh: 使受害；欺负；不公平地对待；把……当作牺牲品
definition_en: to make someone suffer unfairly, especially by treating them badly or blaming them for something
core_image: 一只羊被按住，用绳子捆好，摆在祭台上
scene: 办公室里，人人都在刁难新来的同事，把差错全推给他。Everyone in the office was picking on the new colleague and victimising him for every mistake.
sceneCN: 这里 victimise 是「欺负、使受害」（第 1 个义项：不公平地伤害或苛待某人）；句意：办公室里人人都在刁难新来的同事，把每个差错都算到他头上。

pos.zh: 使受害；欺负；不公平地对待

derivatives.zh: 受害者；牺牲品，动词所由构成的根名词
victimise 加名词词尾 -ation 构成，义为「受害；被不公平对待」
同一名词的美式拼写，以 z 代替 s
动词加 -er 构成，指「施害者；欺负人的人」

senses.title: To treat someone unfairly
senses.definition: to treat a person or group badly and unfairly, so that they suffer
senses.definitionCN: 恶劣而公平地对待某人或某群体，使其遭受痛苦
senses.example: The new rules seem to victimise low paid workers.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定似乎是在苛待低收入工人。
senses.why: The word is built on victim, and its Latin source means a creature offered for sacrifice, so the verb pictures someone being put on the altar for another person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 victim 加动词词尾构成，而 victim 的拉丁语来源指献给神的祭牲，所以动词的画面是某人被摆上祭台、为他人承受代价。

senses.title: To blame someone unfairly
senses.definition: to make someone take the blame or punishment for something that is not mainly their fault
senses.definitionCN: 让某人为并非主要出于其过错的事情承担责任或受罚
senses.example: The company victimised the junior clerk instead of the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 公司拿初级职员当了替罪羊，而不是追究经理。
senses.why: A sacrifice is made so that others escape, so the verb easily slides from hurting someone to pinning the blame on them.
senses.whyCN: 献祭的本意是让别人得以脱身，因此动词很容易从「伤害某人」引申到「把责任推到某人身上」。

senses.title: To claim you have been wronged
senses.definition: to behave as if you are treated badly, or to feel that you have been unfairly hurt
senses.definitionCN: 表现得好像自己遭到苛待，或感到自己受了不公平的伤害
senses.example: Stop playing the victim and victimising yourself over one bad grade.
senses.exampleCN: 别再扮演受害者，因为一次成绩不好就觉得自己受了天大的委屈。
senses.why: Once the verb can be used about unfair treatment, the passive and reflexive patterns let a person wear the victim role almost like a garment.
senses.whyCN: 既然动词可以指「遭受不公平对待」，被动形式和反身用法就让人可以像披上一件衣服那样，把「受害者」的角色穿在自己身上。

senses.title: To make into a sacrifice
senses.definition: to put someone or something to death or loss as an offering or for a larger cause
senses.definitionCN: 为了献祭或更大的目的而让某人或某物丧命、损失
senses.example: In ancient stories, a king might victimise his own child to save the city.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老的故事里，国王可能会牺牲自己的孩子来拯救城池。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the image, the literal victim offered on the altar, kept alive in poetry and formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 这是意象最古老的一层，即真正被摆上祭台的祭品，至今在诗歌与正式文体中仍然保留。

intro.en: Victimise is formed in English from victim plus the verb suffix -ise; victim comes from Latin victima, a victim or sacrificial animal.
intro.cn: victimise 是英语由 victim 加动词词尾 -ise 构成；victim 来自拉丁语 victima，指牺牲品或祭牲。

items.en: Victima names a creature offered in sacrifice to the gods.
items.cn: victima 指献给神明的祭牲。

items.en: The word is recorded in Latin with the same sacrificial meaning; its deeper root is uncertain.
items.cn: 该词在拉丁语中已有记载，含义仍是献祭，更早的词根来源不确定。

items.en: Victim enters English as a word for a living creature killed in sacrifice.
items.cn: victim 进入英语时，指被献祭杀害的活物。

items.en: The noun widens to anyone harmed by an event or by other people.
items.cn: 名词含义扩大，指任何被事件或他人所害的人。

items.en: The noun takes the verb suffix -ise, giving victimise, to make a victim of someone.
items.cn: 名词加上动词词尾 -ise，构成 victimise，义为使人成为受害者。

items.en: Modern usage centres on unfair treatment and discrimination, often in law and social comment.
items.cn: 现代用法集中在不公平对待与歧视，常见于法律与社会评论。

note.en: Victimise shares its root with victim and victimisation, and sits near words of bullying, unfair treatment, and sacrifice.
note.cn: victimise 与 victim、victimisation 同根，并与「欺负、不公平对待、牺牲」一组词义相邻。

entries.definition: a person harmed by something
entries.definitionCN: 受害者；动词所由构成的名词

entries.definition: the act of treating someone unfairly
entries.definitionCN: 加 -ation 构成的抽象名词，义为遭受苛待

entries.definition: having no apparent harmed person
entries.definitionCN: 无受害者的，与目标词同根

entries.definition: to treat someone cruelly over a long time
entries.definitionCN: 迫害；长期残酷对待

entries.definition: to frighten or hurt a weaker person
entries.definitionCN: 欺凌；欺负弱小

entries.definition: to treat a group as worse because of who they are
entries.definitionCN: 歧视；因身份而区别对待

normalIntro.en: Victimise is victim with the verb suffix -ise, so the picture is always of someone being turned into a sacrificial victim.
normalIntro.cn: victimise 就是 victim 加上动词词尾 -ise，画面始终是某人被变成献祭的牺牲品。

normal.en: Victim is the noun, victimise is the verb, and victimisation is the act.
normal.cn: victim 是名词，victimise 是动词，victimisation 指这种行为本身。

normal.en: American spelling writes z instead of s, giving victimize.
normal.cn: 美式拼写把 s 换成 z，写成 victimize。

normal.en: To feel victimised is to believe others treat you unfairly.
normal.cn: feel victimised 表示觉得自己受到不公平对待。

normal.en: The passive is very common: workers were victimised for speaking out.
normal.cn: 被动式很常见：说出真相的工人遭到了苛待。

normal.en: The near word persecute adds cruelty and duration; victimise stresses an unfair outcome.
normal.cn: 近义词 persecute 更强调残酷与长期，victimise 更强调不公平的结果。

abstract.en: Picture a lamb tied and laid on an altar while others step back safely.
abstract.cn: 想象一只羊被捆好放上祭台，旁人则安然退开。

abstract.en: Imagine a tray of blame being slid across the table to the smallest chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一整盘责任沿着桌面，被推到最小那把椅子的主人面前。

abstract.en: See a person wearing a pale mask labelled victim, and pulling it on by themselves.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人戴上写着 «victim» 的苍白面罩，而且是自己动手戴上的。

examples.en: Several staff claimed they had been victimised by their manager.
examples.cn: 几名员工声称自己受到了经理的苛待。

examples.en: Laws exist to protect workers who are victimised for reporting unsafe conditions.
examples.cn: 法律保护那些因举报不安全条件而遭苛待的员工。

examples.en: She refused to victimise the younger members of the team.
examples.cn: 她拒绝拿团队里较年轻的成员开刀。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂客太卖」——把客人喂了就要被卖去祭台，成了 victim；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 victima（祭牲；牺牲品）→ 英语 victim（受害者）→ victim + -ise → victimise（使受害）；更早词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: From the sacrifice image, victimise grows into four senses: unfair treatment, unfair blame, the self made victim, and the literal offering.
sensesIntro.cn: 从献祭的画面出发，victimise 长成四个义项：不公平对待、不公平归责、自我认定的受害者，以及字面上的献祭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamb held down on an altar, offered up for others.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只羊被按在祭台上，替别人献出。

branches.en: Unfair treatment is the everyday modern sense.
branches.cn: 不公平对待是现代最常用的义项。

branches.en: Blaming someone replaces hurting them directly.
branches.cn: 把责任推给别人，取代了直接的伤害。

branches.en: The victim role can be taken up by the person themselves.
branches.cn: 受害者角色也可以由当事人自己穿上。

branches.en: The literal sacrifice is the oldest layer of meaning.
branches.cn: 字面上的献祭是最古老的一层含义。

branches.en: Both treating badly and shifting blame leave one person carrying the cost.
branches.cn: 苛待与推责都让同一个人承担代价。

intro.en: Victimise is built from the noun victim plus the English verb suffix -ise, with victimisation, victimiser and victimless around it.
intro.cn: victimise 由名词 victim 加英语动词词尾 -ise 构成，周围有 victimisation、victimiser 与 victimless。

latinIntro.en: Latin victima means a sacrificial animal or a victim; its deeper origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 victima 意为祭牲或牺牲品，更早的来源不确定。

items.example: Victima supplies the sacrifice image.
items.exampleCN: victima 提供献祭的意象。

items.example: Victim is the noun behind the verb.
items.exampleCN: victim 是动词背后的名词。

items.example: The suffix -ise turns nouns into verbs like victimise.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 把名词变成 victimise 这类动词。

items.example: Victimise means to make a victim of someone.
items.exampleCN: victimise 意为使某人成为受害者。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为与过程的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms victimisation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 victimisation。

items.example: Victimisation names the process itself.
items.exampleCN: victimisation 指这一过程本身。

items.example: The suffix -er forms victimiser.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 victimiser。

items.example: The suffix -less forms victimless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 victimless。

items.meaningCN: 美式拼写中与 -ised 相对
items.example: Victimized keeps the same meaning as victimised.
items.exampleCN: victimized 与 victimised 含义相同。

definition_zh: 活力；精力；体力；魄力；强度
definition_en: physical strength and energy, or active force and lively power
core_image: 春天新生的枝条饱满有力，向上舒展
scene: 老教练走上球场，步伐稳健有力，讲话声音洪亮。The old coach still walked onto the pitch with surprising vigor and a voice that carried.
sceneCN: 这里 vigor 是「活力、精力」（第 1 个义项：身体与时下的充沛精力）；句意：老教练依然步伐出奇有力，讲话声音传得很远。

pos.zh: 活力；精力；体力
魄力；干劲
强度；效力（多用于美式拼写）

derivatives.zh: vigor 加形容词词尾 -ous 构成，义为「有力的；精力充沛的」
vigorous 再加副词词尾 -ly，义为「有力地；积极地」
同一词的英式拼写，以 ou 代替 o
拉丁语 in-（使）+ vigorare 构成，义为「使振奋；使有活力」

senses.title: Physical strength and energy
senses.definition: great physical strength and steady energy of body
senses.definitionCN: 身体上充沛的体力与持久的精力
senses.example: Despite his age, he climbed the hill with real vigor.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管年纪大了，他爬上山坡时依然劲头十足。
senses.why: Latin vigor means liveliness and activity, so the word first names the living force in a body that is fully awake.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vigor 意为「活力、活动」，所以这个词首先指一具充分苏醒的身体里那股活生生的力量。

senses.title: Energy in effort and action
senses.definition: forceful, eager energy shown in the way a person works or acts
senses.definitionCN: 一个人工作或行动时表现出的有力而热切的能量
senses.example: She defended the plan with great vigor.
senses.exampleCN: 她非常有力地维护了这项计划。
senses.why: The energy inside a body naturally shows up outside it, in how firmly someone argues, works, or drives a task forward.
senses.whyCN: 身体里的能量自然会外露，表现为一个人辩论、做事或推进任务时的力度。

senses.title: Force or intensity of something
senses.definition: the strength or intensity with which a thing operates, grows, or takes effect
senses.definitionCN: 事物运作、生长或生效时的强度与猛烈程度
senses.example: The storm hit the coast with unexpected vigor.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴以出人意料的猛烈程度袭击了海岸。
senses.why: Because vigor is living force, it can be lent to storms, plants, and arguments, where it becomes measurable force or intensity.
senses.whyCN: 因为 vigor 是「活的力量」，它可以借给风暴、植物和论证，在那里变成可感知的力度与强度。

senses.title: Legal force or validity
senses.definition: the binding force of a law, agreement, or claim, common in legal phrasing
senses.definitionCN: 法律、协议或主张所具有的约束力，多见于法律用语
senses.example: The clause will keep its vigor for five years.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款将保持效力五年。
senses.why: A rule has force only while it is alive in the minds of those it binds, so the image of living energy gave a formal word for legal force.
senses.whyCN: 规则只有在受约束者心目中「活着」时才有力量，因此这股活生生的能量在正式语体里演化出「法律效力」的含义。

intro.en: Vigor comes from Latin vigor, liveliness or vigour, from vigere, to be lively or thrive; English borrowed it through Old French vigour.
intro.cn: vigor 来自拉丁语 vigor（活力、强健），源于 vigere（有生机、兴盛），经古法语 vigour 进入英语。

items.en: Vigere means to be lively, vigorous, or in full strength.
items.cn: vigere 意为有生机、强健或充满力量。

items.en: Vigor names liveliness and active strength.
items.cn: vigor 指活力与活跃的力量。

items.en: Vigour carries the noun into medieval French with the same sense.
items.cn: vigour 带着同样的含义进入中世纪法语。

items.en: Vigour enters English meaning active physical strength.
items.cn: vigour 进入英语，指活跃的体力。

items.en: The sense widens to the force of things such as storms, laws, and arguments.
items.cn: 词义扩展到风暴、法律、论证等事物的力度。

items.en: American spelling settles on vigor, while British usage keeps vigour.
items.cn: 美式拼写固定为 vigor，英式仍用 vigour。

note.en: Vigor is a living force, close to vigorous and invigorate in form, and to energy words in meaning.
note.cn: vigor 是一股活的力量，形式上与 vigorous、invigorate 同族，意义上与「精力」类词相邻。

entries.definition: strong and full of energy
entries.definitionCN: 有力的；精力充沛的，与目标词同族

entries.definition: in a strong, energetic way
entries.definitionCN: vigorous 加 -ly 构成的副词

entries.definition: to give fresh energy to
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语 in- 加 vigor 同根词，义为使振奋

entries.definition: the strength needed to be active
entries.definitionCN: 能量；精力，最中性的说法

entries.definition: the power to live and grow
entries.definitionCN: 生命力；生机，更强调生长与持续

entries.definition: the quality of being full of life
entries.definitionCN: 活泼；生气，语气更轻松

normalIntro.en: Vigor is the living force behind vigorous and invigorate: a body, a plant, or a debate that is fully awake.
normalIntro.cn: vigor 是 vigorous 与 invigorate 背后的那股活力量：一具身体、一株植物或一场辩论完全苏醒过来。

normal.en: Vigor is the noun; vigorous and vigorously are its adjective and adverb.
normal.cn: vigor 是名词，vigorous 与 vigorously 分别是形容词和副词。

normal.en: Americans write vigor, the British write vigour.
normal.cn: 美式写 vigor，英式写 vigour。

normal.en: With vigor means in a strong and energetic way.
normal.cn: with vigor 表示有力地、精力充沛地。

normal.en: Invigorate adds the prefix in- to give new vigor to someone.
normal.cn: invigorate 加上前缀 in-，表示给人注入新的活力。

normal.en: Compare energy: vigor has a slightly literary and bodily feel.
normal.cn: 对比 energy：vigor 更偏书面，也更有身体感。

abstract.en: Picture a fresh green shoot pushing straight up through hard soil in spring.
abstract.cn: 想象春天里嫩绿的枝条顶开硬土，笔直向上。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand thrusting a heavy door open with one firm shove.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手稳稳一推，把沉重的门推开。

abstract.en: See a storm leaning its whole shoulder against a row of trees.
abstract.cn: 想象一场风暴把整个肩膀压在一排树上。

examples.en: The dancers performed with such vigor that the audience rose to its feet.
examples.cn: 舞者们跳得充满力量，观众纷纷起身鼓掌。

examples.en: After a long holiday she returned to work with renewed vigor.
examples.cn: 长假之后，她带着重振的活力回到工作岗位。

examples.en: Critics attacked the proposal with surprising vigor.
examples.cn: 批评者们以出人意料的强硬猛烈攻击这项提案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威哥」——威猛的哥哥，浑身是劲，就是 vigor；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vigere（有生机、强健）→ 拉丁语 vigor（活力）→ 古法语 vigour → 英语 vigour / vigor；核心义「活的力量」。

sensesIntro.en: Vigor begins as the energy inside a living body, spreads to energetic action, then to the force of storms and arguments, and finally to the binding force of law.
sensesIntro.cn: vigor 起初指活物身体里的能量，继而指充满干劲的行动，再指风暴与辩论的力度，最后指法律的约束效力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spring shoot pushing up, full of living power.
core.cn: 核心意象：春天的新枝充满生机地向上顶出。

branches.en: Bodily strength is the oldest concrete sense.
branches.cn: 体力是最古老、最具体的义项。

branches.en: Energetic action lets the inner force show in public.
branches.cn: 充满干劲的行动让内在力量外显于众人面前。

branches.en: Storms and arguments borrow the force of a living body.
branches.cn: 风暴与论证借用了活物的力量。

branches.en: Legal force is the formal, abstract end of the chain.
branches.cn: 法律效力是链条上最正式、最抽象的一端。

branches.en: A strong body shows vigor both at rest and in effort.
branches.cn: 强壮的身体无论静止还是发力都显出活力。

intro.en: Vigor is a bare Latin noun in English, with vigorous, vigorously, vigour, and invigorate around it.
intro.cn: vigor 在英语中是原样借入的拉丁语名词，周围有 vigorous、vigorously、vigour 与 invigorate。

latinIntro.en: Latin vigere means to be lively, and vigor is its noun of liveliness and strength.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vigere 意为有生机，vigor 是它表示活力与力量的名词。

items.example: Vigere supplies the living energy.
items.exampleCN: vigere 提供活生生的能量。

items.example: Vigor is borrowed unchanged into English.
items.exampleCN: vigor 原样借入英语。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms vigorous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成 vigorous。

items.example: Vigorous describes a lively person or action.
items.exampleCN: vigorous 描述充满活力的人或行动。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms vigorously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 vigorously。

items.example: In- plus a vigor root gives invigorate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 加 vigor 词根构成 invigorate。

items.example: The prefix in- adds the idea of putting energy in.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 带来「把能量放进去」的意思。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms invigoration.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 invigoration。

items.example: Invigoration names the act of refreshing.
items.exampleCN: invigoration 指使人焕然一新的行为。

definition_zh: 卑鄙的；可耻的；令人厌恶的；粗劣的
definition_en: extremely unpleasant, morally bad, or of very poor quality
core_image: 一堆腐烂发臭的垃圾，路人捂鼻绕开
scene: 孩子在地铁上被陌生人当众辱骂，旁边的人都很气愤。The whole carriage was shocked by the vile abuse that the stranger shouted at the boy.
sceneCN: 这里 vile 是「卑劣的、可耻的」（第 1 个义项：道德上极其恶劣）；句意：那陌生人对男孩大喊的污言秽语让整节车厢的人都感到震惊。

pos.zh: 卑鄙的；可耻的；道德败坏
令人厌恶的；恶心的
粗劣的；糟糕透顶的

derivatives.zh: vile 加名词词尾 -ness 构成，义为「卑劣；厌恶」
vile 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「卑劣地；恶劣地」
vile 的拉丁同源动词，义为「诽谤；污蔑」
vilify 加 -ation 构成的名词，义为「诽谤；诋毁」

senses.title: Morally disgusting
senses.definition: extremely bad and shocking in moral terms
senses.definitionCN: 在道德上极其恶劣、令人震惊的
senses.example: It was a vile act of cruelty to a defenceless animal.
senses.exampleCN: 这是对毫无防备的动物的可耻虐待行为。
senses.why: Latin vilis means cheap and worthless, and to be morally worthless is to be vile in the strongest modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vilis 意为廉价、无价值；在道德上一文不值，就是现代最强意义上的 vile。

senses.title: Extremely unpleasant
senses.definition: so unpleasant to the senses that one wants to turn away
senses.definitionCN: 对感官而言极不愉快，让人想转身避开
senses.example: A vile smell came from the drain outside the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房外的下水道传来令人作呕的臭味。
senses.why: The cheap and worthless image is also an image of rot and refuse, which explains why the word covers smells, tastes, and sights.
senses.whyCN: 「廉价、无价值」的意象同时也带出腐烂与垃圾的画面，因此这个词也用于气味、味道和景象。

senses.title: Of very poor quality
senses.definition: of such low quality or in such bad conditions that it is barely worth having
senses.definitionCN: 质量极低、条件极差，几乎不值得拥有
senses.example: The hikers spent a night in a vile cramped hut.
senses.exampleCN: 徒步者在一间又简陋又拥挤的棚屋里过了一夜。
senses.why: Here the original idea of cheapness returns almost literally: things, food, rooms, and weather can all be worthless and wretched.
senses.whyCN: 这里「廉价」的原意几乎原样回来了：物品、食物、房间、天气都可以既一文不值又糟糕。

intro.en: Vile comes through Old French vil from Latin vilis, meaning cheap, inexpensive, or worthless.
intro.cn: vile 经古法语 vil 来自拉丁语 vilis，意为廉价、不值钱的、无价值的。

items.en: Vilis means cheap in price or low in worth.
items.cn: vilis 意为价格低廉或价值不高。

items.en: Vil keeps the sense of base, mean, and of little worth.
items.cn: vil 保留「卑下的、低贱的」含义。

items.en: Vile enters English describing what is cheap and common.
items.cn: vile 进入英语，用来形容廉价而普通的东西。

items.en: The word shifts from cheap toward morally base and despicable.
items.cn: 词义从「廉价」转向「道德卑劣、可鄙」。

items.en: A further shift brings physical disgust, so vile smells and tastes are possible.
items.cn: 词义再进一步，带出生理上的厌恶，于是有了难闻的气味与难吃的味道。

items.en: Modern English keeps the moral, unpleasant, and poor quality senses side by side.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留道德、厌恶与低劣质量三层含义。

note.en: Vile is the adjective of cheapness turned into disgust; its family includes vilify and vileness, and it stands beside words for wickedness and filth.
note.cn: vile 由「廉价」这一形容词义转成厌恶之词，词族包含 vilify 与 vileness，并与表示邪恶、污秽的词相邻。

entries.definition: to say bad things about someone
entries.definitionCN: 同根动词，义为诽谤、污蔑

entries.definition: the quality of being vile
entries.definitionCN: 加 -ness 构成的抽象名词，义为卑劣

entries.definition: a wicked character or person
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同：villain 来自农奴一词

entries.definition: deserving to be hated
entries.definitionCN: 可鄙的；值得憎恨的

entries.definition: so unpleasant that it pushes you away
entries.definitionCN: 令人反感的，更偏生理排斥

entries.definition: bad and miserable in condition
entries.definitionCN: 恶劣的；悲惨的，更强调处境

normalIntro.en: Vile starts as Latin vilis, cheap and worthless, and from there becomes the word for what is disgusting in morals, senses, or quality.
normalIntro.cn: vile 起初是拉丁语 vilis，意为廉价、不值钱，由此变成同时表示道德、感官与质量上「令人恶心」的词。

normal.en: Vile is the adjective; vileness and vilely are its noun and adverb.
normal.cn: vile 是形容词，vileness 与 vilely 分别是名词和副词。

normal.en: The comparative is viler and the superlative is vilest.
normal.cn: 比较级是 viler，最高级是 vilest。

normal.en: Vile language and vile insults are its most common moral collocations.
normal.cn: vile language 与 vile insults 是它最常见的道德类搭配。

normal.en: The same root gives vilify, to make someone look worthless, and vilification.
normal.cn: 同一词根构成 vilify（使人显得一文不值）与 vilification。

normal.en: Villain is only a spelling neighbour and comes from a different word.
normal.cn: villain 只是拼写上的邻居，来自另一个词。

abstract.en: Picture a bin overflowing in summer while everyone holds their breath.
abstract.cn: 想象夏天的垃圾桶满溢，所有人都屏住呼吸。

abstract.en: Imagine words dropping out of a mouth and turning black as they land.
abstract.cn: 想象话语从口中落下，一落地就变黑。

abstract.en: See a hut so cramped and damp that the door sags.
abstract.cn: 想象一间又挤又潮的小屋，门都塌了下来。

examples.en: The court condemned the vile treatment of the prisoners.
examples.cn: 法庭谴责了那种对待囚犯的卑劣做法。

examples.en: There was a vile smell coming from the old fridge.
examples.cn: 旧冰箱里散发出一股恶臭。

examples.en: They were forced to leave their homes for a vile shelter on the edge of town.
examples.cn: 他们不得不离开家，住进城郊一个条件极差的避难所。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪了」——品行歪了，就是卑劣的 vile；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vilis（廉价的；无价值的）→ 古法语 vil → 英语 vile（卑劣的；令人厌恶的）；核心义「低贱、不值钱」。

sensesIntro.en: Vile begins with the idea of cheapness and worthlessness, which splits into moral vileness, physical disgust, and poor quality.
sensesIntro.cn: vile 从「廉价、无价值」出发，分出道德卑劣、感官厌恶与质量低劣三层含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heap of rotting rubbish that passers by step away from.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堆腐烂的垃圾，路人纷纷绕开。

branches.en: Moral vileness is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 道德卑劣是现代最主要的义项。

branches.en: Physical disgust grows out of the rubbish image.
branches.cn: 生理厌恶由垃圾意象生长而来。

branches.en: Poor quality returns to the original idea of cheapness.
branches.cn: 质量低劣回到「廉价」的原意。

branches.en: A vile act and a vile smell both make people step back.
branches.cn: 卑劣的行为与恶臭都让人退开一步。

branches.en: Vile rooms and vile weather are both wretched to live through.
branches.cn: 糟糕的房间与恶劣的天气都令人难以忍受。

intro.en: Vile is a Latin borrowing with little internal structure in English, so its family is built with suffixes and the Latin root vilis.
intro.cn: vile 是从拉丁语借入的词，在英语里几乎没有内部结构，所以它的词族靠加词尾与拉丁词根 vilis 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is vilis, cheap or worthless, with the related verb vilificare, to cheapen or despise.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 vilis（廉价、无价值），相关动词 vilificare 意为贬低、轻视。

items.example: Vilis gives the core idea of cheapness.
items.exampleCN: vilis 提供「廉价」的核心含义。

items.example: Vil is the Old French step into English.
items.exampleCN: vil 是进入英语的古法语形式。

items.example: Vile keeps the base and worthless sense.
items.exampleCN: vile 保留低贱与无价值的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms vileness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 vileness。

items.example: Vileness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: vileness 指这种性质本身。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms vilely.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 vilely。

items.example: The suffix -ify forms vilify from the Latin root.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ify 由拉丁词根构成 vilify。

items.meaning: to speak ill of, to slander
items.example: Vilify means to make someone cheap in others eyes.
items.exampleCN: vilify 意为使某人在他人眼中变得一文不值。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms vilification.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 vilification。

definition_zh: 别墅；乡间宅邸；（尤指度假用的）海滨别墅；古罗马的乡村庄园
definition_en: a large house in the countryside or by the sea, often used for holidays, or a country estate of the ancient Roman kind
core_image: 葡萄园边一座白色大宅，露台朝向山坡与海面
scene: 意大利南部的山坡上，白墙红瓦的宅子藏在橄榄树之间，露台正对着平静的海面。Our holiday villa looked out over the sea from the olive groves.
sceneCN: 这里 villa 是「（度假用的）别墅」（第 1 个义项：乡下或海边的宽敞住宅）；句意为我们度假住的那栋别墅从橄榄林间眺望海面。白墙、露台与山坡正是这个词的核心画面。

pos.zh: 别墅；乡间宽敞的住宅（尤指度假住宅）
庄园宅邸；古代罗马人的乡村别墅
（英国地名中）沿街独立的联排住宅或宅邸建筑

collocations.phrase: the ruins of a Roman villa

derivatives.zh: 由 villager 与 -er 构成，指村中居住的人，即「村民」；与 villa 同出于拉丁语「村落」一词
由古法语 village 构成，义为「村庄」；与 villa 同源，都指一群人聚居的地方
由古法语 ville 演变而来，指中世纪英格兰的村庄或采邑单位，保留「聚居地」的古义

senses.title: A grand holiday house in the country or by the sea
senses.titleCN: 乡间或海边的度假别墅
senses.definition: a large, comfortable house in the countryside or near the sea, often rented for holidays
senses.definitionCN: 乡间或海边宽敞舒适的住宅，常被租来度假
senses.example: We rented a villa in Tuscany for two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在托斯卡纳租了一栋别墅，住了两个星期。
senses.why: Latin villa was the country house of a landowner, and the holiday sense keeps the same image: a fine house set out of town where people go to rest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 villa 是地主的乡间宅邸，度假义沿用同一画面：一栋精致的宅子建在城外，供人前去歇息。

senses.title: A wealthy country estate of the Roman kind
senses.definition: in ancient Rome, a country estate with a house and farmland worked by tenants or slaves
senses.definitionCN: 古罗马带宅邸与农田的乡村庄园，由佃农或奴隶耕种
senses.example: Archaeologists excavated a Roman villa near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 考古学家在河边发掘了一处古罗马庄园。
senses.why: Both farm and dwelling sat inside one boundary, so villa named not just the house but the whole estate with its land.
senses.whyCN: 住宅与田地在同一圈地界之内，所以 villa 不只指房子，还兼指连同土地的整座庄园。

senses.title: A fashionable suburban house
senses.definition: in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, a detached house in a smart suburb built for a wealthy family
senses.definitionCN: 十八、十九世纪建在时髦郊区、供富裕家庭居住的独立住宅
senses.example: The street was lined with modest Georgian villas.
senses.exampleCN: 这条街两侧是一排排朴素的乔治式住宅。
senses.why: Town houses were tall and shared, so a villa promised detached walls and a small garden, echoing the manor outside the city.
senses.whyCN: 城里住宅高耸而联排，villa 则意味着独门独户加一方小园，是对城外宅邸的呼应。

senses.title: A house with a private pool and staff
senses.titleCN: 带私人泳池与管家的宅邸
senses.definition: a modern holiday property let complete with a pool, garden and sometimes household staff
senses.definitionCN: 现代可供整栋租住的度假房产，通常带泳池、花园，有时还配管家
senses.example: The villa came with a cook and two cleaners.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋别墅配有厨师和两名保洁。
senses.why: A rented villa is more than a room: the whole estate is hired, so the word now implies luxury and full facilities.
senses.whyCN: 租别墅租的是整座庄园而不只是一个房间，于是这个词如今带着奢华与配套齐全的意味。

senses.title: A name in British street addresses
senses.definition: in British use, a house or block of houses named Villa in a street or residential terrace, as in Acacia Villas
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法中街道或联排住宅里以 Villa 命名的独立住宅或一排房子，如金合欢别墅
senses.example: They lived in one of the Villas off the High Street.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在高街附近那排别墅住宅中的一栋。
senses.why: Victorian builders borrowed the grand name for ordinary terraces, so villa became an address label as much as a type of house.
senses.whyCN: 维多利亚时代的营造商把这个气派的名字借给普通联排住宅，于是 villa 既是房屋类型，也成了门牌的一部分。

intro.en: Villa is a Latin word for a country house and estate, built on the farmstead root vic-, which also gave vicus and village.
intro.cn: villa 是拉丁语中表示乡间宅邸与庄园的词，建在表示农庄的词根 vic- 上，同一词根还给出 vicus 与 village。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning a clan settlement or homestead lies behind the family.
items.cn: 一个表示氏族聚落或家园的重构词根是这一词族的源头。

items.en: Villa means a country house with its land; vicus means a cluster of dwellings, and vicinus means a neighbour.
items.cn: villa 意为带田地的乡间宅邸，vicus 指一片聚居的房舍，vicinus 意为邻居。

items.en: Roman writers describe working estates, and grander ones with gardens, baths and frescoes.
items.cn: 罗马作家笔下既有耕作的庄园，也有带花园、浴场与壁画的豪华庄园。

items.en: Ville means a town or country house, and the English form villa is taken from the Latin original.
items.cn: 古法语 ville 指城镇或乡下宅子，英语 villa 则直接取自拉丁语原形。

items.en: Travellers bring villa back in the classical sense of a fine house on an estate.
items.cn: 旅行者把 villa 以「庄园中的精美宅邸」这一古典义带回英语。

items.en: The word spreads from suburban houses to rented seaside homes and hotel resorts.
items.cn: 这个词从郊区住宅扩展到出租的海边住宅与度假酒店。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words from the same settlement root, and the near-meaning group holds other kinds of fine dwelling with different scale or tenure.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「聚居地」词根出来的词，近义组收其他类型的精美住宅，规模与产权形式各不相同。

entries.definition: a small settlement in the countryside
entries.definitionCN: 村子；村庄

entries.definition: a person who lives in a village
entries.definitionCN: 村民

entries.definition: a wicked character, once simply a farm worker; it only looks like kin and comes from Latin villa, a farmyard, without the villa sense
entries.definitionCN: 恶棍；反派，原指农庄里的人，来自拉丁语 villa「农家庭院」而不是庄园义，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: a very large impressive house, often in a town
entries.definitionCN: 豪宅；大厦

entries.definition: a small old house, especially in the country
entries.definitionCN: 小村舍；乡间小屋

entries.definition: a house with all rooms on one level
entries.definitionCN: 平房；单层住宅

normalIntro.en: Villa belongs to the Latin settlement family: it was the house on the estate, beside the ground farmed by the people of the village.
normalIntro.cn: villa 属于拉丁语「聚居地」词族：它是庄园里的那栋宅子，旁边就是村里人耕种的田地。

normal.en: The same Latin family gives village and villager, both about people clustered on the land.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词族还给出 village 与 villager，都与土地上聚居的人有关。

normal.en: Ancient villa meant house plus farmland, not a weekend home.
normal.cn: 古时的 villa 指宅子加农田，而不是周末的度假屋。

normal.en: To rent a villa is to take the whole house and garden for a holiday.
normal.cn: rent a villa 就是把整栋房子和花园租下来度假。

normal.en: A Roman villa ruin is dug up with floors under the plough soil.
normal.cn: 古罗马别墅遗址被发掘出来时，地面往往埋在耕地之下。

normal.en: Compare mansion: mansion has no land and often sits in a city, while villa implies country or sea.
normal.cn: 对比 mansion：mansion 不带土地，多在城市里，而 villa 暗示乡间或海边。

abstract.en: Picture a white house among vines with a terrace facing the sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋白房子立在葡萄园中，露台面朝大海。

abstract.en: See a boundary wall run around a house, a well and rows of crops.
abstract.cn: 看一堵围墙把住宅、水井和一排排庄稼圈在一起。

abstract.en: Think of a suburban street where every second house says Villa on the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一条郊区街道，隔几户门牌上就写着别墅。

examples.en: Their villa has a pool and a view of the bay.
examples.cn: 他们的别墅有泳池，还能看到海湾的景色。

examples.en: The guide showed us the mosaic floor of a Roman villa.
examples.cn: 导游带我们看了古罗马别墅的马赛克地面。

examples.en: Families often rent a villa instead of booking hotel rooms.
examples.cn: 一家人出游常常租整栋别墅，而不是订酒店房间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「微勒」——微风吹着，勒绳一提，小马停在大宅子门口；别墅往往就在这样有风的乡下。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 villa「乡间宅邸、庄园」→ 英语 villa；同根词 vicus（村落）、vicinus（邻居）与 village、villager 共享表示「聚居之处的农庄」的词根，更早的印欧来源只能写作重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Villa starts as the house on a Roman estate, softens into a Victorian suburban house, then becomes the rented holiday home of today, and lingers in British street names.
sensesIntro.cn: villa 起初是古罗马庄园里的宅邸，后来成为维多利亚时代的郊区住宅，再演变为今天可整栋租住的度假别墅，并留在英国的门牌里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a large white house inside its own walled grounds, with vines and a terrace facing the hillside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栋白色大宅立在自家庭院内，院墙里有葡萄藤，露台朝向山坡。

branches.en: The holiday branch: a fine house away from town where guests come to rest.
branches.cn: 度假线：远离城市的精致住宅，客人前来歇息。

branches.en: The estate branch: house and land inside one boundary, worked by others.
branches.cn: 庄园线：住宅与田地在同一圈地界内，由他人耕作。

branches.en: The town branch: builders carry the grand name into detached suburban houses and street names.
branches.cn: 城市线：营造商把这个气派名字带到郊区独栋住宅与门牌上。

branches.en: The luxury branch: renting by the whole house turns the place into a package of pool and staff.
branches.cn: 奢华线：整栋出租让这个地方变成带泳池与管家的整套产品。

branches.en: Both senses share one promise: plenty of space, outdoors, and time away.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享同一个许诺：足够宽敞、有户外空间、远离日常。

intro.en: Villa is a short Latin noun with almost no affixes of its own; its family comes from the settlement root shared with village, villager and the Old French ville.
intro.cn: villa 是简短的拉丁名词，本身几乎没有词缀；它的词族来自与 village、villager 及古法语 ville 共享的「聚居地」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin villa, vicus and vicinus are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European form is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 villa、vicus 与 vicinus 均有文献记录，只有更早的印欧语形式属于重构。

items.meaning: a country house with its land
items.example: Villa is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: villa 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The root vic- ties villa to village words.
items.exampleCN: 词根 vic- 把 villa 与表示村庄的词连在一起。

items.meaning: a village or group of dwellings
items.example: Vicus shows the root outside the villa word itself.
items.exampleCN: vicus 显示这一词根在 villa 之外的用法。

items.example: Vicinus is the person who settles nearby.
items.exampleCN: vicinus 就是住在旁边的人。

items.example: Old French ville develops from the Latin form.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 ville 由拉丁语形式发展而来。

items.example: Village keeps the settlement sense of the root.
items.exampleCN: village 保留词根的「聚居地」含义。

items.example: The suffix -er turns village into villager.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把 village 变成 villager。

items.meaning: a person living in a village
items.example: Villager is the resident of the settlement.
items.exampleCN: villager 是聚居地里的居民。

items.example: Vill survives in old place-name histories.
items.exampleCN: vill 仍见于旧地名的记载中。

definition_zh: 葡萄藤；葡萄属植物；攀缘植物；藤蔓
definition_en: a climbing plant that bears grapes, or more widely any plant that climbs by winding stems
core_image: 一根卷须绕上棚架，藤蔓一路攀爬，挂满成串的葡萄
scene: 法国南部的葡萄园里，成排老藤攀在架子上，卷须紧紧缠住铁丝，枝头垂着沉甸甸的果串。A heavy old vine climbed the wall and hung its grapes over the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 vine 是「葡萄藤」（第 1 个义项：结葡萄的攀缘植物）；句意为一根粗壮的老藤爬上墙头，把葡萄探过大门。卷须、棚架与果串正是这个词的核心画面。

pos.zh: 葡萄藤；葡萄树
攀缘植物；藤蔓
（the vine 的转喻）葡萄酒

collocations.phrase: grapes picked fresh off the vine
collocations.zh: 直接从藤上摘下的新鲜葡萄
（计划、想法）因缺乏支持而夭折

derivatives.zh: 由 vine 加中古英语 yard（园地）构成，义为「葡萄园」
由拉丁语 vinum（葡萄酒）与 cultura（耕种）构成，义为「酿酒葡萄栽培」
由 vinegar 加形容词词尾 -y 构成，义为「酸味的、可酸溜的」；vinegar 本义即「酸酒」

senses.title: The grape plant itself
senses.definition: the climbing woody plant whose fruit is the grape
senses.definitionCN: 以葡萄为果实的攀缘木质植物
senses.example: Each vine is tied to a post and pruned every winter.
senses.exampleCN: 每根葡萄藤都被绑在桩上，每年冬天修剪一次。
senses.why: Latin vinea named the whole plantation, and its small form vinea took on the single plant, so vine now names one growing stalk of grapes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vinea 原指整片葡萄园，其较短形式转指单株，于是 vine 如今指一棵正在生长的葡萄藤。

senses.title: Any climbing plant with tendrils
senses.definition: a plant that climbs or trails by stems, tendrils or runners rather than standing alone
senses.definitionCN: 靠茎、卷须或匍匐枝攀爬蔓延而不独立挺立的植物
senses.example: Ivy and other vines now cover the old brick wall.
senses.exampleCN: 常春藤和其他藤蔓如今盖满了老砖墙。
senses.why: Grape vines were the best known of all climbers, so gardener speech extended the name to the whole shape: anything that climbs is a vine.
senses.whyCN: 葡萄藤是所有攀缘植物中最出名的一种，园丁的说法于是把名字扩到整个形态：会攀爬的都是 vine。

senses.title: Wine as it is served from the grape
senses.definition: wine, especially as a product that comes off the grape, in set phrases and trade talk
senses.definitionCN: 葡萄酒，尤指直接来自葡萄的产品，见于固定短语与行业用语
senses.example: He makes his own wine from the vine.
senses.exampleCN: 他的酒是自己从葡萄酿出来的。
senses.why: The plant and its drink sit in one continuous process, so the container can stand for the product, as in terms like the fruit of the vine.
senses.whyCN: 植物和它的饮品处在同一个连续的过程里，容器可以代指产物，所以常有「葡萄的果实」这类说法。

senses.title: In idioms, something that grows or withers
senses.definition: in fixed phrases, a picture of growth that is supported or neglected, as in fruit fresh on the vine
senses.definitionCN: 在固定短语里表示受到扶持或遭人冷落的生长，如刚离藤的新鲜果实
senses.example: Without funding the plan will die on the vine.
senses.exampleCN: 没有资金，这个计划会半途夭折。
senses.why: Anything that hangs on a vine must be picked in time or rot, so the image of a fruit still on the stem now describes any unsupported idea.
senses.whyCN: 挂在藤上的果子必须及时采收，否则会烂，于是「还长在藤上」的画面被用来形容无人支持的想法。

senses.title: The vine as a decorative pattern
senses.definition: a curling design of leaves and stems used to decorate pottery, cloth or metalwork
senses.definitionCN: 用于装饰陶器、布匹或金属器的卷曲枝叶图案
senses.example: The cup is trimmed with a band of green vine.
senses.exampleCN: 杯子口沿镶着一圈绿色的藤蔓纹。
senses.why: The winding stem is easy to draw and easy to repeat, so the plant itself became an ornament that can be printed on any surface.
senses.whyCN: 卷曲的藤茎既好画又好重复，于是植物本身成了可以印在任何表面的装饰。

intro.en: Vine comes from Latin vinea, a grape plantation, which grew from vinum, wine, and the two have stayed in the same family.
intro.cn: vine 来自拉丁语 vinea（葡萄园），而 vinea 又出自 vinum（葡萄酒），二者一直同属一族。

items.en: A reconstructed root for wine lies behind the Latin words; the exact form is debated.
items.cn: 一个表示「葡萄酒」的重构词根是拉丁语词的源头，确切形式仍有争议。

items.en: Vinum means wine, vinea means a vineyard, and vinnulus is a mild word for wine.
items.cn: vinum 意为葡萄酒，vinea 意为葡萄园，vinnulus 是对葡萄酒的温和说法。

items.en: Vin means wine and vigne means a vine, both carried north from Latin.
items.cn: 古法语 vin 意为葡萄酒，vigne 意为葡萄藤，都自拉丁语北传而来。

items.en: Wīn, the English word for wine, arrives early from Latin and keeps the plant and drink in one group.
items.cn: 古英语 wīn 很早就借自拉丁语，把植物与饮品留在同一词族里。

items.en: Vine enters English about the thirteenth century as the name of the climbing plant.
items.cn: vine 约在十三世纪进入英语，指攀升的植物。

items.en: The word widens to other climbers and to patterns printed from the stem.
items.cn: 词义扩展到其他攀缘植物，以及取自藤茎的纹样。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the vine and wine family, and the near-meaning group gathers other climbing or fruiting plants with different habits.
note.cn: 形近组收「藤」与「酒」同族的词，近义组收其他攀缘或结果植物，习性各不相同。

entries.definition: a field where grapes are grown
entries.definitionCN: 葡萄园

entries.definition: the growing of grapes for wine
entries.definitionCN: 葡萄栽培；酿酒葡萄种植

entries.definition: the grapes picked in one year, or the wine and the year it came from
entries.definitionCN: 一年采摘下来的葡萄；同一年份出产的葡萄酒

entries.definition: an evergreen climbing plant that clings to walls
entries.definitionCN: 常春藤

entries.definition: a plant that climbs, common in garden writing
entries.definitionCN: 攀缘植物（园艺用语）

entries.definition: a long woody climbing vine of tropical forests
entries.definitionCN: 热带雨林里的木质藤本植物

normalIntro.en: Vine and wine are one family: Latin vinum is the drink and vinea the garden that produces it.
normalIntro.cn: vine 与 wine 同属一族：拉丁语 vinum 是饮品，vinea 是产出它的园子。

normal.en: Vine and wine differ by a single letter; the plant makes the drink.
normal.cn: vine 与 wine 只差一个字母，正是这株植物酿出那杯酒。

normal.en: A vineyard is a field of vine plus an old word for an enclosed yard.
normal.cn: vineyard 就是一片藤加上「园地」的旧词。

normal.en: Vintage began as the wine of a particular year, then spread to anything old and fine.
normal.cn: vintage 原指某一年的酒，后来扩展到一切年代久远的好物。

normal.en: Climbing vines need a support: a post, a wall, or a trellis.
normal.cn: 攀爬的藤需要依靠：木桩、墙壁或棚架。

normal.en: Fruit on the vine is fresh; a plan on the vine has not yet been picked up.
normal.cn: 长在藤上的果子是新鲜的；还挂在藤上的计划则是尚未被人接手的。

abstract.en: Picture a tendril finding the wire and curling round it twice.
abstract.cn: 想象一根卷须摸到铁丝，绕上两圈。

abstract.en: See a single stalk rise from dry soil and carry green strings of grapes.
abstract.cn: 看一根藤茎从干土里升起，挂着一串串绿葡萄。

abstract.en: Think of a wine glass standing at the foot of the same stalk.
abstract.cn: 想象一只酒杯就放在那根藤茎脚下。

examples.en: The vines were heavy with fruit by late summer.
examples.cn: 到了夏末，葡萄藤上挂满了果实。

examples.en: A green vine had wound itself around the drainpipe.
examples.cn: 一根绿藤缠在了排水管上。

examples.en: Without a sponsor the project would die on the vine.
examples.cn: 没有赞助商，这个项目会半途夭折。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪」——藤蔓不长直，总是歪歪扭扭地缠上去，所以 vine 是藤。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vinum「葡萄酒」→ vinea「葡萄园」→ 古法语 vigne「葡萄藤」→ 中古英语 vine；同族的 vintage、viniculture、vineyard 都由「酒」与「藤」两个核心发展出来。

sensesIntro.en: Vine names one grape plant, widens to every climbing plant, slips into the drink made from the fruit, lives on in idioms about growth, and ends as a pattern.
sensesIntro.cn: vine 先指一棵葡萄藤，再扩到所有攀缘植物，继而借指葡萄酿成的酒，活在关于生长的习语里，最后成为一种纹样。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tendril curls round a trellis wire, and strings of grapes hang from the climbing stem.
core.cn: 核心意象：卷须绕上棚架铁丝，成串的葡萄从攀爬的藤茎上垂下。

branches.en: The plant branch: one pruned stalk carrying its yield of fruit.
branches.cn: 植物线：一根经过修剪的藤茎带着它的果实收成。

branches.en: The garden branch: the same climbing shape on a wall, whatever the species.
branches.cn: 园线：同一种攀爬形态长在墙上，不论是什么种类。

branches.en: The drink branch: the grape and the wine share one continuous path.
branches.cn: 饮品线：葡萄与葡萄酒处在同一条连续的路径上。

branches.en: The idiom branch: hanging fruit is an image of something waiting to be picked up.
branches.cn: 习语线：挂着的果实象征等待被摘取的东西。

branches.en: The plant and the drawn pattern share the same winding line.
branches.cn: 真实的植物与画出的纹样共用同一条卷曲的线。

intro.en: Vine has no affixes of its own; English builds its family with compounds such as vineyard and, for the wine side, learned coinages such as viniculture.
intro.cn: vine 本身不带词缀；英语用语素合成造出 vineyard 这类复合词，酒的一侧则采用 viniculture 这类学造词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vinum and vinea are both recorded with the same stem, so only the deeper root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vinum 与 vinea 都有文献记录且共用词干，只有更早的词根属于重构。

items.example: Vinum names the drink that the plant produces.
items.exampleCN: vinum 指这株植物酿出的饮品。

items.example: Vinea is the direct Latin source of the English form.
items.exampleCN: vinea 是英语形式的直接拉丁来源。

items.example: Vigne carries the Latin plant sense into French.
items.exampleCN: vigne 把拉丁语的植物义带入法语。

items.example: Yard joins vine to make vineyard.
items.exampleCN: yard 与 vine 组合成 vineyard。

items.example: The compound sharpens vine into a place.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把藤变成一片场地。

items.meaning: the grape harvest or the wine of one year
items.example: Vintage counts the yield of a single season.
items.exampleCN: vintage 计量的是单个产季的收成。

items.example: Cultura combines with the wine stem to form viniculture.
items.exampleCN: cultura 与酒的词干结合成 viniculture。

items.meaning: the science of growing grapes for wine
items.example: Viniculture keeps the wine stem in modern English.
items.exampleCN: viniculture 在现代英语里保留了「酒」的词干。

items.example: The suffix -y turns vinegar into vinegary.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 vinegar 变成 vinegary。

definition_zh: 中提琴；堇菜属植物；紫罗兰
definition_en: a stringed instrument slightly larger and lower than a violin, or a violet or pansy of the genus Viola
core_image: 一把比小提琴略大的琴搁在深紫色的花丛旁，琴身与花瓣是同一个名字
scene: 音乐课上，老师从柜子里取出一把比小提琴更大的弦乐器，说要请中提琴声部先试音。The teacher took a larger cousin of the violin from the cupboard and called it a viola.
sceneCN: 这里 viola 是「中提琴」（第 1 个义项：比小提琴略大、音区更低的弦乐器）；句意为老师从柜子里取出一把比小提琴更大的同类乐器，称它为中提琴。略大的琴身与琴弓正是这个词的核心画面。

pos.zh: 中提琴（弦乐器）
堇菜属植物；紫罗兰；三色堇

derivatives.zh: 由 viola 加 -ist（从事某项活动的人）构成，义为「中提琴手」
由意大利语 viola 加指小词尾 -ino 构成，义为「小提琴」，字面是「小的中提琴」
由意大利语 viola（弦乐器）、da（属于）与 gamba（腿）构成，义为「腿式维奥尔琴」，一种夹在腿间演奏的古提琴

senses.title: The middle voice of the string family
senses.titleCN: 中提琴：弦乐家族的中音
senses.definition: a stringed instrument a little larger than a violin, tuned a fifth lower, held on the shoulder
senses.definitionCN: 比小提琴略大、定弦低五度的弦乐器，放在肩上演奏
senses.example: She played the viola in the school orchestra.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学校乐团里拉中提琴。
senses.why: Italian kept viola as the name of a bowed string instrument, and English gave it to the middle member of the quartet, the one worth a name of its own.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语用 viola 指弓弦乐器，英语把这个名字给了四重奏里居中声部的这一件，它值得有自己的名称。

senses.title: The family of old bowed instruments
senses.definition: any of the bowed string instruments of the Renaissance and early Baroque viol family, such as the viola da gamba
senses.definitionCN: 文艺复兴与巴洛克早期古提琴家族中的任何一种弓弦乐器，如夹腿演奏的腿式维奥尔琴
senses.example: The concert opened with a duet for two violas.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会以两把古提琴的二重奏开场。
senses.why: Before the modern quartet was fixed, viola named the whole family of bowed string instruments, and some ancient names survive inside longer phrases.
senses.whyCN: 在现代四重奏定型之前，viola 泛指整个弓弦乐器家族，一些古名仍留在较长的短语里。

senses.title: A plant of the violet kind
senses.definition: a plant of the genus Viola, which includes the violet and the pansy, with five-petalled flowers
senses.definitionCN: 堇菜属植物，包括紫罗兰与三色堇，花有五个花瓣
senses.example: Violas flower from spring right through to autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 堇菜从春天一直开到秋天。
senses.why: The Roman name for the flower was viola, and botany kept it as the genus, so the same shape of word names both the plant and the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 罗马人对这种花的称呼就是 viola，植物学沿用它作属名，于是同一个词形既指植物也指乐器。

senses.title: The purple colour named after the flower
senses.definition: a blue-violet colour borrowed from the flower, used in art, dye and design
senses.definitionCN: 取自花朵的蓝紫色，用于绘画、染料与设计
senses.example: The evening sky was a deep viola above the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 山上方傍晚的天空是一片深紫。
senses.why: Once a flower is famous for its shade, the name of the flower can stand for the colour itself.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一种花因颜色而闻名，花名就可以直接指这种颜色。

senses.title: A voice-like personal name
senses.definition: a woman name taken from the flower and the instrument, used in English since the sixteenth century
senses.definitionCN: 取自花朵与乐器的女子名，十六世纪起在英语中使用
senses.example: Shakespeare sends a girl called Viola ashore in a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 莎士比亚让一个名叫维奥拉的女孩在暴风雨中上了岸。
senses.why: Stage plays made the musical name fashionable, and parents carried it on as a given name for daughters.
senses.whyCN: 舞台剧让这个音乐感的名字流行起来，父母们把它当作女儿的名字沿用下去。

intro.en: Viola is Latin for the violet flower, and the word for the stringed instrument came down separately from medieval bowed instruments of the same name.
intro.cn: viola 在拉丁语中本是紫罗兰；乐器义则从中世纪同名的弓弦乐器一路传来，两条线索最终合为一个词形。

items.en: Viola means a violet, and the form is found beside violarium, a bed of violets.
items.cn: viola 意为紫罗兰，常与 violarium（紫罗兰苗圃）一同出现。

items.en: The flower word travels north as viole, keeping the soft rounded sound.
items.cn: 表示花的词以 viole 的形式北传，保留了柔和的圆音。

items.en: Violare and the family of viol names are used for bowed stringed instruments; the connection with the flower is not certain.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中 viol 一系的词形用来指弓弦乐器，它与花的关系并不确定。

items.en: Italian makers use viola for the bigger bow instrument, and -ino makes violin, the small one.
items.cn: 意大利制琴师用 viola 指较大的弓弦乐器，再加 -ino 造成 violin，即小的那件。

items.en: English borrows both the flower and the instrument from Latin and Italian forms.
items.cn: 英语分别从拉丁语与意大利语的形式借入花与乐器两个义。

items.en: Viola settles as the name of the middle string instrument, the violet genus and a girl name.
items.cn: viola 最终固定为中音乐器、堇菜属与女子名这三重身份。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the violin family and their Latin stem, and the near-meaning group holds the other instruments that share a string or a flower colour.
note.cn: 形近组收小提琴家族及它们的拉丁词干，近义组收共享弦乐或花色的其他词。

entries.definition: the smaller, higher stringed instrument of the same family
entries.definitionCN: 同一家族中较小、音区更高的弦乐器

entries.definition: a person who plays this instrument
entries.definitionCN: 中提琴手

entries.definition: the flower whose Latin name gave the word; a small plant of the same genus
entries.definitionCN: 其拉丁名提供本词的紫罗兰，同属的小型植物

entries.definition: the large bowed instrument held between the knees
entries.definitionCN: 夹在两膝之间演奏的大提琴

entries.definition: a garden flower of the same genus as the violet
entries.definitionCN: 与紫罗兰同属的三色堇

entries.definition: a blue-purple colour, slightly redder than the stem colour
entries.definitionCN: 蓝紫色，比中提琴纹路的紫略偏红

normalIntro.en: Viola is Latin for the violet, and the instrument name came down beside it; one short word carries a flower, a purple and a voice in the string quartet.
normalIntro.cn: viola 在拉丁语中是紫罗兰，乐器名与它并列传来；短短一个词同时装着花、紫色和四重奏里的一个声部。

normal.en: Violet came to English by another route, so it looks unlike viola but shares the stem.
normal.cn: violet 走的是另一条路进入英语，外形不像 viola，却共用拉丁词干。

normal.en: Italian adds -ino to viola, giving violin: the little one beside the big one.
normal.cn: 意大利语给 viola 加指小词尾 -ino，造出 violin：大的旁边那个小的。

normal.en: A violist plays the viola; one letter in the middle makes the player.
normal.cn: violist 演奏 viola，中间多出的一两个字母就是演奏者。

normal.en: The viola sits lower than the violin and higher than the cello in the quartet.
normal.cn: 在四重奏里，中提琴比小提琴低、比大提琴高。

normal.en: In botany the whole pansy genus is called Viola, so a garden flower can be a viola too.
normal.cn: 植物学上整个堇菜属都叫 viola，所以花园里的花也被称为 viola。

abstract.en: Picture a fiddle a little longer than a violin, resting against a shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象一把比小提琴略长的提琴，靠在肩上。

abstract.en: See the dark wood of the back of the instrument glow with a violet tint.
abstract.cn: 看琴背的深色木料泛出一点紫罗兰色调。

abstract.en: Think of a small viola flower opening at the foot of the music stand.
abstract.cn: 想象谱架脚下开出一朵小小的堇菜花。

examples.en: The viola carries the inner lines that hold the quartet together.
examples.cn: 中提琴承担着把四重奏串联起来的内声部。

examples.en: Violas grow happily in a cool, shaded border.
examples.cn: 堇菜在阴凉的花坛里长得很自在。

examples.en: He swapped his violin for a viola and joined the orchestra.
examples.cn: 他把小提琴换成了中提琴，加入了乐团。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维欧拉」——维欧拉女士手里这把琴比小提琴大一号，台上她就是中提琴手。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 viola「紫罗兰」与中世纪弓弦乐曲之名并行发展：花开在第一步，乐器名经意大利语定型为比 violin 更大的那一件，二者在现代英语里汇成 viola。

sensesIntro.en: Viola is one word over two histories: the Roman name of a flower and the medieval name of a bowed instrument, later used for the quartet voice between violin and cello, and finally borrowed as a colour and a girl name.
sensesIntro.cn: viola 是一个词压着两段历史：罗马人给花起的名字，与中世纪弓弦乐器的名字；后来它固定为四重奏里介于小提琴与大提琴之间的声部，也被借作颜色与女子名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an instrument a little larger than a violin, lying beside a bowl of dark purple flowers sharing its name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把比小提琴略大的琴，握在与它同名的深紫色花丛旁。

branches.en: The quartet branch: a steady middle voice between the bright top and the deep bass.
branches.cn: 四重奏线：在高音与低音之间稳稳托住的中声部。

branches.en: The early music branch: the same name once covered a whole band of bowed strings.
branches.cn: 早期音乐线：这个名字曾笼罩一整组弓弦乐器。

branches.en: The garden branch: the Roman flower name survives as a botanical genus.
branches.cn: 园线：罗马时代的花名作为植物属名保存下来。

branches.en: The borrowed branch: the flower colour and the musical name pass into art and into families.
branches.cn: 借用线：花色与音乐感的名字进入绘画，也进入家庭。

branches.en: The modern quartet and the old viol family both make viola a voice, not a solo show.
branches.cn: 现代四重奏与古老古提琴家族都让 viola 成为一种声部，而不是独奏主角。

intro.en: Viola is a compact Latin noun; its family is built with the Italian diminutive for violin and the agent suffix -ist for the player.
intro.cn: viola 是紧凑的拉丁名词；它的词族由意大利语指小词尾造出 violin，再由表示「人」的后缀 -ist 造出演奏者。

latinIntro.en: Latin viola, the violet, is recorded, and medieval Latin viol forms the bowed instrument side; the link between the two is not certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 viola（紫罗兰）有文献记录，中世纪拉丁语的 viol 一系代表乐器一侧；两者的关联并不确定。

items.example: Viola names the flower in classical Latin usage.
items.exampleCN: viola 在古典拉丁语用法中指这种花。

items.example: Violarium means a bed of violets.
items.exampleCN: violarium 意为紫罗兰苗圃。

items.example: The viol- stem names the old instrument family.
items.exampleCN: viol- 词干指古老的乐器家族。

items.example: The Old French form shows the instrument in the north.
items.exampleCN: 古法语形式显示乐器名在北方的形态。

items.example: Viole is the flower moving north from Latin.
items.exampleCN: viole 是花名自拉丁语北传的形式。

items.example: The suffix -ino makes violin from viola.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ino 把 viola 变成 violin。

items.example: Violino supplies the English word violin.
items.exampleCN: violino 提供了英语词 violin。

items.meaning: a person who plays or does
items.example: The suffix -ist makes violist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 violist。

items.example: A violist keeps the middle part moving.
items.exampleCN: 中提琴手让中声部保持流动。

items.example: Gamba names the instrument held between the legs.
items.exampleCN: gamba 指夹在腿间演奏的那类乐器。

definition_zh: 处女；处男；未开发的；原始的；未用过的；初榨的
definition_en: a person who has never had sex, or something still in its first untouched or unused state
core_image: 一片从未被踩过的雪地，表面平整，一根脚印都没有
scene: 车开进高地后，路边出现一片从未被砍伐过的森林，树冠一直铺到山脚。Behind the farmhouse lay a vast virgin forest that no logger had ever entered.
sceneCN: 这里 virgin 是「未开发的、原始的」（第 3 个义项：自然界保持原生状态）；句意为农舍后面有一大片伐木工从未进入过的原始森林。画面里可认出农家小院、连绵树冠和山脚一线。

pos.zh: 处女；处男；童男童女
未开发的；原始的；未用过的；初榨的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「处女的；纯洁的；未受触动般的」
由本词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「童贞；处女身份」
义为「使失去童贞」；语音上带 flower，但实际源自中世纪拉丁语 deflorare「使花落」，与本词并无词根关系
同一拼写还作名词，指一种小型古琴，因多由年轻女子弹奏而得名

senses.title: A person who has never had sex
senses.definition: a person, especially a young one, who has never had sexual intercourse
senses.definitionCN: 从未有过性行为的人，尤指年轻人
senses.example: The novel tells of a virgin who leaves home for the first time.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说讲述一个初次离家的处女的故事。
senses.why: The Latin noun virgo means an unmarried young woman, so the word begins with the concrete image of a young girl untouched by marriage.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 virgo 意为「未婚的年轻女子」，所以这个词最初只是一个具体画面：一个尚未进入婚姻的少女。

senses.title: A boy or girl who has not yet had sex
senses.definition: a boy or a girl who has not yet had sexual experience, often used in a religious context
senses.definitionCN: 尚未有性经验的男孩或女孩，常用于宗教语境
senses.example: In the old paintings the virgin saint is shown holding a white lily.
senses.exampleCN: 古画中的童贞圣女手持一支白百合。
senses.why: Religious use widened the personal noun from the young woman to any young person who has kept that untouched state.
senses.whyCN: 宗教用法把这个指人的名词从少女扩大到任何保持这种「未触动」状态的年轻人。

senses.title: Land or nature never altered by people
senses.definition: used of land, forests or countryside that people have never farmed, logged or built on
senses.definitionCN: 用于从未被耕种、砍伐或建造过的土地、森林或乡野
senses.example: The expedition crossed a virgin forest on foot.
senses.exampleCN: 探险队徒步穿越了一片原始森林。
senses.why: Land that people have never touched keeps the very image of the first sense: a surface with no one else on it.
senses.whyCN: 从未被人插手过的土地，保留了第一个义项的那个原始画面：一片没有任何他人痕迹的表面。

senses.title: Material or substance in its first pure state
senses.titleCN: 未用过的；纯净的；初榨的
senses.definition: used of a material that has not yet been used or worked on, so it stays pure and new
senses.definitionCN: 用于尚未被使用或加工、因而保持纯净与全新的材料
senses.example: The pastry chef always uses virgin olive oil.
senses.exampleCN: 这位糕点师一直使用初榨橄榄油。
senses.why: The untouched surface spreads from land to things: wool, oil or paper that industry has not yet worked over stays virgin.
senses.whyCN: 「未触动的表面」从土地扩展到物品：还没有被工业加工过的羊毛、油或纸张，就保持着未动的样子。

senses.title: Snow or ground with no step on it yet
senses.definition: used of snow, ice or a surface that nobody has walked on or touched yet
senses.definitionCN: 用于尚无人踩过或碰过的雪、冰或表面
senses.example: The children ran out into the virgin snow before anyone else.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们抢先跑进了尚未被人踩过的雪地。
senses.why: This is the core image in its purest form, because snow records every footprint and so proves that no one has crossed it yet.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心意象最纯粹的一种，因为雪会记下一切脚印，所以一眼就能证明还没有人走过。

senses.title: The first liquid pressed from fruit
senses.definition: the first amount of juice or oil obtained from fruit or olives that have not been heated, so the least processed grade
senses.definitionCN: 未经加热的水果或橄榄第一次压榨出的液体，是加工程度最低的等级
senses.example: Extra virgin oil keeps the strongest flavour of the fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 特级初榨油保留了果实最浓郁的香味。
senses.why: Oil pressed for the first time is literally the first liquid taken out, so the noun copies the untouched state of the fruit.
senses.whyCN: 第一次压榨得到的油就是最先被取出的液体，这个名词复制了果实「还未被触动」的状态。

senses.title: Not yet created, used or explored
senses.titleCN: 尚未使用的；未被触及的
senses.definition: used of resources, markets, ideas or experiences that no one has used or tried before
senses.definitionCN: 用于尚无人使用或尝试过的资源、市场、想法或体验
senses.example: The company sees a huge virgin market for its electric bicycles.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司为自己的电动自行车看到了一片巨大的待开发市场。
senses.why: A market with no competitor is like a snowfield with no footprints, so business writing borrows the same untouched image.
senses.whyCN: 没有竞争对手的市场，就像一片没有脚印的雪地，于是商业写作借用了同一个「未触动」的意象。

senses.title: A drink without alcohol
senses.titleCN: 不含酒精的；纯果汁饮料
senses.definition: a soft drink with no alcohol, usually a mix of fruit juices
senses.definitionCN: 不含酒精的软饮料，通常是几种果汁的混合
senses.example: She ordered a virgin cocktail and a plate of olives.
senses.exampleCN: 她点了一杯无酒精鸡尾酒和一盘橄榄。
senses.why: Drink menus separate alcohol from fruit drinks by one idea: alcohol has not yet entered, so the drink is still virgin.
senses.whyCN: 饮品单用同一个想法区分酒与果汁：酒精还没有加入，这杯饮品就是「未被介入」的状态。

intro.en: Virgin comes from Latin virgo, an unmarried young woman, through Old French and into English as a noun and later as an adjective.
intro.cn: virgin 来自拉丁语 virgo（未婚的年轻女子），经古法语进入英语，先作名词，后来才作形容词。

items.en: The Latin noun virgo meant a young woman of marriageable age, a maiden. It was also the name of a sign of the zodiac and of a goddess.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 virgo 意为「适婚的年轻女子、少女」；它同时也是黄道十二宫之一与一位女神的名字。

items.en: The accusative and derived forms such as virginalis and virginitas carried the idea of the maiden state.
items.cn: 宾格 virginem 及其派生形式 virginalis、virginitas 承载了「少女状态」这一含义。

items.en: Old French took the word as virgine and passed it into Middle English in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries.
items.cn: 古法语以 virgine 的形式吸收该词，并于十二三世纪把它传入中古英语。

items.en: Early English used virgin first as a personal noun, especially in Christian writing about Mary, then extended it to the land and to materials.
items.cn: 早期英语先把它用作指人的名词，尤其在关于玛利亚的基督教文献中，之后才扩展到土地与材料。

items.en: Nineteenth and twentieth century trade added fresh compounds such as virgin forest, virgin land and virgin wool, and drinks menus added the sense without alcohol.
items.cn: 十九、二十世纪的商贸用语增加了 virgin forest、virgin land、virgin wool 等新复合词，饮品单又增加了「不含酒精」的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin maiden root or close to it in form; the near meaning group gathers words for untouched and pure states.
note.cn: 形近组收录同出拉丁语「少女」词根或拼写接近的词；近义组收录表示「未触动、纯净」状态的词。

entries.definition: An adjective for a pure, untouched or very innocent quality; also a small early keyboard instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「处女的、纯洁的、未受触动的」；也可作名词，指一种早期的小型键盘乐器。

entries.definition: The abstract noun for the state of a person who has never had sex.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「童贞、处女身份」，指从未有过性行为的状态。

entries.definition: The Latin word for a maiden, now used in English as the name of a constellation and zodiac sign.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语「少女」一词，英语中现用作星座与黄道十二宫之一的名称。

entries.definition: A particular form of something; it merely looks close in letters and comes from a different Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「版本、形式」；只是字母上相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Refraining from sex by choice or rule; about conduct and discipline rather than the first state.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「贞洁的、守贞的」，强调出于选择或戒律的克制，而不是「从未」的状态。

entries.definition: Free from anything mixed in; the closest general word for an unworked substance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「纯净的、纯的」，是形容未掺入杂物之物最通用的一词。

entries.definition: Not handled, altered or reached by anyone; literally the core image, but plainer in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未动过的、未触及的」，几乎就是核心意象的字面说法，但语气更朴素。

entries.definition: Existing from the beginning, before any copy or change; usual for landscape and ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最初的、原生的」，用于描述尚无复制或改动时的地貌与想法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root virgo, the recorded compounds and the ways the adjective spreads from people to land and goods.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 virgo、有记录的复合词，以及这个形容词从人扩展到土地与商品的路径。

normal.en: The Latin noun virgo means an unmarried young woman, so the word begins with a person, not with land.
normal.cn: 拉丁语名词 virgo 意为未婚的年轻女子，所以这个词最初指人，而不是土地。

normal.en: A virgin forest is a forest with no axe in it yet, the same untouched picture moved onto the map.
normal.cn: virgin forest 是还没有斧头进入过的森林，就是同一个「未触动」的画面搬到了地图上。

normal.en: Virgin wool means wool taken in one fleece and never mixed or processed before.
normal.cn: virgin wool 指一次剪下、此前从未混纺或加工过的羊毛。

normal.en: Extra virgin is the most carefully pressed grade of olive oil, so the phrase marks the top of a scale.
normal.cn: extra virgin 是压榨最讲究的一档橄榄油，所以这个说法标出的是等级顶端。

normal.en: Compare pure and untouched: pure is about what is inside, virgin keeps the image of no one else having been there.
normal.cn: 对比 pure 与 untouched：pure 讲的是里面含什么，virgin 则保留「还没有别人到过」的画面。

abstract.en: Picture fresh snow at dawn with one long unbroken line of white and no print in it.
abstract.cn: 想象清晨的新雪，一整片白色绵延不断，上面没有任何脚印。

abstract.en: Picture the first cut into a roll of cloth, the shears holding still just before the blade closes.
abstract.cn: 想象一匹布的第一刀，尚未落下的剪刀停在那里。

abstract.en: Picture the first press of an olive, oil running out before a wick has ever been lit by it.
abstract.cn: 想象橄榄第一次被压榨，油流出时还没有任何灯芯用过它。

examples.en: The island still holds virgin woodland that no one has cleared.
examples.cn: 这座岛上仍有无人砍伐过的原始林地。

examples.en: The chef poured extra virgin oil over the warm bread.
examples.cn: 厨师把特级初榨油淋在温热的面包上。

examples.en: Traders call a market with no rivals a virgin market.
examples.cn: 商界把没有竞争对手的市场称为待开发市场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我准」——还没被谁碰过，就「我准」你先来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 virgo「未婚的年轻女子、少女」→ 宾格 virginem → 古法语 virgine → 中古英语 virgin，先指人，后引申为「未被人触及的」土地、材料与资源。

sensesIntro.en: The noun begins with an untouched young person, the adjective spreads that untouched surface onto land, goods, snow, first-pressed oil and unexplored markets.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词的名词义从一个未被触动的年轻人开始，形容词义则把这种「未触动的表面」铺到土地、商品、雪地、初榨油与待开发市场之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fresh snow with a perfectly clean surface and not a single footprint on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片新落的雪，表面干干净净，一个脚印也没有。

branches.en: A person who has never had that experience keeps the image in its most human form.
branches.cn: 从未有过这种经历的人，让这个意象以最接近人的形式保留下来。

branches.en: Land and snow without one mark show the image at its most visible.
branches.cn: 没有任何痕迹的土地与雪地，把这个意象展示得最直观。

branches.en: Wool and first-pressed oil carry the image over to goods whose first state has not been changed.
branches.cn: 羊毛与初榨油把这个意象带到了第一次状态尚未被改变的商品上。

branches.en: A market nobody has tried is the same snowfield drawn on a business plan.
branches.cn: 尚无人尝试的市场，就是把同一片雪地画在了商业计划上。

branches.en: A drink with no alcohol keeps one thing out of it, so the menu calls it untouched.
branches.cn: 不含酒精的饮品把一种成分挡在外面，于是饮品单称它为「未被介入」。

intro.en: Virgin sits in a family of Latin maiden words, with English suffixes adding adjectives and abstract nouns.
intro.cn: virgin 属于一个拉丁语「少女」词族，英语再通过后缀添加形容词与抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin virgo and virginitas are recorded forms; the word simply moved through Old French into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 virgo 与 virginitas 都是有记录的词形，这个词只是经古法语进入了英语。

items.meaning: an unmarried young woman, a maiden
items.example: Virgo is the direct source of the family.
items.exampleCN: virgo 是这一词族的直接来源。

items.example: The changed stem survives inside the English word.
items.exampleCN: 变形后的词干保留在英语词形里。

items.example: It is the source of the English abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语抽象名词的来源。

items.example: It yields the English adjective with the same meaning.
items.exampleCN: 它生成同义的英语形容词。

items.example: This noun carries the first English sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词承载了英语的最初义项。

items.example: It forms virginal.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 virginal。

items.example: It forms virginity.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 virginity。

items.meaningCN: 未触动的；纯净的；初榨的
items.example: The adjective spreads the image over land and goods.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把意象铺到了土地与商品上。

items.example: The adjective looks back to the maiden image.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词回指「少女」的画面。

definition_zh: 有德行的；道德高尚的；贞洁的；自诩清高的；正当的
definition_en: having or showing high moral standards, or behaving in a way that is considered pure and good
core_image: 一个人挺直站着，把手从一叠硬币前收回
scene: 村里人推举一位老人来调解两家的土地纠纷，因为他从不偏袒任何一方。The villagers asked the old judge to settle the quarrel because he had always led a virtuous life.
sceneCN: 这里 virtuous 是「道德高尚的」（第 1 个义项：表现出良好品德的）；句意为村民请那位老法官来调解争吵，因为他一生都过得有德行。画面里可认出村口、两户人家和一位老人。

pos.zh: 有德行的；道德高尚的；贞洁的；正当的

derivatives.zh: 本词的基础名词，义为「美德、德行」，由拉丁语 virtus 得来
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「有德行地；贞洁地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「有德性；美德」
义为「实质上的；虚拟的」；与 virtuous 同出拉丁语 virtus，但走的是「效能」这条支线，与「品德」义已经分家

senses.title: Behaving by high moral standards
senses.definition: behaving in a way that is morally good, honest and fair
