senses.definitionCN: 行为符合良好道德，为人诚实、公平
senses.example: She was remembered as a virtuous ruler who never took a bribe.
senses.exampleCN: 人们记得她是一位从未收受贿赂的有德君主。
senses.why: The Latin noun virtus means excellence and manly worth, so a virtuous person is one whose conduct shows that inner worth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 virtus 意为「卓越、男子气概的价值」，所以一个有德行的人，就是行为体现出这种内在价值的人。

senses.title: Keeping strict sexual purity
senses.definition: keeping sexual purity in a strict moral sense, especially in older moral writing
senses.definitionCN: 在严格的道德意义上保持性纯洁，多见于较早的道德写作
senses.example: Old novels often praise a virtuous wife who keeps to her own house.
senses.exampleCN: 旧小说常赞美守在家中、贞洁的贤妻。
senses.why: Victorian moral writing narrowed virtue to one kind of self-control, and the adjective kept that narrowed sense.
senses.whyCN: 维多利亚时代的道德写作把「美德」收窄成某一种自制，这个形容词就保留了这一狭窄义项。

senses.title: Doing good to others or to society
senses.definition: giving time, money or care to help other people and to improve society
senses.definitionCN: 付出时间、金钱或关心去帮助他人、改善社会
senses.example: Like many mountaineers, he saw it as a virtuous duty to carry rubbish down the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 和许多登山者一样，他把把垃圾背下山看成一种善行义务。
senses.why: From personal character the adjective moves outward: a virtuous act is one that produces good for other people.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从个人品性向外扩展：有德行的行为，就是给他人带来好处的事。

senses.title: Correct, legitimate or worthy of praise
senses.definition: describing a goal or action that people consider right and worthy of praise
senses.definitionCN: 形容人们认为正确、值得称许的目标或行动
senses.example: Buying used goods and repairing them is a virtuous choice for the planet.
senses.exampleCN: 购买旧物并加以修理，对地球而言是正当的选择。
senses.why: When a goal is judged right, praise words move onto the goal itself, so the adjective names a worthy cause rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 当一个目标被判断为正确时，赞许的词就移到了目标本身，于是这个形容词可以指值得肯定的事业，而不只是人。

senses.title: Claiming to be better than other people
senses.titleCN: 自诩清高的；爱标榜道德的
senses.definition: describing people who are too ready to claim that they are morally better than others
senses.definitionCN: 形容过于急于宣称自己比别人道德更高尚的人
senses.example: He stopped sending virtuous letters to the newspaper after his own firm was fined.
senses.exampleCN: 自己的公司被罚款后，他不再往报社寄那些自命清高的信了。
senses.why: Praise can turn into a complaint, and the adjective picks up the idea that virtue is only being talked about, not shown.
senses.whyCN: 赞许可以变成抱怨，这个形容词由此获得一个意思：那点美德只是挂在嘴上，并没有做出来。

senses.title: Forming a self-reinforcing good cycle
senses.definition: used of a process in which one good result leads to another, so that the whole situation improves
senses.definitionCN: 用于一个良好结果引出下一个、使整体越来越好的过程
senses.example: A car-free city centre can set off a virtuous circle of walking, trade and cleaner air.
senses.exampleCN: 无车的市中心可以启动行走、商业与更清洁空气的良性循环。
senses.why: Economists borrowed the moral word for a loop that keeps producing improvement, which is the social version of a good habit paying off.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家借用这个道德词语，指不断产生改进的循环，这正是「好习惯带来回报」的社会版本。

senses.title: Working as a beneficial counter-force
senses.titleCN: 能起矫正作用的；有益的
senses.definition: used of a force, habit or measure that pushes back against a harmful trend
senses.definitionCN: 用于能抵消某种不良趋势的力量、习惯或措施
senses.example: Some economists describe a curb on hidden fees as a virtuous brake on the market.
senses.exampleCN: 一些经济学家把对隐藏收费的限制，称为市场上一道有益的刹车。
senses.why: If something bad is a trap, then when people fail to stop it the result is a vicious circle, and the same picture can work the way round as a counter-force.
senses.whyCN: 如果坏事是陷阱，一旦没人阻止就形成恶性循环，那么同样的画面反着走，就成为一种有益的对抗力量。

intro.en: Virtuous and virtue both come from Latin virtus, meaning excellence, worth and courage, which in turn comes from vir, meaning man.
intro.cn: virtuous 与 virtue 都来自拉丁语 virtus（卓越、价值、勇气），而 virtus 又来自 vir（男人）。

items.en: The Latin noun vir meant a man, as opposed to a woman or a boy.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 vir 意为「男人」，区别于女人与男孩。

items.en: Virtus first named the qualities of an ideal man, especially courage and strength, and later moral excellence in general.
items.cn: virtus 最初指理想男子应有的品质，尤其是勇气与力量，后来泛指道德上的卓越。

items.en: The medieval Latin adjective virtuosus meant possessing virtue, and it already named both moral quality and miraculous power.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语形容词 virtuosus 意为「具有德性的」，当时已兼指道德品质与奇异的效力。

items.en: Old French vertuos, with its stem vertu, carried both the moral and the strength sense into English.
items.cn: 古法语 vertuos 及其词干 vertu 把道德含义与力量含义一并带入英语。

items.en: Middle English vertu and vertuous split off from valour and power, so English virtue settled on good moral action. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 中古英语 vertu 与 vertuous 逐渐与「勇武、力量」分开，于是英语 virtue 固定为「良好道德行为」；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Victorian writing narrowed bygone virtue to female chastity, while medicine, economics and politics turned to unrelated branches such as virtual and by virtue of.
items.cn: 维多利亚时代的写作把往昔的 virtue 收窄为女性的贞洁，而医学、经济学与政治则转向 virtual、by virtue of 等别的分支。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the virtue family, which must be spelled out beside near-twins from another root; the near meaning group gathers moral praise words that differ from it in degree and tone.
note.cn: 形近组收录 virtue 词族，并要在其中点出拼写极近但词根不同的「冒牌兄弟」；近义组收录程度与语气有别的道德褒义词。

entries.definition: The noun for a good quality of character, or for the power to make good things happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「美德、德行」，也指产生良好效果的力量。

entries.definition: An adverb that shares the root but now means almost, not morally.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，与本词同源，但现在的意思是「几乎、差不多」，而不是道德上的。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning nearly or in effect, and in modern use computer-simulated; it stays on the power branch.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「实质上的、几乎的」，现代又指计算机模拟的；仍然走「效力」这条支线。

entries.definition: A person with outstanding skill, especially a musician; it looks like the same family but mainly names skill, not morality.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演奏高手、技艺精湛者」；看起来同族，但主要指技艺而非道德，词源上走的是同一拉丁词的「技艺」分支。

entries.definition: Following a shared set of rules for right conduct; more neutral and rule-based than virtuous.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「合乎道德的、伦理的」，比 virtuous 更中性，更强调遵循共同的规则。

entries.definition: Honest and strictly correct in behaviour; plainer and warmer in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正直的、规矩的」，语气更朴素、更有温度。

entries.definition: Doing what is morally right, often with conviction and a hint of self-assurance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正直的、正义的」，常带坚定信仰与一点自以为是，多用于宗教语境。

entries.definition: Lacking virtue, formed with the suffix -less; rare apart from moral and technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无德行的」，由后缀 -less 构成，除道德与技术写作外少见。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the real Latin root vir and from the fixed phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子从真实的拉丁词根 vir 出发，并结合这个词实际出现的固定搭配。

normal.en: Virtue names excellence in a person, and virtue plus the adjective suffix -ous makes virtuous, an adjective for that excellence.
normal.cn: virtue 指一个人身上的卓越品质，virtue 加上形容词后缀 -ous 就构成 virtuous，用来形容这种卓越。

normal.en: The root is Latin vir, a man, the same vir that gives virile, so the oldest idea was a man of full worth.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语 vir「男人」，与 virile 同一来源，所以最古老的意思是「价值完整的人」。

normal.en: A virtuous circle is the phrase for a loop where one good result brings the next.
normal.cn: virtuous circle 是固定说法，指一个良好结果引出下一个良好结果的循环。

normal.en: Virtuous behaviour is behaviour that other people could hold up as an example.
normal.cn: virtuous behaviour 就是别人可以拿出来当榜样的行为。

normal.en: Compare virtual and virtuous: both come from virtue, but virtual now means almost or in effect, deeply separated from morality.
normal.cn: 对比 virtual 与 virtuous：二者都来自 virtue，但 virtual 现在的意思是「几乎、实质上」，与道德已相距很远。

abstract.en: Picture a coin lying on a table in a warm lit room and a hand slowly moving back from it.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币放在暖光下的桌上，一只手慢慢地从它前面收回去。

abstract.en: Picture a judge handing the wooden gavel to a stranger before the trial starts, so no one can say the choice was bought.
abstract.cn: 想象审判开始前，法官先把木槌交给一位陌生人，这样谁也说不出选择是被买通的。

abstract.en: Picture a straight white line drawn on a dark floor; it has to stay straight even when the crowd swings left and right.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗地面上画的一条笔直白线：人群左右摇晃时，它仍然要保持笔直。

examples.en: The mayor was praised as a virtuous and honest leader.
examples.cn: 这位市长被誉为有德行、诚实的领导者。

examples.en: Every family is different, so parents should not try to force the same virtuous life on their children.
examples.cn: 每个家庭都不一样，因此父母不该把同一种有德行的生活方式强加给孩子。

examples.en: Cheap bus fares can begin a virtuous circle for a small town.
examples.cn: 便宜的公交票价能为小镇带来良性循环。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我秋」——我秋后算账时心里清白，一生守德；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vir「男人」→ virtus「卓越、价值、勇气」→ 中世纪拉丁语 virtuosus「具有德性的」→ 古法语 vertuos → 英语 virtuous。核心义由「男子的优秀品质」扩展为「品德高尚」。

sensesIntro.en: One idea of outstanding worth runs through the senses: a person shows it in conduct, a goal is judged by it, a process keeps producing it, and a counter-force brakes what destroys it.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「卓越价值」的念头贯穿各个义项：人在行为里体现它，目标按它被评判，某种循环不断产生它，而一种矫正力量用它刹住破坏性的趋势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing straight and pulling a hand back from a pile of coins.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人挺直站着，把手从一叠硬币前收回。

branches.en: Personal worth in the best light, and the same word squinting at someone who only claims it.
branches.cn: 个人价值呈现出的最好一面，与同一个词眯着眼看那些只是自称有德的人。

branches.en: One kind of self-control, where restraint and the body meet.
branches.cn: 一种自制，是克制与身体相遇的地方。

branches.en: Good behaviour leaving the body and reaching other people or a shared goal.
branches.cn: 良好品行走出身体，抵达他人或一个共同的目标。

branches.en: A loop that keeps giving good results is a habit lifted to the level of economics.
branches.cn: 不断给出好结果的循环，就是把习惯提升到经济层面。

branches.en: The same loop working against a harmful trend as a brake.
branches.cn: 同一个循环反过来对抗某种不良趋势，起到刹车的作用。

intro.en: The virtue family grows from the Latin noun vir and virtus; English suffixes build verbs, adjectives and adverbs around it.
intro.cn: virtue 词族由拉丁语名词 vir 与 virtus 长成，英语再用后缀在周围造出动词、形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vir, virtus and medieval virtuosus are recorded forms, so no reconstructed root is needed for this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vir、virtus 与中世纪拉丁语 virtuosus 都是有记录的词形，这个词族不需要重构词根。

items.example: Veritas and virile share with the root one early meaning.
items.exampleCN: virile 等词与本词根共享早期含义。

items.meaning: having qualities traditionally seen as male
items.example: Virile keeps the oldest bodily sense of the root.
items.exampleCN: virile 保留了词根最古老的男性含义。

items.example: Virtus gives the whole family its moral core.
items.exampleCN: virtus 给整个词族提供道德内核。

items.example: Virtue is the noun the adjective is built from.
items.exampleCN: virtue 是这个形容词所依据的名词。

items.example: The medieval adjective already mixed worth and power.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪这个形容词已经把「价值」与「效力」混在一起。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: It forms virtuous, famous and generous.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 virtuous、famous 与 generous。

items.example: The adjective stays on the power branch of the root.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词留在词根的「效力」支线上。

items.example: The adverb no longer carries any moral sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词已不再带道德含义。

items.example: It forms virtually and virtuously.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 virtually 与 virtuously。

definition_zh: 签证；护照签注；签发签证；申请签证
definition_en: an official mark or document, usually put in a passport, that allows a person to enter or stay in a country
core_image: 护照页上的一枚戳记，边角印着看过的字样
scene: 出发前一周，她把护照交到使馆窗口，工作人员翻了几页后贴上一张彩色贴纸。The student collected her passport at the embassy, its pages now showing a two-year student visa for the United Kingdom.
sceneCN: 这里 visa 是「签证」（第 2 个义项：护照上的入境或停留许可）；句意为这名学生在使馆取回了护照，内页上已经有了为期两年的英国学生签证。画面里可认出使馆窗口、翻开的护照与彩色贴纸。

pos.zh: 签证；护照上的签注
给……签发签证；申请签证

derivatives.zh: 由本词与 free 合成，义为「免签证的」
由 electronic 与 visa 缩合，义为「电子签证」
合成短语，义为「签证持有人」
形容词，义为「看得见的」；与本词同出拉丁语 videre，但走的是「看见」那条分支，与行政审批无关

senses.title: An official travel permit
senses.definition: an official document or stamp that allows a person to travel to a country or cross its border
senses.definitionCN: 允许一个人前往某国或越过该国边境的官方文件或戳记
senses.example: She got a ten-year multiple visa for business trips to Asia.
senses.exampleCN: 她拿到了十年多次往返的商务签证，用于前往亚洲出差。
senses.why: Latin visa meant things seen, so the word begins with inspection: an officer has looked at a traveler and agreed to let them pass.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 visa 意为「被看见的事物」，所以这个词始于一次检查：官员看过了旅客，同意放行。

senses.title: The mark put inside a passport
senses.definition: the paper sticker, stamp or page in a passport that records the permission to enter or stay
senses.definitionCN: 贴在护照上的纸张、戳记或页面，记录进入或停留的许可
senses.example: The border officer took one long look at the visa before he stamped it.
senses.exampleCN: 边检官仔细看了那张签证很久，才盖章放行。
senses.why: Because the certificate of approval is itself a thing that can be seen, the noun moved from the act of inspection to the physical mark.
senses.whyCN: 由于这份批准证书本身就是一件能被看见的东西，这个名词就从「检查」这一动作移到了那张实物标记上。

senses.title: Permission to stay, work or study
senses.titleCN: 居留许可；工作或学习许可
senses.definition: an endorsement that lets a person stay, work or study in a country for a stated period
senses.definitionCN: 允许某人在一国停留、工作或学习一段指定时间的背书
senses.example: Without a work visa she could not accept the contract in Dublin.
senses.exampleCN: 没有工作签证，她无法接受都柏林的那份合同。
senses.why: A short inspection deepened into a long permission: what began as a right to enter became the right to remain for months or years.
senses.whyCN: 一次短暂的检查深化成了长期的许可：原本只是进入的权利，变成了数月至数年的居留权利。

senses.title: Official approval of a document
senses.definition: an official sign or mark by which an authority approves a document it has inspected
senses.definitionCN: 权威机关检查文件后所加的正式签字或标记，表示批准
senses.example: The customs officer put a visa on the invoice for the imported machines.
senses.exampleCN: 海关官员在进口机器的发票上签字确认。
senses.why: The core idea of having seen and approved stays even without travel: any paper an officer has checked and signed carries the same word.
senses.whyCN: 「看过并批准」这个核心观念在没有出行时也照样成立：任何经官员查验并签字的纸，都可以用这个词。

senses.title: The act of adding an official mark
senses.titleCN: 给文件加签注；签证盖章
senses.definition: the act of putting an official mark or signature on a document
senses.definitionCN: 在文件上加盖官方标记或签名的行为
senses.example: One clerk handled the visaing of hundreds of forms each week.
senses.exampleCN: 一名职员每周要为成百上千份表格办理签字盖章。
senses.why: Since the noun names a physical mark, the verb can name the action that puts the mark on the page.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词可以指实物标记，动词就可以指把标记盖到纸上的那个动作。

senses.title: To grant a visa to someone
senses.definition: to grant a visa to a person or to endorse that person as officially permitted
senses.definitionCN: 给某人签发签证，或在其证件上背书表示获准
senses.example: The consul visaeed the whole group on the same morning.
senses.exampleCN: 领事在同一个上午为整个团队签发了签证。
senses.why: The verb takes the object of the official action, either a person who receives the permission or a document that receives the mark.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词的宾语可以是一项官方动作的对象：或接受许可的人，或接受标记的证件。

senses.title: To stamp a document as checked
senses.definition: to stamp or sign a document to show that an official has checked it
senses.definitionCN: 在文件上盖章或签字，表明官员已经查验过
senses.example: The officer visaed our papers and waved us through the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 官员为我们的文件签注盖章，然后招手让我们通过闸口。
senses.why: The stamp on the document does not so much grant permission as record that a person walked through a gate with a paper already checked.
senses.whyCN: 文件上的这个戳与其说是授予许可，不如说是记录：有人带着一份查验过的纸，走过了某道闸口。

senses.title: To apply for permission to enter
senses.definition: to obtain a visa for a country, used mainly in the compound expressions visa in and visa for
senses.definitionCN: 为一个国家取得签证，主要出现在 visa in 与 visa for 这类固定说法中
senses.example: Apply for your visa early, because interviews in summer fill up fast.
senses.exampleCN: 要早点申请签证，因为夏季的名额很快约满。
senses.why: The noun is so common in travel talk that it turns into a verb for the whole errand: doing the paperwork that ends with the mark.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在旅行话题中太常用，以至于整个办事流程都可以用它来作动词：办完那一套手续，最后拿到那个标记。

intro.en: Visa is the plural of the neuter Latin participle visum, meaning a thing seen, used in charters as a note that an authority had inspected and approved a document.
intro.cn: visa 是拉丁语中性分词 visum「被看见的事物」的复数，在中世纪的文书里表示权威已经查验并批准。

items.en: The Latin verb videre meant to see; its participle visum meant a thing seen, seen and approved.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 videre 意为「看见」，其分词 visum 意为「被看见的事物」，并带有「看过并批准」的意思。

items.en: Medieval Latin scribes wrote visa or vidit on a charter to record that this document had been seen and approved.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语书记员在文书上写下 visa 或 vidit，记录「此件已查验批准」。

items.en: French government use widened visa to an endorsement on a passport that allowed the bearer to enter.
items.cn: 在十八九世纪，法国官方把 visa 扩大为护照上允许持照人入境的背书。

items.en: English borrowed the passport sense in the middle of the nineteenth century, and the word spread with mass tourism and tighter border control.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪中叶借入这个护照义，此后随着大众旅游与边境管控加强而普及开来。

items.en: Electronic records took over from ink, so the noun now covers a paper, a stamp and a database entry alike, and the verb was formed by back-formation.
items.cn: 电子记录取代了墨迹，所以这个名词现在同时指纸张、戳记与数据库记录，动词则由名词反推而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the short vis- words that end up meaning different things, and the near meaning group gathers the permission documents a traveler actually meets.
note.cn: 形近组收录以 vis- 开头、含义却各不相同的短词；近义组收录旅行者真正会遇到的各类通行文件。

entries.definition: Force or power in Latin; now rare, but it shares the same three letters and a faint root idea of strength.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中意为「力量、权力」；现今罕用，但三个字母相同，词根上也隐约带力量意味。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of the rarer verb meaning to stamp a document.
entries.definitionCN: 较罕用动词的过去式与过去分词，义为「在文件上签注盖章」。

entries.definition: The front part of a helmet or cap; it looks close to visa, but comes from a different but related Latin root for seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「面甲、帽檐」；只是拼写相近，来自另一个与「看见」相关的拉丁词。

entries.definition: A literary word for a face; it resembles visa only in spelling, and its root is the face, not the document.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「面容、面貌」，文学用语；只是拼写相近，词根指脸而不指文件。

entries.definition: The travel document that identifies you and that usually carries the visa inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「护照」，是证明身份的行证件，签证通常就贴在里面。

entries.definition: An official document allowing a specific activity; broader than visa and not tied to a border.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「许可证」，指允许某项特定活动的官方文件，范围比签证宽，也不只针对边境。

entries.definition: The British official term for permission to enter the country before arrival.
entries.definitionCN: 英国官方用语，义为「入境许可」，指抵达前获得的入境批准。

entries.definition: The mark itself; a passport stamp is the physical act that puts a visa on the page.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「印章、戳记」；护照上的戳就是把签证按在纸上的那个动作留下的痕迹。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin participle visum and the fixed travel phrases this word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据真实的拉丁语分词 visum，以及这个词常见的出行搭配。

normal.en: The plural of the Latin word for a thing seen is visa, so a visa is a paper that has been looked at and approved.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「被看见的事物」的复数就是 visa，所以签证就是一份被看过并批准的纸。

normal.en: Passports hold the person, visas hold the permission, so the two words share a page but not a job.
normal.cn: 护照装着身份，签证装着许可，二者同在一页，职责却不同。

normal.en: Apply for a visa is the phrase anyone preparing for a long journey will meet first.
normal.cn: apply for a visa 是准备长途旅行的人最先会遇到的说法。

normal.en: Visa-free countries are those where the looking and approving happens at the border instead of beforehand.
normal.cn: 免签国家是指在边境现场完成查看与批准，而不必事先办妥的国家。

normal.en: Compare visible and visa: both come from the Latin verb to see, but visible describes what eyes can catch, while visa records that an official has already looked.
normal.cn: 对比 visible 与 visa：二者都来自拉丁语「看」，但 visible 描述眼睛能捕捉的东西，visa 则记录官员已经看过。

abstract.en: Picture a passport held open at a page with one bright sticker, the thumb of a guard resting on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本翻开的护照，其中一页贴着一张亮色贴纸，一名守卫的拇指按在上面。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge with a gatehouse in the middle, where two flags meet and a lamp is lit only at night.
abstract.cn: 想象一座中间设有岗亭的桥，两面旗子会合于此，那里的灯只在夜里亮起。

abstract.en: Picture a date on a ticket that begins on the day you arrive and ends before you have finished a course.
abstract.cn: 想象车票上的日期：从你落地那天开始，却在你课程结束前就到期了。

examples.en: Apply for your visa at least two months before classes start.
examples.cn: 至少在开课前两个月申请签证。

examples.en: He was refused a visa because his papers were incomplete.
examples.cn: 他的文件不齐，签证被拒。

examples.en: Business travellers often need a multiple-entry visa.
examples.cn: 商务旅客常常需要多次入境签证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尾札」——出境前贴在护照末尾的一张批文；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 videre「看见」→ 分词 visum「被看见的事物」→ 公文上的复数 visa「已查验」→ 法语 visa「护照背书」→ 英语 visa。核心义「经人查看并批准」。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts from a thing that has been seen and approved, then moves from the act of checking to the paper mark, then to long permission to stay, and finally to the everyday verbs for the whole errand.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「被看见并批准的东西」出发，先由查验动作转到纸上的标记，再到长期居留的许可，最后变成指整件办手续的日常动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a passport page carrying one official stamp that shows an officer has looked and let the holder through.
core.cn: 核心意象：护照内页上的一枚官方戳记，表明官员已经看过并放行。

branches.en: The permission as a thing and the permission as a visible mark on a page.
branches.cn: 既指许可这件事，也指页面上看得见的那块标记。

branches.en: Entry permission stretched in time into the right to study, work or stay.
branches.cn: 入境许可被拉长成学习、工作或居留的权利。

branches.en: The signature and stamp of the inspecting officer, whether named as a mark, an act or a procedure.
branches.cn: 查验官员的签字与盖章，无论叫作一种标记、一个动作还是一套手续。

branches.en: The verb taking the person or the document as its object.
branches.cn: 动词的宾语可以是人，也可以是文件。

branches.en: The whole errand of applying, from form to stamp, named by one word.
branches.cn: 从填表到盖章的整件办事流程，都用这一个词来指称。

intro.en: Visa is a Latin participle that became a paper word; the family around it comes from the verb to see, not from a prefix.
intro.cn: visa 是一个后来变成「纸上用语」的拉丁语分词；它周围的词族都来自「看见」这个动词，而没有前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, visum and the derived adjective visibilis are all recorded, so nothing in this family needs reconstructing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre、visum 与派生形容词 visibilis 均有记录，这个词族没有任何需要重构的部分。

items.example: Videre is the source of the whole seeing family.
items.exampleCN: videre 是整个「看见」词族的源头。

items.meaning: a thing seen; the having been seen
items.meaningCN: 被看见的事物；已经看过
items.example: Visum supplies the stem of visa.
items.exampleCN: visum 提供了 visa 的词干。

items.example: The ending turns visum into visa.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 visum 变成 visa。

items.meaning: a permit marked on a passport
items.example: The noun keeps the finished inspection.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词保留了「查验完毕」的结果。

items.example: Visible keeps the plain sense of seeing.
items.exampleCN: visible 保留了「看见」的本义。

items.meaning: sight, or something seen in the mind
items.example: Vision names the power and the picture.
items.exampleCN: vision 既指看见的能力，也指看见的画面。

items.meaning: a person who comes to see
items.example: Visitor puts the seeing action on a person.
items.exampleCN: visitor 把「看」这个动作放到一个人身上。

items.example: Visual ties the root to the eye.
items.exampleCN: visual 把词根系在眼睛上。

items.example: It forms visible from the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词词干构成 visible。

definition_zh: 粘稠的；黏滞的；浓稠难流动的
definition_en: thick and sticky, and flowing very slowly because of that texture
core_image: 蜂蜜从勺子上缓缓垂下，拉成一条迟迟不断的细线
scene: 厨房里，一勺蜂蜜从勺边慢慢垂落，拉成细丝久久不断，怎么也滴不快。In the kitchen, the viscous honey hung from the spoon in a slow, unbroken thread.
sceneCN: 这里 viscous 是「粘稠的、流动缓慢的」（第 1 个义项：液体浓稠、不易流动）；句意：厨房里那勺粘稠的蜂蜜从勺子上拉成一条缓慢不断的细丝。

pos.zh: 粘稠的；黏滞的；浓稠难流动的

derivatives.zh: 粘性；黏度（形容词加名词后缀构成，指流体浓稠的程度）
粘稠地；黏滞地（形容词加副词后缀构成）
黏度计（用粘性与测量仪器两部分合成，测量流体的浓稠度）
无粘性的；理想流体的（拉丁否定前缀 in- 加在 viscous 前构成，物理学常用）

senses.title: Thick and slow to flow
senses.definition: having a thick, sticky texture that makes a liquid flow slowly
senses.definitionCN: 质地浓稠发粘，因而流动缓慢的
senses.example: The syrup was too viscous to pour easily.
senses.exampleCN: 糖浆太粘稠，不容易倒出来。
senses.why: The Latin adjective viscide meant sticky like birdlime, so the word still pictures a gluey substance that clings and creeps.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁形容词 viscide 意为「像捕鸟胶一样粘」，所以这个词至今描绘一种黏黏糊糊、慢慢爬动的东西。

senses.title: A technical property of fluids
senses.definition: used in science to describe a fluid whose internal friction slows its motion
senses.definitionCN: 科学上用来描述内部摩擦会拖慢其运动的流体
senses.example: Engineers selected a highly viscous oil for the gearbox.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师为变速箱选用了高度粘稠的机油。
senses.why: Physics borrowed the everyday image of honey and gave it a measurable meaning: how much a fluid resists being stirred.
senses.whyCN: 物理学借用了「蜂蜜」这个日常画面，并给它一个可测量的含义：流体在多大程度上抗拒被搅动。

senses.title: Of lava and molten rock
senses.definition: describing molten rock that is thick and therefore spreads slowly and briefly
senses.definitionCN: 形容熔岩浓稠，因而蔓延缓慢且流不远
senses.example: Viscous lava builds a steep dome instead of running far.
senses.exampleCN: 粘稠的熔岩会堆成陡峭的穹丘，而不是流得很远。
senses.why: In geology the slow creep of sticky matter becomes a way to predict how far a volcano will flow and how violent it may be.
senses.whyCN: 在地质学中，黏稠物质的缓慢爬行被用来预测火山熔岩能流多远、爆发会有多猛烈。

senses.title: Figurative: thick and sluggish
senses.definition: used of air, silence, or speech that feels heavy, slow, and hard to break
senses.definitionCN: 形容气氛、寂静或言语沉重、缓慢、难以打破
senses.example: The air in the cellar felt viscous and hard to breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 地窖里的空气显得凝重，令人难以呼吸。
senses.why: Once the word meant hard to get through, writers extended it from liquid to atmosphere and silence.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词表示「难以穿透」之后，作家就把它从液体扩展到空气与寂静上。

senses.title: Of fluids in the body
senses.definition: describing blood, mucus, or other body fluids that are thick rather than watery
senses.definitionCN: 形容血液、黏液等体液浓稠而不稀薄
senses.example: Dehydration can leave the blood more viscous than usual.
senses.exampleCN: 脱水会使血液比平时更粘稠。
senses.why: Medical use applies the sticky physical image to the body, where thickness of blood matters for health.
senses.whyCN: 医学把「黏」这个身体可感的形象用到人体上，血液的浓稠度直接关乎健康。

senses.title: Of adhesives and pastes
senses.definition: describing a substance that sticks to what it touches and is hard to wipe off
senses.definitionCN: 形容一碰到什么就粘上、很难擦去的物质
senses.example: A viscous paste held the broken tiles together.
senses.exampleCN: 一种黏稠的浆糊把碎瓷砖粘在了一起。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is birdlime, a sticky paste, so glue and paste keep the word close to its physical origin.
senses.whyCN: 词根最古老的含义就是捕鸟用的黏胶，所以胶水和浆糊保留了这个词最物理的本义。

senses.title: Of muddy, clogging soil
senses.definition: describing ground or mud that holds the foot and slows every step
senses.definitionCN: 形容地面或泥浆黏住脚、让每一步都变慢
senses.example: After the rain the track turned viscous and slippery.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后那条小路变得泥泞粘脚、滑溜溜的。
senses.why: A thick substance that grips whatever touches it explains why a muddy road feels like glue under the boots.
senses.whyCN: 浓稠的物质会抓住碰到它的一切，这就解释了为什么泥泞的路在靴子下像胶水一样。

senses.title: Slang: heavy with strain
senses.definition: informal use for something overdone, sticky, and tiresomely heavy
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指过分、发腻、沉重得让人生厌
senses.example: The humour in that sitcom felt viscous by the second episode.
senses.exampleCN: 那部情景喜剧笑到第二集就让人觉得腻得发沉。
senses.why: The image of honey that will not stop dripping naturally becomes a metaphor for excess that clings and slows everything down.
senses.whyCN: 「怎么也滴不完的蜂蜜」这一画面自然而然地引申为粘人又拖沓的过量之物。

intro.en: Viscous comes from the Latin adjective viscide, sticky, which grows from viscum, the mistletoe and the birdlime made from its berries.
intro.cn: viscous 来自拉丁形容词 viscide（粘的），源于 viscum，意为槲寄生以及用其浆果制成的粘鸟胶。

items.en: Viscum names mistletoe and the sticky birdlime made from its berries.
items.cn: viscum 指槲寄生，也指用其浆果熬制的粘鸟胶。

items.en: The adjective viscide means sticky, gluey, and thick.
items.cn: 形容词 viscide 意为粘的、如同胶质的、浓稠的。

items.en: The related form viscosus is recorded with the sense of sticky matter.
items.cn: 相关的形式 viscosus 有记载，同样表示黏稠的物质。

items.en: English borrows the adjective as viscous, meaning gluey and clammy.
items.cn: 英语借入这一形容词作 viscous，表示胶粘的、黏腻的；确切首见年代存疑。

items.en: Science turns the old gluey image into viscosity, a measured property of fluids.
items.cn: 现代科学把古老的「胶质」形象转为黏度，即流体一项可测量的属性。

note.en: Viscous joins a small sticky family, viscosity and viscid, and neighbours words for thickness and grip.
note.cn: viscous 与 viscosity、viscid 同属一个「黏」小词族，并与表示浓稠、抓住的词相邻。

entries.definition: the degree to which a fluid resists flowing
entries.definitionCN: 黏度；流体抗拒流动的程度

entries.definition: sticky and gluey
entries.definitionCN: 胶粘的；黏稠的

entries.definition: obstinate and awkward
entries.definitionCN: 固执的；别扭的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: having a dense, heavy consistency
entries.definitionCN: 浓的；稠的

entries.definition: tending to adhere to whatever touches it
entries.definitionCN: 黏的；黏性的

entries.definition: like glue, sticky and hard to wash off
entries.definitionCN: 胶粘的；像胶水一样难洗掉

normalIntro.en: Viscous shares its root with viscosity, and both come from a Latin word for birdlime, the sticky paste once smeared on twigs.
normalIntro.cn: viscous 与 viscosity 同源，都出自拉丁语中表示「粘鸟胶」的词，那是旧时涂在树枝上的黏稠胶膏。

normal.en: Viscous and viscosity are a pair, one adjective and one noun.
normal.cn: viscous 与 viscosity 成对，一个形容词、一个名词。

normal.en: A viscous liquid moves like honey, not like water.
normal.cn: viscous liquid 流动起来像蜂蜜，而不像水。

normal.en: Viscid is the short, old-fashioned cousin that also means gluey.
normal.cn: viscid 是更短、更老的同族词，同样表示黏糊糊。

normal.en: In chemistry, low viscosity means thin and high viscosity means viscous.
normal.cn: 在化学里，低黏度是稀，高黏度就是 viscous。

normal.en: Compare sticky and thick: both describe texture, while viscous often adds the idea of slow flow.
normal.cn: 对比 sticky 与 thick：两者都描述质地，而 viscous 常额外带上「流动缓慢」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon of honey lifted and pulled upward, one long thread refusing to break.
abstract.cn: 想象一勺蜂蜜被提起、向上拉，拉出一条久久不断的细丝。

abstract.en: Think of an oil can tipped over and the oil creeping out drop by drop.
abstract.cn: 想象一只油壶被打翻，油一滴一滴地慢慢爬出来。

abstract.en: Imagine warm engine oil between your fingers, thick enough to hold a slow groove.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖间温热的机油，稠到能留下一道缓慢的纹路。

examples.en: Molten plastic becomes viscous as it cools.
examples.cn: 熔化的塑料随着冷却变得粘稠。

examples.en: The paint was so viscous that it left thick brush marks.
examples.cn: 油漆太粘稠，刷上去留下了厚厚的笔痕。

examples.en: Scientists measured the viscous drag on a sphere in the tank.
examples.cn: 科学家测量了水箱中球体所受的黏性阻力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读起来像「微丝克死」——蜂蜜能拉出细丝，丝一被扯住就牢牢粘住，怎么也扯不断，这就是粘稠。这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 viscum（槲寄生；用其浆果制的粘鸟胶）→ viscide / viscosus（粘的、胶质的）→ 英语 viscous，核心义「黏住、流动迟缓」。

sensesIntro.en: Viscous starts as the sticky texture of a substance, then spreads to the science of slow flow, molten rock, and to anything that feels heavy and slow.
sensesIntro.cn: viscous 最初指物质黏稠的质地，继而扩展到流动缓慢的科学含义、熔岩，以及一切沉重滞缓的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: honey creeping off a spoon as one unbroken thread.
core.cn: 核心意象：蜂蜜从勺上缓缓垂下，拉成一条不断的细丝。

branches.en: Thick and sticky matter that will not run freely is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 浓稠发黏、不能自由流动的物质是日常义项。

branches.en: Science measures the slow flow, first in fluids then in molten rock.
branches.cn: 科学测量这种缓慢流动，先用于流体，再用于熔岩。

branches.en: From liquid texture the word reaches air, silence, and clumsy speech.
branches.cn: 从液体的质地，这个词伸手触及空气、寂静和笨拙的言辞。

branches.en: The body keeps the same picture when blood or mucus grows thick.
branches.cn: 当血液或黏液变稠时，人体仍然使用同一个画面。

branches.en: Glue, mud, and cloying humour all make things grip and slow down.
branches.cn: 胶水、烂泥和发腻的幽默都让事物黏住并变慢。

intro.en: Viscous grows from the Latin stem visc- and builds viscosity, viscously, and the instrument word viscometer.
intro.cn: viscous 由拉丁词干 visc- 生长而来，并构成 viscosity、viscously 与仪器词 viscometer。

latinIntro.en: Latin viscum gives the root visc- for sticky, and viscide adds the adjectival ending that English shortened to -ous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 viscum 提供了表示「黏」的词干 visc-，viscide 的形容词词尾在英语中化为 -ous。

items.example: The stem visc- carries the sticky idea into English words.
items.exampleCN: 词干 visc- 把「黏」的意思带进英语单词。

items.example: The suffix -ous turns visc into viscous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 把 visc 变成 viscous。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms viscosity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 viscosity。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms viscously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 viscously。

items.example: The suffix -meter forms viscometer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -meter 构成 viscometer。

items.example: The prefix in- makes inviscid mean not sticky.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 让 inviscid 表示无粘性。

items.example: Low viscosity means a thin liquid.
items.exampleCN: 低黏度意味着液体很稀。

items.example: Viscous describes a slow, heavy liquid.
items.exampleCN: viscous 描述流动缓慢、沉重的液体。

items.example: A viscometer checks how thick the oil is.
items.exampleCN: 黏度计用来检验油有多稠。

黏度计

definition_zh: 生命力；活力；生机；持久力
definition_en: the energy and liveliness that makes a person, place, or idea strong and able to keep going
core_image: 清晨的草地上，一颗小芽顶开泥土，抖掉露水往上长
scene: 清晨的草地上，一颗小芽顶开泥土，抖落露水，一天天长高长壮。The garden regained its vitality after the cool rain of spring.
sceneCN: 这里 vitality 是「生命力、活力」（第 1 个义项：人、地方或事物的旺盛精力）；句意：春天那场凉雨过后，花园重新有了生机。

pos.zh: 生命力；活力；生机；持久力

derivatives.zh: 生命的；至关重要的（名词去掉后缀 -ity 得到的形容词形式）
使有活力；赋予生机（形容词 vital 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，英式拼写 vitalise）
使复兴；使重新充满活力（前缀 re- 表「再」加 vitalize 构成，英式拼写 revitalise）
极其重要地（形容词 vital 加副词后缀 -ly 构成）
活力论；生机论（vital 加抽象名词后缀 -ism 构成，哲学与生物学术语）

senses.title: Physical energy and liveliness
senses.definition: the strength and energy that let a living body stay active and healthy
senses.definitionCN: 使有生命的身体保持活跃与健康的力气和精力
senses.example: At eighty she still dances with remarkable vitality.
senses.exampleCN: 八十岁的她跳起舞来依然活力惊人。
senses.why: Latin vita means life itself, so the word begins as the sheer force of being alive and moving.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vita 就是「生命」本身，所以这个词一开始指的就是「活着并在动」的那股劲。

senses.title: An institution or community that is flourishing
senses.definition: the vigour that keeps a group, town, or economy growing and productive
senses.definitionCN: 使群体、城镇或经济持续生长并富有产出的那股劲头
senses.example: Small shops bring vitality to the old town centre.
senses.exampleCN: 小店铺给老城中心带来了活力。
senses.why: The same life force that moves a body is pictured as moving a street or a market.
senses.whyCN: 推动身体的那股生命力，被投射到街道与集市上，于是它们也有了生机。

senses.title: The quality of being long-lasting
senses.definition: the ability of a thing, such as a plant or a fabric, to survive and remain strong
senses.definitionCN: 植物或织物等事物存活并保持强韧的能力
senses.example: This rose is prized for its vitality in cold winters.
senses.exampleCN: 这种玫瑰以能在寒冬中挺立生长而受人喜爱。
senses.why: Life that keeps going is life that lasts, so the noun also measures how much a thing endures.
senses.whyCN: 能持续的生命就是能长久的生命，所以这个名词也用来衡量事物能撑多久。

senses.title: A lively quality of language or art
senses.definition: the force and freshness that make words, music, or a painting feel alive
senses.definitionCN: 使文字、音乐或画作显得鲜活的劲道与新意
senses.example: Her prose has a vitality that keeps readers awake.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文字有一种让人读而不倦的生气。
senses.why: Critics borrowed the word from the body to describe art that seems to breathe.
senses.whyCN: 批评家把这个词从身体借到艺术上，用来形容仿佛会呼吸的作品。

intro.en: Vitality comes from Latin vitalitas, formed from vitalis, of life, which itself comes from vita, life.
intro.cn: vitality 来自拉丁语 vitalitas，由 vitalis（生命的）构成，而 vitalis 又源于 vita（生命）。

items.en: A root reconstructed as gweiH- sits behind Latin vita, life.
items.cn: 一个重构词根 gweiH- 是拉丁语 vita（生命）的源头。

items.en: Vita means life, and vitalis means of life or life-giving.
items.cn: vita 意为生命，vitalis 意为「生命的、赋予生命的」。

items.en: The abstract noun vitalitas names the quality of being alive.
items.cn: 抽象名词 vitalitas 指「有生命的性质」。

items.en: English borrows vitality through learned Latin, and the exact first written use is not certain.
items.cn: 英语经由书面拉丁语借入 vitality，确切书面首见年代存疑。

items.en: The word spreads from bodies to towns, economies, and works of art.
items.cn: 这个词的使用从身体扩展到城镇、经济和艺术作品。

note.en: Vitality shares the Latin root for life with vital, vitalize, and revive, and stands close to words for vigour and animation.
note.cn: vitality 与 vital、vitalize、revive 共享表示「生命」的拉丁词根，并与表示精力、生气的词义相邻。

entries.definition: necessary for life, and extremely important
entries.definitionCN: 维持生命所必需的；至关重要的

entries.definition: to bring back to life or strength
entries.definitionCN: 使复活；使恢复生机

entries.definition: pointlessness
entries.definitionCN: 徒劳；无意义（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: physical strength and active energy
entries.definitionCN: 体力；旺盛的精力

entries.definition: the power to act or work
entries.definitionCN: 能量；干劲

entries.definition: liveliness of manner or expression
entries.definitionCN: 活泼；生气

normalIntro.en: Vitality belongs to the Latin life family, next to vital, vitalize, and revive, all built on vita, life.
normalIntro.cn: vitality 属于拉丁语「生命」词族，与 vital、vitalize、revive 同族，它们都建在 vita（生命）之上。

normal.en: The suffix -ity makes a quality noun, so vitality is the state of being vital.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ity 构成性质名词，所以 vitality 就是「有生命力的状态」。

normal.en: To be full of vitality is to be full of life.
normal.cn: full of vitality 就是充满生命力。

normal.en: Revitalize means to give vitality again, with re- adding the sense of again.
normal.cn: revitalize 意为重新赋予活力，其中 re- 加上了「再一次」。

normal.en: Vital and vitality are a pair, one adjective and one noun.
normal.cn: vital 与 vitality 成对，一个形容词、一个名词。

normal.en: Compare vigour: vigour stresses strength, while vitality stresses being alive and able to grow.
normal.cn: 对比 vigour：vigour 偏重力气，vitality 偏重「活着、能生长」。

abstract.en: Picture a seedling pushing up through cracked soil in early spring.
abstract.cn: 想象早春时节一颗幼苗顶破泥土向上钻。

abstract.en: Think of a crowded market at noon, noisy, warm, and never still.
abstract.cn: 想象正午拥挤的集市，喧闹、温热、一刻不停。

abstract.en: Imagine a heartbeat on a screen, a steady line that keeps jumping.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上的心电图，一条不断跳动、始终平稳的线。

examples.en: The city centre has regained the vitality it lost in the war.
examples.cn: 市中心重新恢复了在战争年代失去的活力。

examples.en: Children bring enormous vitality to any household.
examples.cn: 孩子给任何一个家庭都带来巨大的活力。

examples.en: Doctors were surprised by the vitality of the old man after surgery.
examples.cn: 医生对这位老人术后的活力感到惊讶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「外──它乐」：只要外面有「它」在乐，就说明还有生命力。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vita（生命）→ vitalis（生命的）→ 晚期拉丁 vitalitas（有生命的性质）→ 英语 vitality，核心义「生命之力」。

sensesIntro.en: Vitality begins with the life force of a body, then spreads to flourishing groups, to things that endure, and to art that feels alive.
sensesIntro.cn: vitality 始于身体的生命力，继而扩展到兴旺的群体、能够长存的事物，以及显得有生命的艺术。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seedling pushing through soil, shaking off the dew.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗幼苗顶开泥土，抖落露水。

branches.en: A living body moving with energy is the first sense.
branches.cn: 有生命的身体充满精力地活动，是最初的义项。

branches.en: The same force is seen at work in towns, markets, and economies.
branches.cn: 同一股力量被看作在城镇、集市和经济中起作用。

branches.en: Life that keeps going becomes durability in plants and materials.
branches.cn: 能延续的生命，在植物和材料身上表现为耐久。

branches.en: The body image is lent to language, music, and painting.
branches.cn: 身体的意象被借给语言、音乐和绘画。

branches.en: Liveliness of body, community, and art all share the refusal to be still.
branches.cn: 身体、社群与艺术的生气，都共享同一种「不肯静止」。

intro.en: Vitality is built from the Latin root vit- for life, with the noun suffix -ity, and it feeds vital, vitalize, and revitalize.
intro.cn: vitality 由表示「生命」的拉丁词根 vit- 加名词词尾 -ity 构成，并衍生出 vital、vitalize 与 revitalize。

latinIntro.en: Latin vita means life and vitalis means of life, so the root vit- points to the word for life itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vita 意为生命，vitalis 意为生命的，因此词根 vit- 指向「生命」这个词本身。

items.example: The stem vit- carries the idea of life.
items.exampleCN: 词干 vit- 承载「生命」之意。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms vitality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 vitality。

items.example: The suffix -al makes vital mean of life.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 使 vital 表示「生命的」。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms vitalize.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 构成 vitalize。

items.example: The prefix re- makes revitalize mean bring back to life.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 让 revitalize 表示使复活。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms vitally.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 vitally。

items.example: Good news can vitalize a dull meeting.
items.exampleCN: 好消息能让沉闷的会议活跃起来。

items.example: Water is vital for every living thing.
items.exampleCN: 水对每个生物都至关重要。

items.example: The town is famous for its vitality.
items.exampleCN: 这座小镇以充满活力著称。

使复兴；使重新有活力

definition_zh: 活泼的；有生气的；开朗爱闹的
definition_en: full of life and energy, eager to talk, laugh, and brighten any room
core_image: 聚会上一个人眼睛发亮，笑得张开手臂，把整屋人都带动起来
scene: 聚会上，有人坐在角落不说话，另一个人眼睛发亮、笑声不断，把整屋人都带动起来。At the party, a vivacious young woman kept the whole room laughing.
sceneCN: 这里 vivacious 是「活泼的、有生气的」（第 1 个义项：人神情活跃、言语轻快）；句意：聚会上，一位活泼的年轻女子让满屋的人笑个不停。

pos.zh: 活泼的；有生气的；开朗爱闹的

derivatives.zh: 活泼；生气（形容词去掉词尾换成名词后缀 -ity 构成）
活泼地；生动地（形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成）
使有生气；使生动（同源于拉丁语 vivere，词根 viv- 加 -fy 构成）
生动的；鲜明的（与 vivacious 共享拉丁词根 viv-，意为「活的」）

senses.title: Lively in a charming way
senses.definition: having a lively, cheerful manner that attracts and cheers other people
senses.definitionCN: 举止轻快开朗、能吸引旁人并使旁人愉快的
senses.example: Her vivacious manner made the interview feel like a chat.
senses.exampleCN: 她活泼开朗的举止让面试变得像聊天。
senses.why: Latin vivax, from vivere, means long-lived and lively, so the word is built directly on the idea of being full of life.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vivax（出自 vivere）意为「长久活着、生机勃勃」，所以这个词直接建在「充满生命」这一概念上。

senses.title: An animated conversation or performance
senses.titleCN: 轻快的；充满生气的（言谈、表演）
senses.definition: describing talk, music, or a performance that is quick, bright, and full of movement
senses.definitionCN: 形容言谈、音乐或表演轻快、明亮、充满动感
senses.example: The duo played a vivacious waltz to open the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 这两人奏了一首轻快的华尔兹作为音乐会的开场。
senses.why: If a person bursts with life, then what they produce, such as words or rhythm, can be described as bursting with life too.
senses.whyCN: 一个人若满溢着生气，那么他产出的语言或节奏也自然被描述为满溢着生气。

senses.title: Boldly bright in colour
senses.definition: used of colours and patterns that look strong, warm, and alert
senses.definitionCN: 形容强烈、温暖、醒目的色彩与图案
senses.example: The market stalls were painted in vivacious reds and greens.
senses.exampleCN: 集市摊位被漆成明艳的红绿两色。
senses.why: Colour that seems to jump is colour that seems alive, so the life root reaches into the world of paint.
senses.whyCN: 仿佛会跳出来的颜色就像活着的颜色，于是「生命」这个核心一路伸进颜料的世界。

senses.title: Formal, and slightly old-fashioned
senses.definition: a polite, literary adjective often used of women in older writing and in reviews
senses.definitionCN: 一种礼貌而略带文学色彩的形容词，旧时多用于描写女性或见诸评论
senses.example: The novel describes a vivacious aunt with a quick tongue.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说写到一位口齿伶俐、活泼的姑妈。
senses.why: Borrowed from French in the seventeenth century, the word kept a polished, slightly period tone of praise.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在十七世纪自法语借入，至今保留着一种打磨过、略带年代感的赞誉语气。

intro.en: Vivacious comes from Latin vivax, lively and long-lived, a form of vivere, to live, and reaches English by way of French.
intro.cn: vivacious 来自拉丁语 vivax（活泼的、长生的），是 vivere（活着）的一种形式，再经法语传入英语。

items.en: A root reconstructed as gweiH- underlies Latin vivere, to live.
items.cn: 一个重构词根 gweiH- 是拉丁语 vivere（活着）的基础。

items.en: Vivere means to live, and the adjective vivax means lively and long-lived.
items.cn: vivere 意为活着，形容词 vivax 意为活泼的、长命的。

items.en: French vivace develops from the same Latin form with the sense of lively.
items.cn: 法语 vivace 从同一拉丁形式发展而来，表示活泼的。

items.en: English adopts vivacious, apparently following French, though the exact first written use is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语借用 vivacious，一般认为循法语而来，确切书面首见年代存疑。

items.en: The word settles into descriptions of lively people, music, and bright colour.
items.cn: 这个词最终稳定用于描写活泼的人、音乐与明艳的色彩。

note.en: Vivacious belongs to the Latin life family with vivacity, vivid, and revive, and stands near words for liveliness and cheer.
note.cn: vivacious 与 vivacity、vivid、revive 同属拉丁语「生命」词族，并与表示活泼、快活的词义相邻。

entries.definition: liveliness of manner
entries.definitionCN: 活泼；生动

entries.definition: producing clear, lively images
entries.definitionCN: 生动的；鲜明的

entries.definition: eating or wanting far too much
entries.definitionCN: 贪吃的；渴望过度的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: full of energy and movement
entries.definitionCN: 充满活力的；生气勃勃的

entries.definition: cheerful and excited in a friendly way
entries.definitionCN: 热情开朗的；欢快的

entries.definition: full of courage and energy
entries.definitionCN: 精神饱满的；勇猛的

normalIntro.en: Vivacious is built on the Latin life root viv-, shared with vivid, vivacity, and revive, and the -aceous ending gives it the feel of full of.
normalIntro.cn: vivacious 建在拉丁语「生命」词根 viv- 之上，与 vivid、vivacity、revive 同族，而词尾 -aceous 带来「充满」的语感。

normal.en: The root viv- means life, so vivacious literally suggests full of life.
normal.cn: 词根 viv- 意为生命，所以 vivacious 字面上就有「充满生命」的意思。

normal.en: The noun is vivacity, and the pattern -ous to -ity repeats in many adjectives.
normal.cn: 它的名词是 vivacity，形容词 -ous 换成 -ity 的规律在很多词里重复出现。

normal.en: Vivid and vivacious are cousins, both bright and alive, but vivid is about pictures and vivacious about people.
normal.cn: vivid 与 vivacious 是同族，都明亮而有生气，但 vivid 多用于画面，vivacious 多用于人。

normal.en: Revive shares the root: to revive is to bring the life back.
normal.cn: revive 同根：revive 就是把生命带回来。

normal.en: Compare lively: lively is the plain everyday word, while vivacious sounds more formal and more complimentary.
normal.cn: 对比 lively：lively 是日常平实的词，vivacious 更正式、更带褒义。

abstract.en: Picture a person entering a quiet room and turning all the heads with a laugh.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人走进安静的屋子，一声笑让所有人都转过头来。

abstract.en: Think of a bright red scarf flashing past in a grey crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象灰扑扑的人群中闪过一条明艳的红围巾。

abstract.en: Imagine a violin tune skipping upward, refusing to sit still on the beat.
abstract.cn: 想象一段小提琴旋律向上跳跃，怎么也不肯好好待在拍子上。

examples.en: A vivacious guide kept the whole group entertained.
examples.cn: 一位活泼的导游让整个团队兴致勃勃。

examples.en: Her vivacity made the boring lecture bearable.
examples.cn: 她的活泼让那场无聊的讲座变得可以忍受。

examples.en: The town is famous for its vivacious street life.
examples.cn: 这座小城以热闹生动的街头生活闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「维──爱你思」：说话时举手「维」护、满脸「爱你」的样子，再配上一脸「思」念的表情，就是活泼开朗。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vivere（活着）→ vivax（活泼的、长命的）→ 法语 vivace → 英语 vivacious，核心义「充满生命、生机盎然」。

sensesIntro.en: Vivacious starts with a person who is full of life, then describes lively talk and music, bright colour, and finally settles into a formal compliment.
sensesIntro.cn: vivacious 从「一个人充满生命」出发，再描述轻快的言谈与音乐、明艳的色彩，最后收敛为一种正式用语中的赞美。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a laughing guest who fills a room with light and movement.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位笑着的客人，让满屋都有了光与动。

branches.en: A person full of life and warmth is the central sense.
branches.cn: 充满生命与暖意的人，是中心义项。

branches.en: Words and rhythm can carry that same spark.
branches.cn: 言语与节奏也能承载同样的火花。

branches.en: Colour that feels awake and bold joins the family.
branches.cn: 仿佛醒着、大胆醒目的颜色也加入这一族。

branches.en: Borrowed from French, the word keeps a polite, literary polish.
branches.cn: 词自法语借入，至今保留一层礼貌而文雅的打磨。

branches.en: People, talk, and paint all appear to move, and that motion is the shared core.
branches.cn: 人、言谈与颜料都显得在动，这种「动」就是它们共同的内核。

intro.en: Vivacious grows from the Latin life root viv- and the ending -acious, and builds vivacity, vivaciously, vivid, and revive.
intro.cn: vivacious 由拉丁语「生命」词根 viv- 加词尾 -acious 生长而来，并衍生 vivacity、vivaciously、vivid 与 revive。

latinIntro.en: Latin vivere means to live, and its stem viv- passes into vivid, vivacity, and revive alike.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vivere 意为活着，其词干 viv- 同样进入 vivid、vivacity 与 revive。

items.example: The stem viv- carries the idea of life into English.
items.exampleCN: 词干 viv- 把「生命」带进英语。

items.example: The suffix -acious gives the sense of fullness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -acious 带来「充满」的语感。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms vivacity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 vivacity。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms vivaciously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 vivaciously。

items.example: The suffix -fy forms vivify.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -fy 构成 vivify。

items.example: The prefix re- makes revive mean come back to life.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 让 revive 表示复活。

items.example: Vivid memories stay bright and alive.
items.exampleCN: 鲜明的记忆依旧清晰生动。

items.example: Vivacity is the noun that goes with vivacious.
items.exampleCN: vivacity 是与 vivacious 对应的名词。

items.example: The old style has revived in recent years.
items.exampleCN: 这种旧风格近年来又流行起来。

items.example: Vivacious describes a person who lights up a room.
items.exampleCN: vivacious 形容能让满屋都亮起来的人。

definition_zh: 声音的；发声的；用言语表达的；直言的；声乐的人声部分

scene: 合唱排练前，指挥让大家先放松喉咙，再由嘴巴把声音送出去。Before the rehearsal, the conductor asked the choir to warm up their vocal cords.
sceneCN: 这里 vocal 是「发声的、与声音有关的」（第 1 个义项：与声音或发声相关的）；句意是合唱排练前，指挥让大家先把声带活动开。

pos.zh: 声音的；发声的；用言语表达的；直言的
（常作复数）声乐部分；人声
