senses.title: Relating to the voice or sound
senses.definition: connected with the voice, with making sounds, or with the organs that produce sound
senses.definitionCN: 与嗓音、发声或发声器官有关的
senses.example: Damage to the vocal cords can change the pitch of a voice.
senses.exampleCN: 声带受损会使嗓音的音高发生变化。
senses.why: Vocal comes straight from the Latin word for voice, so the most literal branch simply marks anything belonging to the voice.
senses.whyCN: vocal 直接来自拉丁语中表示「嗓音」的词，所以最字面的分支就是用来说明某物属于嗓音。

senses.title: Sung rather than played
senses.definition: the part of a song or band that is sung by the human voice rather than played on an instrument
senses.definitionCN: 歌曲或乐队中由人声演唱而非乐器演奏的部分
senses.example: She sang the lead vocals on the whole album.
senses.exampleCN: 整张专辑的主唱都是她唱的。
senses.why: In music the word for the voice became a noun naming the sung layer of a track, set against guitars or drums.
senses.whyCN: 在音乐里，「嗓音」这个词变成名词，专门指一首曲子里由人唱出来的那一层，与吉他、鼓等乐器相区别。

senses.title: Expressing feelings openly in words
senses.definition: given or expressed freely in speech rather than kept inside
senses.definitionCN: 自由地用言语说出而非藏在心里的
senses.example: Their anger was vocal rather than physical.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的愤怒只是说出口来，并没有动手。
senses.why: A voice carries thoughts outward, so anything openly spoken becomes a vocal expression of inner feeling.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音把心里的想法送出去，因此凡是公开说出来的东西，也算是一种「发声」式的表达。

senses.title: Speak up loudly and openly
senses.definition: willing to give opinions loudly, often to complain or to protest
senses.definitionCN: 愿意大声表达意见，常常是抱怨或抗议的
senses.example: Residents became vocal about the noise from the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 居民们对这条新路带来的噪音开始大声抱怨。
senses.why: When people speak one step louder than private speech, voice becomes public protest, so a vocal group is one that refuses to stay quiet.
senses.whyCN: 当人们比私下说话更进一步大声时，嗓音就成了公开的抗议，所以 vocal 的群体就是不肯沉默的那群人。

senses.title: Producing sound with your voice
senses.definition: of an animal, making sounds with its voice or throat
senses.definitionCN: 指动物用嗓子或喉咙发出声音的
senses.example: Dogs are highly vocal animals and will signal with their voices.
senses.exampleCN: 狗是发声很频繁的动物，会用叫声传递信号。
senses.why: The voice is not only a human tool, so the same adjective extends to any creature that makes itself heard.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音不只是人类的工具，同一个形容词也就延伸到任何能让自己被听见的动物身上。

senses.title: Involved in singing
senses.definition: of or for singing, rather than for playing instruments
senses.definitionCN: 属于或在歌唱这一类别中的，而非器乐的
senses.example: The school offers vocal training along with piano lessons.
senses.exampleCN: 学校除了钢琴课，也提供声乐训练。
senses.why: When music is divided into singing and playing, the voice side of the split takes the adjective vocal, as in vocal music.
senses.whyCN: 当音乐被分为「唱」与「奏」两大类时，属于嗓音的那一边就用形容词 vocal，例如「声乐曲」。

senses.title: Full of sound
senses.definition: of speech or writing, strong, lively, and full of feeling rather than dull
senses.definitionCN: 指言语或文字有力、生动、饱含感情而非平淡的
senses.example: The critic praised the novel for its vocal prose.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞这部小说文字洪亮感人。
senses.why: A voice can be strong across a room, and literary use gives the same strength to sentences that sound as if someone is speaking them aloud.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音可以洪亮到传遍整间屋子，文学用法也把这种力量给到那些读起来像有人在大声说出来的句子。

senses.title: Expressed in a vowel sound
senses.definition: in grammar, pronounced with the open flow of a vowel rather than with friction
senses.definitionCN: 语法学上指以元音的开放气流发出、而非摩擦发音的
senses.example: The teacher marked each vocal sound in the word with a dot.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在词中的每个元音处点上小圆点。
senses.why: Vowel and vocal both point back to voice, so the technical term for open sounds simply repeats the idea of the sounding voice.
senses.whyCN: vowel（元音）与 vocal 都指向「嗓音」，所以这个表示开放音的技术术语只是重述了「发出声音的嗓音」这一想法。

intro.en: Vocal goes back to Latin vocalis, an adjective from vox, the voice, and entered English through Old French.
intro.cn: vocal 追溯至拉丁语 vocalis，它是由 vox（嗓音）构成的形容词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root wek- probably carried the idea of speaking, and vox is traced to it by most handbooks.
items.cn: 重构词根 wek- 可能表示「说话」，多数词源手册把 vox 追溯到这个词根。

items.en: Nouns from the same root include vocare, to call, and vocalis, a voice belonging adjective.
items.cn: 同一词根的名词还包括 vocare（呼喊）与形容词性极强的 vocalis。

items.en: Vocalis means belonging to the voice, and in grammar it also names a vowel sound.
items.cn: vocalis 意为「属于嗓音的」，在语法里也指元音。

items.en: Vocal reaches French with the same voice meaning and passes the form on.
items.cn: vocal 带着同样的含义进入法语，并把词形传了下去。

items.en: Middle English takes vocal directly from Latin learning for things of the voice.
items.cn: 中古英语直接从拉丁文知识中借入 vocal，用来指与嗓音有关的事物。

items.en: Modern English adds the musical noun vocals and the figurative sense of speaking out loudly.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了音乐名词 vocals，以及「大声直言」的引申义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects spelling neighbours built on vox or vocalis, and the near-meaning group collects ordinary words for voice and speaking.
note.cn: 形近组收集拼写相近、确实出自 vox 或 vocalis 的同族词；近义组收集日常表示嗓音与说话的词。

entries.definition: noisy and forceful in expressing a view
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「喧嚷的、大声叫喊的」，由 vox 与 ferre 构成，与 vocal 同源。

entries.definition: a singer, especially one in a band
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「歌手、主唱」，是 vocal 加 -ist 构成的派生词。

entries.definition: to speak in favour of something; the root is vocare, to call
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「主张、倡导」，出自 vocare（呼喊），与 vocal 同根。

entries.definition: spoken in words or connected with words
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「口头的、言语的」，强调用词表示，而 vocal 强调用嗓子发出声音。

entries.definition: spoken rather than written
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「口头的、口述的」，多用于正式的对比场合，如口试。

entries.definition: expressed out loud, or, in phonetics, pronounced with vibrating vocal cords
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「说出口的」，语音学上指「浊音的」，是 voice 的形容词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks hang on the Latin vox, the voice, and on the musical and public uses that grew from it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子挂在拉丁语 vox（嗓音）这个词上，以及由它长出来的音乐与公开场合用法。

normal.en: Compare vocabulum, a word, from the same Latin root as vox: both deal with the spoken voice.
normal.cn: 对比 vocabulum（词），它与 vox 出自同一拉丁词根：两者都关于「说出来的声音」。

normal.en: Vocal cords, vocal range, and vocal music all keep the voice near the front of the meaning.
normal.cn: vocal cords、vocal range、vocal music 这三组搭配都把嗓音留在语义的核心。

normal.en: Be vocal about something means saying it out loud instead of keeping silent.
normal.cn: be vocal about 某事，就是把话说出来而不是保持沉默。

normal.en: Contrast instrument and vocals: one is played, the other is sung.
normal.cn: 对比 instrument 与 vocals：一个是弹奏的，一个是唱出来的。

normal.en: A vocalist sings; a vocal group speaks up; vociferous people shout the view even louder.
normal.cn: vocalist 负责唱；a vocal group 负责发声表明态度；vociferous 的人则喊得更大声。

abstract.en: Picture two thin cords in the throat pulled tight and buzzing like guitar strings.
abstract.cn: 想象喉咙里两根细带被拉紧，像琴弦一样嗡嗡震动。

abstract.en: In a band, imagine a glowing column rising above the drummer: that column is the vocals.
abstract.cn: 在乐队里想象鼓手上方升起一道发光的立柱：那道立柱就是 vocals。

abstract.en: Think of an idea climbing out of a head and stepping onto a stage to be heard.
abstract.cn: 想象一个想法从头脑里爬出来，登上舞台让所有人听见。

examples.en: The soprano showed a remarkable vocal range in the final aria.
examples.cn: 这位女高音在终曲咏叹调中展现了惊人的音域。

examples.en: Several members were vocal about how the funding had been spent.
examples.cn: 有几名成员就资金如何花销直言不讳。

examples.en: The album pairs quiet guitar parts with loud vocals.
examples.cn: 这张专辑把安静的吉他段落与高亢的人声配在一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「沃可」——嗓子一旦「沃」得有水分，说话唱歌就「可」以大声，这就是嗓音与发言。这只是近似读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般追溯至原始印欧语重构词根 wek-（说话）→ 拉丁语 vox（嗓音）→ vocalis（属于嗓音的）→ 古法语 vocal → 英语 vocal；核心义「与嗓音和发声有关」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the voice in action, and the senses move from sound itself to sung parts, spoken feelings, public protest, and finally music and grammar labels.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「嗓音在动作中」，义项从声音本身，依次扩展到唱出来的部分、说出口的感情、公开的抗议，最后落到音乐与语法的类别标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tense cords in the throat buzz and sound pours out of an open mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：喉咙里绷紧的声带嗡嗡震动，声音从张开的嘴里涌出。

branches.en: Anything belonging to the voice keeps the literal Latin meaning.
branches.cn: 凡属嗓音的事物，都保留了拉丁语的字面含义。

branches.en: The sung layer of music turns the adjective into a label for singing.
branches.cn: 音乐中唱出来的那一层，把这个形容词变成了歌唱的标签。

branches.en: What is said out loud becomes visible feeling and then public opinion.
branches.cn: 说出口的话先变成可见的情感，再变成公共意见。

branches.en: Animals with voices extend the look and the noun to the whole living world.
branches.cn: 有嗓音的动物把这一形容词延伸到整个生物界。

branches.en: Literary strength and open vowel sounds both keep the echo of a sounding voice.
branches.cn: 文学上的力度与开放的元音发音，都保留着「嗓音在响」的回声。

intro.en: Vocal is built on the Latin root for voice, with -al marking an adjective and a whole family of words around it.
intro.cn: vocal 建立在拉丁语「嗓音」词根上，词尾 -al 表示形容词，周边还有一整族同源词。

latinIntro.en: Vox means voice in Latin, and its oblique stem voc- plus suffixes gives vocare, vocalis, and many English relatives.
latinIntro.cn: vox 在拉丁语中意为嗓音，它的变格词干 voc- 加上各种后缀，产生了 vocare、vocalis 以及许多英语同源词。

items.example: Vox is the root every form here shares.
items.exampleCN: vox 是这里每个词形共有的词根。

items.example: The stem voc- appears in voice and vocal.
items.exampleCN: 词干 voc- 出现在 voice 与 vocal 中。

items.example: Vocare gives words such as advocate and provoke.
items.exampleCN: vocare 衍生出 advocate、provoke 等词。

items.example: Vocalis is the immediate source of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: vocalis 是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -al turns voc into vocal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 把 voc 变成 vocal。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms vocalist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 vocalist。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms vocalize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 vocalize。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms vocally.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 vocally。

items.example: The suffix -ferous helps form vociferous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ferous 帮助构成 vociferous。

items.example: Vociferous joins the voice root to ferre.
items.exampleCN: vociferous 把嗓音词根与 ferre 连在一起。

definition_zh: 发声；鸣叫；说话（英式拼写）
definition_en: the act of making sounds with the voice, or the sounds produced, spelled as in British English
core_image: 一个人张开嘴，喉咙震动，一串声音滑出来又被看得见地拉成一条线
scene: 观鸟者安静地坐着，用耳朵记下林子里鸟的叫声。The watchers stayed still and noted every vocalisation from the birds in the wood.
sceneCN: 这里 vocalisation 是「发声、鸣叫」（第 1 个义项：用嗓音发出声音的行为）；句意是观鸟者一动不动，记下林中鸟儿的每一声鸣叫。

pos.zh: 发声；鸣叫；（英式拼写）说话

derivatives.zh: vocal 加动词后缀 -ise 构成，义为「发声、用嗓子唱出」，美式作 vocalize
vocalisation 的基础形容词，义为「声音的、发声的」
由 vocalise 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「发声者、练声者」
由 vocal 加 -ist 构成，义为「歌手」，与 vocalisation 属同一词族

senses.title: The act of making sounds with the voice
senses.definition: the act of producing sound with the voice, or a sound so produced
senses.definitionCN: 用嗓音发出声音的行为，或由此产生的声音
senses.example: The baby began to smile and make soft vocalisations.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿开始微笑，发出柔和的声音。
senses.why: The Latin verb vox grows into vocalis and then vocal, and the suffix -ation turns the sounding action into a noun.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vox 长出 vocalis 与 vocal，后缀 -ation 又把「发声」这个动作变成名词。

senses.title: A cry or call of an animal
senses.definition: in biology, a sound made by an animal, especially one with a purpose such as warning or courtship
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中指动物发出的声音，尤指带有警示或求偶等作用的声音
senses.example: Each whale species has its own pattern of vocalisation.
senses.exampleCN: 每个鲸类物种都有自己的一套叫声模式。
senses.why: When ethologists needed a neutral word for any animal sound, the voice noun was the obvious choice, since animals use the same throat we do.
senses.whyCN: 动物行为学家需要一个中性的词来泛指动物的各种声音，既然动物用的是和我们相似的喉咙，「发声」这个名词自然最合适。

senses.title: Speech expressed in words
senses.definition: the use of speech to express thoughts, views, or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 用言语表达想法、观点或感情的行为
senses.example: Her calm vocalisation of the problem helped the meeting move forward.
senses.exampleCN: 她把问题平静地说清楚，让会议得以推进。
senses.why: Sound becomes meaning once it is shaped into words, so the noun also names speech itself, not only noise.
senses.whyCN: 声音一旦被组织成词就有了意义，所以这个词也指言语本身，而不只是声响。

senses.title: Singing without words
senses.definition: the singing of a melody on vowels without words, used as a training exercise
senses.definitionCN: 用元音唱出旋律而不带歌词，常作为训练练习
senses.example: The teacher asked the class to begin with a gentle vocalisation on a single note.
senses.exampleCN: 老师让学生先在一个音上轻轻地练习发声。
senses.why: A sung vowel shows the sounding voice at its purest, and singers borrowed the noun for the wordless warm-up exercises built on it.
senses.whyCN: 唱出的元音是「发声的嗓」最纯粹的样子，歌唱者便借这个词来指建立在元音上的无词练声。

senses.title: Turning a sound into a voiced sound
senses.definition: in phonetics, the process of pronouncing a sound with vibration of the vocal cords
senses.definitionCN: 语音学中指用声带振动来发出某个音的过程
senses.example: The vocalisation of the final consonant is common in this dialect.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个方言里，词尾辅音浊化很常见。
senses.why: Because voice is what the vocal cords add to a sound, phonetics uses this noun for the act of adding that vibration.
senses.whyCN: 因为「嗓音」正是声带给一个音加进去的东西，语音学便用这个名词指加上这种振动的动作。

senses.title: The British spelling of vocalization
senses.definition: the -ise form of the word, used in British English and in some dictionaries
senses.definitionCN: 采用 -ise 词尾的拼写形式，用于英式英语及部分词典
senses.example: The journal accepts both vocalisation and vocalization.
senses.exampleCN: 这本期刊同时接受 vocalisation 与 vocalization 两种拼写。
senses.why: British English spells the noun ending with s where American English uses z, so the two forms split from one sound change.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语把这个名词的词尾写成 s，美式则用 z，两个形式同出一次拼写惯例的分化。

intro.en: Vocalisation is a learned formation: the Latin voice adjective vocalis took the action suffix atio, and English spelled the result with -ise.
intro.cn: vocalisation 是书面构词的结果：拉丁语形容词 vocalis（嗓音的）接上表示动作的后缀 atio，英语再把结果拼成 -ise 形式。

items.en: The reconstructed root wek- is generally taken as the origin of Latin vox, though the evidence is indirect.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语 vox 来自重构词根 wek-，不过证据是间接的。

items.en: Vox means voice, and its adjective vocalis means belonging to the voice.
items.cn: vox 意为嗓音，它的形容词 vocalis 意为「属于嗓音的」。

items.en: The suffix atio forms action nouns, and Latin already had the sounding voice noun inside this family.
items.cn: 后缀 atio 构成表示动作的名词，这个家族中拉丁语早已有表示「发声」的名词。

items.en: The voice adjective vocal passes into French, and the action noun later follows the same path.
items.cn: 表示嗓音的形容词 vocal 进入法语，表示动作的名词后来也走同一条路。

items.en: English formed the -ise noun on the pattern of other Latin action nouns, so the first date is only approximate.
items.cn: 英语依照其他拉丁动作名词的模式造出了 -ise 形式，确切首见年代只能大致估计。

items.en: The spelling split yields vocalisation in Britain and vocalization in America, and sciences adopted the noun widely.
items.cn: 拼写分化使英国用 vocalisation、美国用 vocalization，各门科学也广泛采用这个名词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other nouns and verbs from the same voice root, and the near-meaning group holds plain words for sound and speech.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「嗓音」词根下的其他名词与动词；近义组收日常表示声音与说话的词。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same word
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发声、叫声」，是本词的另一种拼写形式，两者同源同义。

entries.definition: to make sounds with the voice, or to sing a tune without words
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发声、用元音唱旋律」，是本词去掉名词后缀得到的动词。

entries.definition: a singer
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「歌手」，与本词同出 vocal 词族，但只指人。

entries.definition: something said, or the act of saying it
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「话语、说出的话」，偏重言语内容，本词偏重发出的声音。

entries.definition: the clear pronunciation of words
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发音、咬字」，强调吐字清楚，本词强调嗓音本身在响。

entries.definition: a loud sound made by a person or an animal
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「呼喊、鸣叫」，是更日常的对应说法，本词多用于科学语境。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the voice root inside the word, the -ation action ending, and the British spelling with s.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子借助词中的「嗓音」词根、表示动作的 -ation 词尾，以及用 s 的英式拼写。

normal.en: Strip -ation and -ise and you are left with vocal, the voice word, so the noun names the act of using it.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ation 与 -ise 就剩下 vocal 这个「嗓音」词，所以名词指的就是使用它的动作。

normal.en: British spelling uses s in vocalisation, just as it does in realise and organise.
normal.cn: 英式拼写用 s 写成 vocalisation，就像 realise 与 organise 一样。

normal.en: Contrast the verb vocalise with the noun vocalisation: one is the act, the other is its name.
normal.cn: 对比动词 vocalise 与名词 vocalisation：一个是动作，一个是动作的名称。

normal.en: Biologists say bird vocalisation where a casual speaker would say bird song.
normal.cn: 生物学家说 bird vocalisation，而日常说话的人更常说 bird song。

normal.en: A vocalist performs, a vocalisation happens; both trace back to the Latin vox.
normal.cn: vocalist 是人去做的事，vocalisation 是发生的事；两者都回到拉丁语 vox。

abstract.en: Picture the moment before speech: the mouth is open and the throat is already humming.
abstract.cn: 想象说话之前的那一刻：嘴已经张开，喉咙已经在嗡嗡作响。

abstract.en: Think of a bird on a branch that sends one bright note into a still forest.
abstract.cn: 想象枝头一只鸟，把一声清亮的音符送进寂静的林子。

abstract.en: Imagine a lumpy thought being rolled around in the mouth until it becomes a sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一个粗糙的想法在嘴里被反复滚磨，最后变成一句完整的话。

examples.en: Researchers recorded the vocalisations of dolphins over three seasons.
examples.cn: 研究人员在三个季节里录下了海豚的叫声。

examples.en: The toddler uses vocalisation to attract her parents long before she can speak.
examples.cn: 这个幼儿早在会说话之前就会用发声来吸引父母。

examples.en: British journals print vocalisation, while American journals print vocalization.
examples.cn: 英国期刊印作 vocalisation，美国期刊印作 vocalization。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「我可来晒」——我一开口「我可来」了，声音「晒」出去，就是发声。只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vox（嗓音）→ vocalis（嗓音的）→ vocal（声音的）→ 动词 vocalise → 名词 vocalisation；后缀 -ation 表示动作或过程，-ise 是英式拼写习惯。

sensesIntro.en: One noun built on the voice word covers the act of sounding the voice, animal calls, everyday speech, wordless singing, phonetic voicing, and a spelling variant.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个建立在「嗓音」词上的名词，覆盖了发声这个动作、动物叫声、言语、无词吟唱、语音浊化，以及一种拼写变体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open mouth, a buzzing throat, and a thread of sound being drawn out.
core.cn: 核心意象：张开的嘴、震动的喉咙，以及被拉出来的一缕声音。

branches.en: The general act of using the voice is the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 一般的发声行为是最平实的义项。

branches.en: Animal sound is the same act in a different throat.
branches.cn: 动物叫声是同一个动作换了一副喉咙。

branches.en: Words and sung vowels are two shapes given to the same out-breath.
branches.cn: 言语与唱出的元音，是同一次呼气被塑成的两种形状。

branches.en: Phonetic voicing narrows the noun to the vibration of the vocal cords.
branches.cn: 语音浊化把这个名词收窄到声带的振动。

branches.en: The spelling variant shows the same word travelling through two writing traditions.
branches.cn: 拼写变体显示同一个词穿过了两种书写传统。

intro.en: Vocalisation is built from the Latin voice root plus an action suffix, with British -ise spelling.
intro.cn: vocalisation 由拉丁语「嗓音」词根加上表示动作的后缀构成，并采用英式 -ise 拼写。

latinIntro.en: Vox means voice in Latin, vocalis means of the voice, and the suffix atio marks a process or a result.
latinIntro.cn: vox 在拉丁语中意为嗓音，vocalis 意为嗓音的，后缀 atio 表示过程或结果。

items.example: Vox is the root behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: vox 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: Vocalis supplies the base for vocal.
items.exampleCN: vocalis 提供了 vocal 的基础。

items.example: The suffix -ation turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 把动词变成名词。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms vocalize and vocalization.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 vocalize 与 vocalization。

items.meaningCN: 英式拼写中的 -ize 变体
items.example: The suffix -ise forms vocalise and vocalisation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 构成 vocalise 与 vocalisation。

items.example: The suffix -er forms vocaliser.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 vocaliser。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms vocalist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 vocalist。

items.meaning: the act of sounding the voice
items.example: Vocalisation is the noun most sciences use for animal calls.
items.exampleCN: vocalisation 是各门科学用来指动物叫声的名词。

definition_zh: 发声；鸣叫；语音浊化（美式拼写）
definition_en: the act or result of putting sound into the voice, or the process of turning a sound into a voiced one, spelled as in American English
core_image: 一口无声的气被喉咙拦住、震动起来，于是变成了看得见的声波
scene: 实验室里，研究者把麦克风架在笼子边，整夜录下动物发出的各种声音。In the lab, the researchers left a microphone running all night to record patterns of vocalization.
sceneCN: 这里 vocalization 是「发声、鸣叫」（第 1 个义项：把气变成声音的过程）；句意是研究者在实验室里让麦克风整夜运转，记录动物发声的各种模式。

pos.zh: 发声；鸣叫；（语音）浊化；（美式拼写）

derivatives.zh: 由 vocal 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「发声、出声地说出」，英式作 vocalise
vocalization 的基础形容词，义为「声音的、发声的」
与 vocal 同出 vox 词根，义为「（语法）呼格的」，用于称呼某人时的词形
由 vocalize 加表示人或工具的后缀 -er 构成，义为「发声者、发声器」

senses.title: Putting sound into the voice
senses.definition: the act of producing sound with the voice, or the sound produced
senses.definitionCN: 用嗓音制造声音的行为，或由此产生的声音
senses.example: A baby uses vocalization long before producing real words.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿在说出真正的词之前很早就开始发声了。
senses.why: The Latin voice noun took the action suffix -ation, so the word names the whole process of turning breath into sound.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「嗓音」名词接上表示动作的后缀 -ation，于是这个词指把气息变成声音的整个过程。

senses.title: A behavioral act in animals
senses.definition: in animal behavior, a sound produced by an animal that serves a specific function
senses.definitionCN: 动物行为学中指动物发出、具有特定功能的声音
senses.example: Scientists link the frog vocalization to mating calls.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家把青蛙的鸣叫与求偶行为联系在一起。
senses.why: Because animal behavior studies every audible signal, the noun was borrowed to cover any call from a creature that cannot use words.
senses.whyCN: 因为动物行为学要研究每一个能被听见的信号，这个词就被借来覆盖任何不能使用语言的生物所发出的叫声。

senses.title: Turning a sound into a voiced sound
senses.definition: the phonetic process in which a sound is produced with vibration of the vocal cords
senses.definitionCN: 语音学中指某个音伴随声带振动而发出的过程
senses.example: The vocalization of voiceless stops is rare in that language.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种语言里，清塞音浊化的情况很少见。
senses.why: Phonetics borrowed the noun for the exact moment when a silent consonant takes on the buzz of the vocal cords.
senses.whyCN: 语音学借用这个名词，指的正是无声辅音带上声带振动的那个瞬间。

senses.title: Saying the vowels as you read
senses.definition: the traditional system of vowel signs or marks that tell a reader how to pronounce a sacred text
senses.definitionCN: 用来告诉朗读者在诵读圣典时如何读出元音的传统标记体系
senses.example: The pointers added vocalization marks to the text in the tenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 这些注家在大约十世纪给经文加上发声标记。
senses.why: A sacred text written without vowels needed a system to show where the voice should fall, and that system itself took the name vocalization.
senses.whyCN: 没有标出元音的圣典需要一套办法来指出嗓音应落在哪里，而这套办法本身就以 vocalization 命名。

senses.title: The American spelling of vocalisation
senses.definition: the -ize form of the word, the usual spelling in American English
senses.definitionCN: 采用 -ize 词尾的拼写形式，是美式英语中的常用写法
senses.example: The US edition prefers vocalization throughout.
senses.exampleCN: 美国版全书都采用 vocalization 这个写法。
senses.why: American dictionaries made -ize the standard ending for Latin verbs, so the same noun split into an s form and a z form.
senses.whyCN: 美国词典把 -ize 定为拉丁来源动词的标准词尾，于是同一个名词分成了 s 形式与 z 形式。

intro.en: Vocalization stands on Latin vocalis, of the voice, plus the Latin action suffix atio, which English writes as -ation, with -ize as the American ending.
intro.cn: vocalization 建立在拉丁语 vocalis（嗓音的）之上，加上拉丁语表示动作的后缀 atio，英语写作 -ation，并以 -ize 作为美式词尾。

items.en: Most handbooks trace vox back to a reconstructed root wek-, meaning broadly to speak, but the link is indirect.
items.cn: 多数词源手册把 vox 追溯到重构词根 wek-，大意为「说话」，但这一联系是间接的。

items.en: Vox is voice, and the adjective vocalis covers both the voice and, in grammar, the vowel.
items.cn: vox 意为嗓音，形容词 vocalis 既指嗓音，在语法中也指元音。

items.en: The action noun ending atio, inherited through French as -ation, joins the voice stem to name the act.
items.cn: 表示动作的名词词尾 atio 经法语以 -ation 的形式传来，与「嗓音」词干结合来表示这个动作。

items.en: English builds vocalization on the model of similar Latin action nouns, and the first use is approximate.
items.cn: 英语依照同类拉丁动作名词的模式造出 vocalization，首次使用的年代只能大致估计。

items.en: American spelling settles on -ize, so vocalization becomes the standard form across the Atlantic.
items.cn: 美式拼写定型为 -ize，于是 vocalization 成为大西洋彼岸的标准写法。

items.en: Phonetics, animal behavior, and the study of ancient manuscripts all adopt the noun for their own processes.
items.cn: 语音学、动物行为学以及古籍研究都各自采用这个名词，指称自己的过程。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the British spelling and other members of the voice family, while the near-meaning group gathers plainer words for sound and speech.
note.cn: 形近组收集英式拼写与「嗓音」词族的其他成员；近义组收集更日常表示声音与说话的词。

entries.definition: the British spelling of the same word
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发声、鸣叫」，是本词的英式拼写，两者同义，只差词尾字母。

entries.definition: to make or express something with the voice
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发声、出声说出」，是本词对应的动词形式。

entries.definition: the sung parts of a recording
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演唱部分、人声」，与本词同出 vocal，但多用于音乐语境。

entries.definition: the clear production of speech sounds
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发音、咬字」，强调嘴和舌如何把音发清楚，本词强调声音被发出。

entries.definition: something that can be heard
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「声音」，是泛指听觉现象的常用词，本词专指嗓音与喉咙。

entries.definition: the act of speaking, or a formal talk
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「说话、演讲」，指有内容的言语，本词可指无意义的声音。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -ation ending, the American -ize spelling, and the common scientific settings of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子借助 -ation 词尾、美式 -ize 拼写，以及这个词常见的科学场景。

normal.en: Take vocal, add -ization, and the adjective becomes the name of the action.
normal.cn: 把 vocal 加上 -ization，形容词就变成了动作的名称。

normal.en: American spelling prefers z, as in organized, so vocalization matches organize.
normal.cn: 美式拼写偏爱 z，就像 organized 一样，所以 vocalization 与 organize 一致。

normal.en: Pair vocalization with vocalize: the verb does it, the noun names it.
normal.cn: 把 vocalization 与 vocalize 配对：动词去做，名词来命名。

normal.en: In labs the word appears with microphone and pattern, so vocalization pattern is a natural chunk.
normal.cn: 在实验室里这个词常与 microphone、pattern 同现，所以 vocalization pattern 是自然的搭配。

normal.en: Compare the British twin vocalisation: swap the z for an s and nothing else changes.
normal.cn: 对比英式写法 vocalisation：把 z 换成 s，其余都不变。

abstract.en: Picture a column of silent air passing through the throat and coming out as a bright ribbon.
abstract.cn: 想象一柱无声的空气穿过喉咙，出来时变成了一条发亮的丝带。

abstract.en: Imagine two cups, one for silent and one for voiced, and watch a consonant being moved from one to the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两只杯子，一只装无声、一只装有声，看着一个辅音从左杯被挪到右杯。

abstract.en: Think of a reader following tiny marks above the letters to know where the voice should rise.
abstract.cn: 想象一位诵读者顺着字母上方的小记号，知道嗓音该在哪里升高。

examples.en: The team measured the vocalizations of captive birds in three habitats.
examples.cn: 研究团队测量了圈养鸟类在三种栖息地中的发声。

examples.en: The change from a silent sound to a voiced one is called vocalization.
examples.cn: 从一个清音变成浊音，称为浊化。

examples.en: Learning a language involves many hours of vocalization and imitation.
examples.cn: 学习一门语言要经历大量发声与模仿的练习。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「沃克拉零」——嗓子「沃」克需要水分，一到「零」度就打颤，声音照样能出来，这就是发声。只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vocalis（嗓音的）← vox（嗓音）→ 英语 vocal → 动词 vocalize（-ize 动词词尾，英式作 -ise）→ 名词 vocalization（拉丁语动作词尾 atio → -ation）；核心义「把气变成嗓音的过程」，美式拼写以 z 为标准。

sensesIntro.en: The senses keep the action of sounding the voice at the center and spread to animal calls, phonetic voicing, a manuscript tradition, and the spelling choice.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项都围绕「把嗓音发出声音」这个动作，向动物叫声、语音浊化、诵读标记传统以及拼写选择扩散。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: silent breath is caught by the throat and released as visible sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：无声的气息被喉咙拦住，又被放出来成为看得见的声音。

branches.en: The plain process of sounding the voice is the central sense.
branches.cn: 把嗓音发成声音的平实过程是中心义项。

branches.en: Animal calls apply the same process to creatures without words.
branches.cn: 动物叫声把同一过程用在没有语言的生物身上。

branches.en: Phonetic voicing narrows the process to one consonant gaining vibration.
branches.cn: 语音浊化把这个过程收窄为一个辅音获得了振动。

branches.en: Ancient readers needed marks to show where the voice should be heard.
branches.cn: 古代诵读者需要记号来标出嗓音应在何处响起。

branches.en: The spelling variant is the same word seen from the other side of the Atlantic.
branches.cn: 拼写变体是从大西洋另一边看到的同一个词。

intro.en: Vocalization combines the Latin voice root with two English endings, -ize for the verb and -ation for the noun.
intro.cn: vocalization 把拉丁语「嗓音」词根与两个英语词尾结合：动词的 -ize 与名词的 -ation。

latinIntro.en: Vox is Latin for voice; vocalis means of the voice, and atio forms nouns of action.
latinIntro.cn: vox 在拉丁语中意为嗓音；vocalis 意为嗓音的；atio 构成表示动作的名词。

items.example: Vox is the shared root of the family.
items.exampleCN: vox 是整个词族共有的词根。

items.example: Vocalis gives English the word vocal.
items.exampleCN: vocalis 给英语带来 vocal 一词。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms vocalize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 vocalize。

items.meaningCN: 英式拼写中的 -ize 变体
items.example: The suffix -ise forms vocalise.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 构成 vocalise。

items.example: The suffix -ation turns vocalize into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 把 vocalize 变成名词。

items.example: The suffix -er forms vocalizer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 vocalizer。

items.meaning: to produce sound with the voice
items.example: Vocalize is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: vocalize 是名词背后的动词。

items.meaning: the act of sounding the voice
items.example: Vocalization appears in both British and American texts.
items.exampleCN: vocalization 在英美文本中都会出现。

items.meaning: one who or that which vocalizes
items.example: Vocalizer names the person or device.
items.exampleCN: vocalizer 指发声的人或装置。

definition_zh: 使命感；天职；职业；志向
definition_en: a strong feeling that a particular way of life or work is your special calling, and the work or career that answers it
core_image: 远处传来一声召唤，一个人转身朝那个方向走去
scene: 她原本在银行工作，却总觉得有另一种声音在叫她去做护理。After years of feeling called to help the sick, she finally left her bank job and trained as a nurse, calling it her true vocation.
sceneCN: 这里 vocation 是「使命感、天职」（第 1 个义项：感到某种生活方式或工作是自己的召唤）；句意为感到自己被呼唤去照顾病人多年之后，她终于辞去银行工作去学护理，并称这才是自己真正的天职。

pos.zh: 使命感；天职；职业；志向

derivatives.zh: 由名词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「职业的、职业培训的」
由形容词再加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「在职业方面」
在 vocational 之后加 -ism，指重视职业教育的教育取向
由前缀 a- 与 vocation 构成，义为「业余爱好」，与正业相对

senses.title: A strong sense of calling
senses.definition: a strong inner feeling that you are meant to do a particular kind of work or to live in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 内心强烈地觉得某类工作或某种生活方式是注定由自己来做的
senses.example: From an early age she felt a vocation for teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小就觉得自己适合教书，有一种使命感。
senses.why: The Latin root vocare means to call, so a vocation is literally a voice calling you towards a life.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 vocare 意为「呼唤」，所以 vocation 字面上就是有一个声音在呼唤你去过某种人生。

senses.title: The career that answers the call
senses.definition: the work or career that a person feels this calling has led them into
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在这种召唤下走上并投入的工作或职业
senses.example: Medicine is not just a job to him; it is his vocation.
senses.exampleCN: 对他而言医学不只是一份工作，而是他的天职。
senses.why: Once the inner call is followed, the career itself takes the name, so the same word now names the work.
senses.whyCN: 一旦内心那声呼唤被追随，那份职业本身也沿用这个词，于是同一个词又可以指这份工作。

senses.title: A duty or mission laid on a person
senses.definition: a special duty or purpose that a group or institution believes it must carry out
senses.definitionCN: 某个群体或机构认为自己必须完成的一项特殊职责或目标
senses.example: The university sees public service as its central vocation.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学把公共服务视为自己的核心使命。
senses.why: If a person can be called, so can an institution, and the calling becomes a mission shared by many.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个人能被呼唤，一个机构也能，于是这声呼唤变成众人共担的使命。

senses.title: A special fitness for an occupation
senses.definition: a natural liking and talent that makes a person suited to a particular kind of work
senses.definitionCN: 一种天然的喜爱与才能，使人特别合适做某类工作
senses.example: Children with a vocation for music need patient teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 有音乐天赋和兴趣的孩子需要耐心的老师。
senses.why: The calling was read as evidence of a God-given gift, so the word also names the talent behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这种召唤曾被理解为上天赋予的才能，所以这个词也指支撑它的那份天赋与兴趣。

senses.title: A call to religious life
senses.definition: a belief, especially in the Christian tradition, that God is calling a person to be a priest or monk
senses.definitionCN: 尤其在基督教传统中，相信自己受到上帝召唤去当神父或修士
senses.example: He left engineering to answer a religious vocation.
senses.exampleCN: 他放弃工程工作，去回应一份宗教上的圣召。
senses.why: The earliest recorded use of the word in English was religious, where the voice calling was understood as the voice of God.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在英语中最早的用法就是宗教性的，那声呼唤被理解为上帝的声音。

intro.en: Vocation comes from Latin vocatio, a calling, from vocare, to call, and reaches English through Old French.
intro.cn: vocation 来自拉丁语 vocatio（召唤），源于 vocare（呼唤），再经由古法语进入英语。

items.en: Vocare means to call or to summon, and vox means a voice.
items.cn: vocare 意为呼唤、召唤，vox 意为声音。

items.en: Christian writers use vocatio for the calling of God, a meaning that became central.
items.cn: 基督教作家用 vocatio 指上帝的召唤，这一含义后来成为核心。

items.en: Vocacion names a divine calling in the religious language of the Church.
items.cn: vocacion 在教会的宗教语言中指神圣的召唤。

items.en: Middle English vocation appears first in a religious sense.
items.cn: 中古英语中 vocation 最早出现，并用于宗教含义。

items.en: Reformers use vocation for a person calling within ordinary work and daily life.
items.cn: 宗教改革者用 vocation 指各人在日常劳作中的职责与召唤。

items.en: Modern English widens the word to any strong sense of calling and to vocational training.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到任何强烈的使命感，并派生出 vocational（职业培训的）。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the Latin calling root; the near-meaning group gathers work words that differ in how much feeling or calling they carry.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「呼唤」词根构成的一族词；近义组收与工作有关的词，区别在于其中带着多少使命感和召唤感。

entries.definition: relating to the voice or to speaking out
entries.definitionCN: 与嗓音或大声表达有关的

entries.definition: all the words a person knows or a language has
entries.definitionCN: 一个人所掌握的或一种语言所拥有的全部词汇

entries.definition: to speak in favour of a cause
entries.definitionCN: 为某项主张发声；提倡

entries.definition: relating to training for a particular job
entries.definitionCN: 与某类工作的技能培训有关的

entries.definition: a strong urge to do a certain kind of work
entries.definitionCN: 从事某类工作的强烈冲动或使命感

entries.definition: a job that needs long training and a formal qualification
entries.definitionCN: 需要长期训练和正式资格的专门职业

entries.definition: the series of jobs a person does during their working life
entries.definitionCN: 一个人一生所从事的一连串工作

entries.definition: a strong purpose that one feels bound to carry out
entries.definitionCN: 自己觉得必须完成的强烈宗旨

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin calling root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子用真实的拉丁语「呼唤」词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: The Latin verb vocare means to call, so a vocation is a life that calls you.
normal.cn: 拉丁语动词 vocare 意为呼唤，所以 vocation 是呼唤你的那种人生。

normal.en: Vocal and vocabulary share the voice root, and one of them sounds like a call, the other is the words you speak.
normal.cn: vocal 和 vocabulary 共享「声音」词根，前者像呼唤，后者是说出口的词。

normal.en: A sense of vocation puts the feeling first and the job second.
normal.cn: a sense of vocation 先把感觉摆在前面，再谈工作。

normal.en: Vocational training teaches a trade but does not claim to hear a call.
normal.cn: vocational training 只教一门手艺，并不声称听到了召唤。

normal.en: Compare career: a career is a path of jobs, a vocation is the inner voice behind it.
normal.cn: 对比 career：career 是一串职业的路，vocation 是这条路上内心的声音。

abstract.en: Picture a distant voice across a field and one person turning towards it.
abstract.cn: 想象田野对面传来一个声音，有个人转身朝它走去。

abstract.en: Imagine a name written on a door and the person who walks through it every morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门上写着一个名字，而那个人每天早上都推开这扇门。

abstract.en: Think of a town that paints a key sentence on its city hall wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小镇在市政厅的墙上刷上一句关键的话。

examples.en: Nursing is a vocation that demands patience and warmth.
examples.cn: 护理是一份需要耐心与热情的使命。

examples.en: He could not settle in an office and turned his hobby into his vocation.
examples.cn: 他在办公室里待不住，就把爱好变成了自己的天职。

examples.en: Young people in the region prefer vocational courses to long academic ones.
examples.cn: 这个地区的年轻人更偏爱职业课程，而不是漫长的学术课程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我去信」——好像有个声音在招我去，于是信了它：使命、天职；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vox「声音」与 vocare「呼唤」→ vocatio「召唤」→ 古法语 vocacion → 英语 vocation，核心义「有一声呼唤，你应声而去」。

sensesIntro.en: Vocation starts as a voice calling a person to a way of life, then names the work that answers it, the mission of a group, the talent behind it, and finally the call to religious life.
sensesIntro.cn: vocation 起初是一个声音把一个人呼唤向某种人生，继而指应声而去的职业、团体的使命、支撑它的天赋，最后还专指对宗教生活的圣召。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice calls from far away, and a person turns and walks towards it.
core.cn: 核心意象：远处传来呼唤，一个人转身朝它走去。

branches.en: The inner feeling of being called is the root sense.
branches.cn: 被呼唤的内心感受是最根本的义项。

branches.en: The work that follows the call is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 追随召唤而从事的工作是日常义项。

branches.en: A shared calling becomes a mission of an institution.
branches.cn: 共同的呼唤就成为一个机构的使命。

branches.en: A special fitness for work is the talent that the call seems to point to.
branches.cn: 适合某种工作的禀赋，就是那声呼唤似乎指向的天赋。

branches.en: The religious sense keeps the oldest meaning of the word alive.
branches.cn: 宗教义项保存着这个词最古老的含义。

intro.en: Vocation is built on the Latin voice root voc- with noun suffixes; English adds adjective and adverb endings to make a small family.
intro.cn: vocation 建立在拉丁语「声音」词根 voc- 与名词后缀之上；英语再加形容词和副词词尾，扩展出一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vox means a voice and vocare means to call, so the family gathers around the act of calling and being called.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vox 意为声音，vocare 意为呼唤，整个词族都围绕「呼唤与被呼唤」这一行为聚集。

items.example: The root voc- carries the calling image into English.
items.exampleCN: 词根 voc- 把「呼唤」的意象带入英语。

items.example: Vox supplies the voice behind the call.
items.exampleCN: vox 提供呼唤背后的那个声音。

items.example: Vocare is the verb of calling.
items.exampleCN: vocare 是表示呼唤的动词。

items.example: Vocatio is the direct Latin source of the word.
items.exampleCN: vocatio 是这个词的直接拉丁语来源。

items.example: Vocation keeps the noun sense of the Latin word.
items.exampleCN: vocation 保留拉丁语名词的义项。

items.example: The suffix -al turns the noun into vocational.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把名词变成 vocational。

items.example: Vocational describes courses that teach a trade.
items.exampleCN: vocational 描述教授手艺的课程。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms vocationally.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 vocationally。

items.meaning: a hobby, work done for pleasure
items.example: The prefix a- and the calling root make avocation, calling away from work.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 a- 与「呼唤」词根构成 avocation，即被唤离正业的爱好。

definition_zh: 职业的；职业培训的；就业导向的
definition_en: connected with the skills and training needed for a particular job or trade rather than with general academic study
core_image: 车间里一排学生拿着工具，跟着师傅练一门手艺
scene: 很多高中毕业生不想念完四年大学，而是想尽快学一门手艺去工作。More school leavers now choose a vocational course that leads straight to a job.
sceneCN: 这里 vocational 是「职业的、就业导向的」（第 1 个义项：为某种工作或手艺提供训练）；句意为如今越来越多的毕业生选择直接通向工作岗位的职业课程。

pos.zh: 职业的；职业培训的；就业导向的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「在职业方面、从职业培训角度」
在 vocational 之后加名词后缀 -ism，指偏重职业技能训练的教育取向
由 vocationalism 去掉后缀再加 -ist 构成，指主张职业教育的人
去掉形容词后缀 -al 得到的名词，义为「使命、天职」

senses.title: Connected with training for a job
senses.definition: connected with the teaching of the skills and knowledge a person needs for a particular job or trade
senses.definitionCN: 与教授某人从事某种工作或手艺所需的技能和知识有关
senses.example: The centre runs vocational courses in welding and plumbing.
senses.exampleCN: 这个中心开设焊接和管道的职业课程。
senses.why: Vocation is a sense of calling, so work aimed at the jobs people actually take is called vocational.
senses.whyCN: vocation 指使命感，因此围绕人们真正从事的工作而设的内容就叫 vocational。

senses.title: Preparing students for employment rather than university
senses.titleCN: 就业导向的；职业教育方向的
senses.definition: describing education that trains people for work instead of for further academic study
senses.definitionCN: 形容为工作培养人才、而非为进一步学术深造做准备的教育
senses.example: Vocational education is expanding across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的职业教育正在不断扩大。
senses.why: When education is split between academic paths and working paths, the working side takes this label.
senses.whyCN: 当教育被分成学术路线和就业路线两条时，就业的那一条就用这个词来标注。

senses.title: Related to a way of life or calling
senses.definition: related to an occupation in the older sense of the calling a person follows
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧的「人所追随的召唤」这个意义上，表示与某种职业或生活方式有关
senses.example: Monks once wrote about their vocational duties within the monastery.
senses.exampleCN: 修士们曾在著述中谈到自己在修道院中的职责。
senses.why: The adjective appeared in religious writing first, describing duties that went with a sacred calling.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最早出现在宗教写作中，描述与神圣召唤相伴的职责。

intro.en: Vocational is the Latin calling noun vocation with the English adjective suffix -al added in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: vocational 是来自拉丁语的呼唤名词 vocation 在十九世纪加上英语形容词词尾 -al 构成的。

items.en: Vocare means to call, and vocatio means a calling.
items.cn: vocare 意为呼唤，vocatio 意为召唤。

items.en: Vocation enters English through Old French with a religious sense first.
items.cn: vocation 经由古法语进入英语，先有宗教含义。

items.en: The adjective suffix -al is taken from Latin endings such as -alis.
items.cn: 形容词词尾 -al 来自拉丁语 -alis 一类的词尾。

items.en: Industrial schooling gives vocational the sense of training for trades.
items.cn: 近代工业化的学校教育让 vocational 获得了「为手艺做训练」的义项。

items.en: Vocational now covers job-training education and career guidance.
items.cn: 现代英语中 vocational 覆盖职业培训教育与就业指导。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same calling root; the near-meaning group gathers training and job adjectives that differ in scope.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「呼唤」词根构成的一族词；近义组收与培训、工作有关的形容词，区别在于适用范围。

entries.definition: a strong sense of calling to a kind of work
entries.definitionCN: 对某类工作的强烈使命感

entries.definition: relating to the voice
entries.definitionCN: 与嗓音有关的

entries.definition: public support for a cause
entries.definitionCN: 对某项主张的公开支持

entries.definition: relating to a job that needs formal training and standards
entries.definitionCN: 与需要正式训练和职业规范的专门工作有关的

entries.definition: relating to a job, often to hazards or health at work
entries.definitionCN: 与工作有关的，常指工作中的危害或健康问题

entries.definition: relating to machines or to practical applied skills
entries.definitionCN: 与机器或实用技术技能有关的

entries.definition: relating to study and theory rather than to work
entries.definitionCN: 与学业和理论有关而非与工作有关的

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real root of calling and the pairs the adjective commonly appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子用真实的「呼唤」词根，以及这个形容词常见的成对搭配。

normal.en: Vocation plus the adjective suffix -al gives vocational: a course that answers a job.
normal.cn: vocation 加上形容词词尾 -al 就是 vocational：一门回应工作的课程。

normal.en: Vocational training sits opposite academic study in school debates.
normal.cn: 在学校讨论里，vocational training（职业培训）与学术学习相对。

normal.en: A vocational school hands out tools, not textbooks.
normal.cn: vocational school（职业学校）发的是工具，不是课本。

normal.en: Vocational qualifications are checked by employers before they hire.
normal.cn: vocational qualifications（职业资格）在招人前由雇主核对。

normal.en: Compare occupational: occupational names the job itself, vocational names the preparation for it.
normal.cn: 对比 occupational：occupational 指工作本身，vocational 指为工作做的准备。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where students hold tools and copy the teacher.
abstract.cn: 想象一间车间，学生们拿着工具跟着老师模仿。

abstract.en: See two roads at a school gate, one to books and one to work.
abstract.cn: 想象校门口有两条路，一条通向书本，一条通向工作。

abstract.en: Think of a quiet cloister where each task is done as a duty.
abstract.cn: 想象一处安静的修道院回廊，每件事都当作职责完成。

examples.en: The government is funding vocational training for young workers.
examples.cn: 政府正在资助年轻工人的职业培训。

examples.en: She took a vocational route after finishing secondary school.
examples.cn: 中学毕业后她选择了职业方向的升学路线。

examples.en: Employers complain that vocational skills are taught too late.
examples.cn: 雇主抱怨职业技能教得太晚了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我开心」——学一门手艺，我很快就开开心心上岗：职业的、职业培训的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vocare「呼唤」→ vocatio「召唤」→ 古法语 vocacion → 英语 vocation → 十九世纪加形容词词尾 -al 成 vocational，核心义「为那声呼唤所指的工作做准备」。

sensesIntro.en: Vocational begins as the adjective of a calling, then narrows to training for trades and to schooling that leads to work rather than university, and still keeps a formal sense of duties that belong to a way of life.
sensesIntro.cn: vocational 最初是「召唤」的形容词形式，后来收窄为手艺培训，再指通往工作而非大学的学校教育，同时仍保留「某种生活方式所带的职责」这一正式义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: students in a workshop practise a trade with tools in their hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：车间里的学生手握工具练习一门手艺。

branches.en: Training for a particular job is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 为特定工作做训练是最日常的义项。

branches.en: An education that leads to work is the schooling sense.
branches.cn: 以就业为目标的教育是学校语境下的义项。

branches.en: Duties that belong to a way of life keep the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 某种生活方式所带的职责保留着最古老的义项。

branches.en: Both senses point to study that ends in a job rather than a degree.
branches.cn: 这两个义项都指向以工作而非学位收尾的学习。

branches.en: A trade learned and a calling followed both tie skill to duty.
branches.cn: 学会一门手艺与追随一种使命，都把技能与责任连在一起。

intro.en: Vocational is the noun vocation with the adjective suffix -al; the same root gives vocal, vocabulary and advocate.
intro.cn: vocational 是名词 vocation 加形容词词尾 -al；同一词根还构成 vocal、vocabulary 与 advocate。

latinIntro.en: Latin vox means a voice and vocare means to call; the adjective uses the Latin suffix -alis, the twin of English -al.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vox 意为声音，vocare 意为呼唤；形容词用到拉丁语词尾 -alis，正是英语词尾 -al 的对应形式。

items.example: The root voc- ties every member of the family together.
items.exampleCN: 词根 voc- 把这个词族的每个成员连在一起。

items.example: Vocare supplies the calling image.
items.exampleCN: vocare 提供「呼唤」的意象。

items.example: Vocatio is the noun behind vocation.
items.exampleCN: vocatio 是 vocation 背后的拉丁名词。

items.example: The suffix -al makes the adjective vocational.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成形容词 vocational。

items.example: Vocation is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: vocation 是这个形容词的词基。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb vocationally.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 vocationally。

items.example: Vocationally describes training aimed at work.
items.exampleCN: vocationally 描述以工作为目标的培训。

items.meaningCN: 某种主张或做法的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ism forms vocationalism.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ism 构成 vocationalism。

items.example: Vocal keeps the voice part of the Latin root.
items.exampleCN: vocal 保留拉丁词根中「声音」这一部分。

definition_zh: 语音信箱；语音留言；语音邮件
definition_en: an electronic system that records spoken messages when a person cannot answer the phone, or a message recorded by that system
core_image: 无人接听的话筒旁，录音带安静地收下对方说的话
scene: 会议开到一半，手机在桌上震动了一下，她没接到那个电话。During the meeting her phone buzzed, but she only found a voicemail from her client afterwards.
sceneCN: 这里 voicemail 是「语音留言」（第 1 个义项：电话无法接通时系统录下的一段语音消息）；句意为开会时手机震动，她事后才发现客户留下的一段语音留言。

pos.zh: 语音信箱；语音留言

collocations.zh: 处于语音留言状态；用语音信箱

derivatives.zh: 组成 voicemail 的前半部分，义为「声音、嗓音」
组成 voicemail 的后半部分，义为「邮件、投递的消息」
与 voicemail 同构的复合词，用 electronic 的首部加 mail，指电子邮件
二战时期的缩合邮寄方式，用 victory 的首字母加 mail，是 mail 复合词的早期先例

senses.title: A recorded spoken message
senses.definition: a message that someone has spoken into a phone and that is stored so the receiver can listen later
senses.definitionCN: 某人对电话说的一段话，被存起来供接听者事后收听
senses.example: She left a voicemail asking me to call back.
senses.exampleCN: 她留了一段语音留言，请我回电话。
senses.why: The word joins a voice to mail, so a spoken message is posted into a box the way a letter is.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「声音」和「邮件」合在一起，于是说的话像信一样被投进一个信箱。

senses.title: The system that stores the messages
senses.titleCN: 语音信箱；语音留言系统
senses.definition: the telephone or network service that answers calls and records messages when nobody picks up
senses.definitionCN: 在无人接听时代为接听并录下留言的电话或网络服务
senses.example: Turn on voicemail before the long flight.
senses.exampleCN: 长途飞行前先开通语音信箱。
senses.why: As the mailbox is electronic, the word also names the whole service that keeps the messages.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个信箱是电子化的，这个词也用来指保存留言的整套服务。

senses.title: The answering greeting
senses.definition: the short recorded greeting a caller hears before being asked to leave a message
senses.definitionCN: 来电者在被要求留言之前听到的简短录音问候
senses.example: Change your voicemail to a short, clear greeting.
senses.exampleCN: 把你的语音信箱提示音换成简短清楚的一句问候。
senses.why: The first thing heard on the line is a recorded voice, so that greeting also goes by the same name.
senses.whyCN: 电话那头最先听到的就是一段录音人声，于是这条问候语也沿用同一个名字。

intro.en: Voicemail is a modern English compound of voice and mail, modelled on email, and it names a mailbox that holds speech instead of letters.
intro.cn: voicemail 是英语中由 voice 与 mail 构成的现代复合词，仿照 email 造出，指装语音而不是信件的信箱。

items.en: Voice and mail are both old English words; mail once meant a travelling bag.
items.cn: voice 与 mail 都是古老的英语词，mail 早期意为旅行用的袋子。

items.en: Telephone answering machines record messages when a household is out.
items.cn: 上世纪七十年代的电话答录机在家人外出时录下留言。

items.en: Office computer systems begin storing speech in a personal electronic mailbox.
items.cn: 八十年代办公室计算机系统开始把语音存进个人电子信箱。

items.en: Voice mail, later written voicemail, spreads from offices to mobile phones.
items.cn: 到了九十年代，分写的 voice mail（后来写作 voicemail）从办公室普及到手机。

items.en: Voicemail becomes a common verbless noun used in every workplace.
items.cn: 现代英语中 voicemail 成为各工作场所都常用的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built with the same voice or mail parts; the near-meaning group gathers the ways a spoken message travels.
note.cn: 形近组收由同样的「声音」或「邮件」部分构成的复合词；近义组收一段口信传递出去的几种方式。

entries.definition: a message sent and stored by computer network
entries.definitionCN: 通过计算机网络发送并储存的消息

entries.definition: spoken commentary added over filmed images
entries.definitionCN: 在影像之上加配的旁白

entries.definition: the stored collection of spoken messages for one number
entries.definitionCN: 某个号码所存语音消息的集合

entries.definition: a piece of information passed from one person to another
entries.definitionCN: 由一人传给另一人的一条信息

entries.definition: a device at a landline that records callers when nobody answers
entries.definitionCN: 装在座机旁、无人接听时录下来电的设备

entries.definition: a short written message sent by mobile phone
entries.definitionCN: 用手机发送的一条简短文字消息

entries.definition: sound that has been stored so it can be heard again
entries.definitionCN: 被存下来可以反复收听的声音

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real English parts of the compound and the phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子用这个复合词真实的两半，以及它常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Voice plus mail: a letter replaced by a voice.
normal.cn: voice 加 mail：把信换成了声音。

normal.en: Email put the mail online, and voicemail put the mail on the phone.
normal.cn: email 把邮件搬到网上，voicemail 把邮件搬到电话里。

normal.en: To leave a voicemail is to post a spoken note into the other person box.
normal.cn: leave a voicemail 就是把一条口述便条投进对方的信箱。

normal.en: A voicemail greeting is the first voice the caller hears.
normal.cn: voicemail greeting 是来电话的人最先听到的那句声音。

normal.en: Compare answering machine: the machine sits at home, voicemail lives in the network.
normal.cn: 对比 answering machine：机器放在家里，而 voicemail 活在网络里。

abstract.en: Imagine a small ribbon that keeps a stranger voice safe until you return.
abstract.cn: 想象一小盘带子，在你回来之前替你收好一个陌生人的声音。

abstract.en: Picture a metal letterbox that plays a sound when you open it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只金属信箱，你一打开它就放出声音。

abstract.en: See a phone politely clearing its throat before it lets the caller speak.
abstract.cn: 想象电话先礼貌地清一下嗓子，再让来电的人开口。

examples.en: Please leave a voicemail after the tone.
examples.cn: 请听到提示音后留言。

examples.en: I never check my voicemail until the evening.
examples.cn: 我总要到晚上才会去听语音留言。

examples.en: The office switched to a cloud voicemail service last year.
examples.cn: 这家办公室去年改用了云端语音留言服务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我信妹儿」——叫上「我信」那条小助手妹儿，让她把话录下来：语音留言；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 现代英语复合词，由 voice（声音，源自拉丁语 vōx）与 mail（信件，源自古法语，更早来源不确定）合成，仿 email 的构词方式，核心义「把声音投进信箱」。

sensesIntro.en: Voicemail names the spoken message that is stored, then the mailbox service that stores it, and finally the recorded greeting that plays before the message.
sensesIntro.cn: voicemail 先指被存下来的那段语音消息，再指存下它的信箱服务，最后还指留言之前播放的那段录音问候。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a phone with nobody beside it quietly takes down what the caller says.
core.cn: 核心意象：一部无人守着的电话，安静地记下来电人说的话。

branches.en: The stored spoken message is the object sense.
branches.cn: 被存下的语音消息是「物」的义项。

branches.en: The service that keeps the messages is the system sense.
branches.cn: 保存消息的服务是「系统」的义项。

branches.en: The recorded greeting is the voice heard first.
branches.cn: 录音问候是最先听到的那段声音。

branches.en: A message sits inside the service that records it.
branches.cn: 留言就存在录下它的那项服务之中。

branches.en: Both the service and its greeting answer calls when nobody can.
branches.cn: 系统与它的问候语都在无人接听时代为答话。

intro.en: Voicemail is a modern compound of two free words, voice and mail, built on the pattern of email; it has no affixes of its own.
intro.cn: voicemail 是由两个自由单词 voice 与 mail 构成的现代复合词，照着 email 的模式造出，本身不含词缀。

latinIntro.en: Only the first half goes back to Latin: vōx means a voice. The second half comes from Old French and its earlier source is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前半部分可追溯到拉丁语：vōx 意为声音；后半部分来自古法语，更早的来源不确定。

items.example: Voice is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: voice 是这个词的前半部分。

items.meaning: letters and packages sent by post
items.meaningCN: 通过邮局寄送的信件和包裹
items.example: Mail is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: mail 是这个词的后半部分。

items.meaningCN: 通过计算机网络投递的邮件
items.example: Email is the pattern that voicemail copied.
items.exampleCN: email 是 voicemail 仿照的模式。

items.example: Voicemail joins speech to post.
items.exampleCN: voicemail 把言语与邮寄连在一起。

items.example: The element -box appears in voicemail box.
items.exampleCN: -box 出现在 voicemail box 中。

items.example: The suffix -s gives the plural voicemails.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成复数 voicemails。

items.example: Voiceover uses the same voice half.
items.exampleCN: voiceover 用了同一个 voice 部分。

items.meaning: a wartime form of mail on microfilm
items.meaningCN: 战时用缩微胶片传递邮件的方式
items.example: V-mail shows an early compound with mail.
items.exampleCN: v-mail 展示了 mail 早期参与的复合词。

items.meaning: a written message sent by phone
items.meaningCN: 用手机发送的书面消息
items.example: Text message is the written partner of voicemail.
items.exampleCN: text message 是 voicemail 的文字搭档。
